# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, with project-specific notes for engineering verification.

## [Unreleased]

### Fixed

- Ask for a canvas plan once more when the model service broke its run off while it was answering, and name a plan whose model wrote its whole output budget as such (2026-10-23, at the owner's 「做 a，按你的建议直接上线」). Of the 34 planner runs that failed `runtime_failed` from 2026-10-16 13:30Z to the planner follow-up's release (read only: `.local/release/read-plan-runtime-failed.sh` in the context-limit worktree, the workers' journals and CloudTrail), 22 were the global Claude Haiku 4.5 profile refusing calls on 2026-10-19 02:07Z-08:03Z, which the workers' profile fallback has taken since 08:42Z that day; 6 were Bedrock streams that broke off partway, which nothing asked for again; and 6 were `qwen3.8-27b-p6` plans past the planner model's then 60,000-byte ceiling that used all 16,384 of its output tokens in about 432 s each. Pi, which runs every hosted plan, reports every model failure but a size refusal as `MODEL_ERROR`, which the API names `runtime_failed`: a stream the service broke off, but also a throttle, a content filter or a refused credential. So the page now asks once more, within its one retry, for a plan whose run failed `runtime_failed`, `provider_unavailable` or `runtime_stream_ended` while it was answering: it had written some of its plan or reasoning, or had run 10 s, and it failed within 3 minutes (`canvasPlanning.ts` `providerFault`, `PROVIDER_RETRY_AFTER_MS`, `PROVIDER_RETRY_BEFORE_MS`). A refusal of the request itself comes within seconds with nothing written and is not asked for again: a throttle or an outage there the worker has already asked of the model's other route (on Bedrock), and a refused credential or request would be refused again. A worker stream that ended without an answer (`runtime_stream_ended`) is never such a refusal and needs only the other bound, and no run past 3 minutes is asked for again, which would double a long wait. Of the 34, the 22 refusals and the 6 runs out of room fall outside these bounds, and 5 of the 6 broken streams within them. The status line then says 「模型服务中途出错，正在自动重试一次」 / "The model service failed partway; trying once more", and where the retry fails with a cause of its own (a plan out of room, a malformed plan), that cause is said rather than the first failure's. A run the bridge attached to rather than started (the same request already in flight, `plannerRecovery.ts`) is not asked for again, nor for a malformed plan or one the page's own check refuses (`canvasBridge.ts` `recovered`, on its error and plan frames). A plan the workspace cannot apply (a review loop) is refused with its own code, `unsupported_plan_operation`, never asked for again and said as itself after a retry. The API names a failed planner run whose worker reported output tokens that reach the cap its snapshot froze for its model `output_limit` (`runs.go` `plannerSpentOutput`, the model matched exactly first), which the page says as a plan too long to write at once and does not ask for again; a node's run is as it was. Qwen still plans for a workspace past its daily planner ceiling (16 plans on 2026-10-22) and for a request past 128,000 bytes (none in 14 days). Tests: `planning_output_limit_test.go`, `canvas-planning-client.test.ts`, `saas-planning-recovery.test.ts` and `canvas-assistant.test.tsx`; each of 17 mutants of the change caught.
- Say that a node's model is working from the run's own event, not from how its run stands (2026-10-23, at the owner's 「继续做完」, who chose the cheaper of the two shapes when it was put to them as a cost decision). While a node waits for its first token the row under it showed 运行中 / Running with a running clock (`TileTranscript.tsx` `presenceLabel`, `WorkingTimer`; the status the transport sets at `runTransport.ts` and the run's own `running` event). That says a run is in flight, not that the model is doing anything, and on a reasoning model the first `text_delta` can be minutes away (see the Opus 5.5 stalls, where nothing came back at all) — so a reader could not tell a model that was working from a call whose delivery was lost. A node run now opts in to reasoning activity like a planner run (`X-Awwo-Run-Activity: reasoning`, which the Pi, JS and Python workers have always honoured per request and all gate *emission* on, so a run that does not ask still gets nothing), and the first count it reports becomes one `{"type":"reasoning_started"}` event on the run (`runs.go`, written through the same live-guarded `appendRunProgress`, and the flag set only once the row is in, so a failed write does not lose the signal for the whole run); the bridge turns it into the status 「模型正在思考…」 / "The model is thinking…" (`canvasBridge.ts`). Named for reasoning, not thinking, because `assertNoScratchpad` treats any durable sink or replay holding "think" as a leaked scratchpad — the tags being `<think>`/`<thinking>` — and a guard is not worth weakening for a name. Only a run that reaches the agent path asks: a media, team, computer or workspace run returns earlier and admits with no header, so a sandbox node still shows only how its run stands. A node run keeps **only the fact**: however many counts the worker sends, one event a run, and the counts are added neither to the run's hidden tokens nor to anything a reader can see. What a run is charged from is a separate decision from what its page says, and this was asked for as the latter, so a node run's charge is exactly what it was — worth knowing where that leaves things: for a call the provider refused without reporting usage, `creditCharge` and `sizeRefusal` both read hidden tokens as "did the provider do work?", so a node run that reasoned for minutes and was then refused is charged nothing while this very row says work happened. That gap predates this change, which only makes it visible, and closing it is the owner's to decide — reporting each would write a row about twice a second (`REASONING_REPORT_MS`), up to about 1,800 for a quarter-hour of thinking, on far more runs than the planner's. The status goes back to the run's own before the answer's first text, or the row under a long answer would go on saying the model was thinking while the answer streamed past it (found in review) — back to `running`, not to nothing, since an empty status is what makes the transcript fall back to `Sent. Waiting for the agent to start…`, the one label that otherwise never shows on a live run. Its own event type, not a `progress` frame, so the deploy readback's count of progress rows on non-planner runs stays zero; `readback.sh` gains a named count of those rows and of the runs that have one, which must be **equal**: one row a run. The run archive projects it by name (`run_archive.go`), beside the other events that are a fact with no payload — left out it would stand in a run's evidence as an `unsupported` row, once for every node run whose model reasoned. A malformed count is still `invalid_runtime_event` everywhere. Tests: `planner_progress_test.go` (two runs on one session each opt in, deliver their answer, and publish exactly one event carrying nothing but its type, for three reported counts, before their terminal event, with no progress and no hidden tokens; a malformed count on a node run is still refused; the archive projects the event by name and drops a count smuggled onto it) — this replaces the test that asserted the opposite, that a node run opted in to nothing and failed on the event; `canvas-media-nodes.test.tsx` (the bridge says it once for two events carrying counts, puts the status back to the run's own before the answer's first text and never to nothing, the answer still arrives, and neither count reaches the page).
- Take a canvas plan that gives a node's persona on `set_task` (2026-10-23, at the owner's 「persona 那个也按你的建议改」). Of the 15 plans that finished on the planner follow-up before the next release went live, one failed `invalid_canvas_plan` for it (08:18Z, Claude Haiku 4.5): a 193-character persona beside its acceptance criteria, on an Agent node already on the canvas. It is the one `set_task` with a key of its own among the 84 plans refused in the 14 days to 2026-10-23 11:36Z (`.local/release/read-plan-persona.sh` in the context-limit worktree, which prints key names, lengths and counts only), and a port of the gate takes that plan with this reading and nothing else: 44 of the 7 days' 61 refused plans against 43. The gate now reads such a persona as the protocol's own step for it, an `update_node` of that node right before the `set_task`, which keeps its lists, or is left out where it gave none (`planTaskSlips`); the canvas applies it as it applies any `update_node`'s persona: it sets an Agent node's, a media node has none, and on a form, assemble or edit node it refuses the plan, which it then does not ask for again as it does a plan the gate refused (none of the 84 gave such a node a persona). A persona that is blank (it could mean "clear it" or "nothing") or not text, and a `set_task` with any other key of its own (which a `set_task` left out must not take away with it), are still refused, and `update_node` keeps its 8,000-character limit. Tests: `planning_task_persona_test.go` (the 08:18Z plan in shape; a persona alone; on a node the same plan adds; every other persona and key refused, with a list and without), each of seven mutants of `planTaskSlips` caught.
- Take a canvas plan whose new node names the model that node takes anyway, and read a new node's outputs given on `add_node` (2026-10-23, at the owner's 「做，新节点上的模型也按你的建议改」). Of the first 5 plans after the planner follow-up went live, one was refused: its new node's constraints and input definitions were now read, but it also named a model and gave its outputs on `add_node`, which the gate still refused. In the 7 days to 2026-10-23 08:30Z, 4 of the 62 refused plans gave a model on `add_node` and 2 gave outputs there (`.local/release/read-plan-model-outputs.sh` in the context-limit worktree, which prints model ids and shapes only): in the one made since requests name the model new nodes take, the model given was that one (`deepseek-flash`), and both outputs were lists of whole field definitions. The gate now reads that model from the page's new-node line in the request's own context, when the request is made and before the request text and the asker's personal settings join it, as the page reads only its context (`planNewNodeModel` in `planCanvas`, kept in the run's snapshot as `planNewNodeModel`; `runs.go` passes it to `acceptPlanFor` when the run completes). It drops a model given on an Agent `add_node` that is that one, with no effort beside it, since such a node takes that model anyway (`planNodeSlips`). A model on an image, video or 3D node, which takes its own media model, any other model, a model where the context named none (a line in the request itself does not count), and a model with an effort are still refused: a plan changes a node's model only with `set_model`. A new node's outputs given as a list of whole field definitions are read as `add_field` steps of its output side right after it (`planNodeOutputs`), their values emptied as every new field's is, since an output is never filled; any other shape is still refused. Tests: `planning_new_node_model_test.go` (the line read in both languages and only at a line's start; the model dropped only where it is the one new nodes take, and never on a media node; outputs read, and every other shape refused; the refused plan of 06:10Z, in shape, taken whole; a planner run completing through `runs.go` with its context's model, and failing with another, none, or a line only in its request).
- Keep a checkout's own `.env` files and installed packages out of the worker images. `deploy/saas/pi.Dockerfile.dockerignore`, `openai-agents.Dockerfile.dockerignore` and `openmaus.Dockerfile.dockerignore` named the files each image copies after `**`, but also `!apps/` and the worker's own folder, and BuildKit counts a pattern that matches a folder for everything in it, so each build context took all of `apps/` (99 MB of tracked files alone; the managed execution's all of `third_party/` too, 357 MB), with a checkout's gitignored `.env` files and installed `node_modules` in it. The Pi and OpenAI Agents images copy their worker's folder after `npm ci`, so they held the checkout's `.env` in `/app` and laid the host's packages (Windows or macOS builds) over the Linux ones `npm ci` had installed. Each of the three now lets in only the files its Dockerfile copies, the managed execution's three notices of `third_party/openmaus-core/` by name, and ends with `**/.[eE][nN][vV]*` and `**/[nN][oO][dD][eE]_[mM][oO][dD][uU][lL][eE][sS]`: `.env*` and `node_modules` in any case of their names, since BuildKit matches names case-sensitively while Windows and macOS by default open `.ENV` as `.env`. A test plants both in every folder such a file reaches, in a folder of the checkout's own in each, and where each of its patterns lets them in itself (`.env.mjs` for `*.mjs`), and fails if a build context would take one (`scripts/awwo-saas-scripts.test.mjs`); it reads the files as BuildKit does, which compose and the SaaS workflow build with (the classic builder, `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0`, reads no Dockerfile's own ignore file). Built for real from a tree holding planted `.env` files and host packages: the old files put both into `/app`, the new ones into no context or image (each context is now under 1 MB); the Pi and OpenAI Agents workers still answer `/health` and pass the SaaS workflow's import smokes, and the managed execution's image passes its smoke. No worker reads a `.env` itself, and the hosted service runs its workers from release folders, not from these images (2026-10-23, found by the review of the worker images' fix below).
- Build the native release archive again (`scripts/awwo-saas-release.ts`, run by the SaaS workflow's `native-release` job): its source and its copy of the files the workers load beside their folders lacked `apps/context-estimate.ts` and `apps/context-overflow.ts`, which the workers import since the context-limit work of 2026-10-21, so its own import check of the assembled package stopped every build with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. One list names those files now, for the source and the copy, and a test reads what the released workers import or open against it (2026-10-23, with the worker images' fix below).
- Start the Pi and OpenAI Agents workers from their images again: `deploy/saas/pi.Dockerfile` and `openai-agents.Dockerfile` copy the files their worker imports beside its folder one by one, and neither copied `apps/context-estimate.ts` or `apps/context-overflow.ts`, which the workers and their shared modules import since the context-limit work of 2026-10-21, so a worker built from either image (as `deploy/saas/compose.yml` and the SaaS workflow's container job build them) stopped as it started. Both images copy them now, and a test reads each worker image's COPY lines, `.dockerignore` and `RUN rm` against what its scripts import, open with `new URL(…, import.meta.url)` or start by name, so the next such module fails a test instead (2026-10-23, found after the Windows installer's payload missed the same two files). The hosted service runs its workers from release folders, not from these images, and was not affected.
- Play the homepage film case as the canvas delivered it, and name the frame that is on screen (2026-10-23, released as `saas-5cc10aa56d69`, at the owner's 「继续往下落地运行，上线部署吧」). THE LONG CHORD Episode I's master — 1680x720 24p, h264 2.07 Mbps, AAC 195 kbps stereo, 951.67 s, 270,243,384 bytes — has been staged on the host since 2026-10-22 and was offered only as a download; the player streamed only the web copy the publisher makes, 1280x548 at 891 kbps (129,908,711 bytes), which is 58% of the master's pixels and 43% of its rate, while the heading above it read `1680×720`, the master's frame, over it. So a visitor who watched the film in AwwO never saw the frame the run delivered, and was told otherwise. `ProductionFilm.tsx` now offers that file: one button swaps the player's source, carrying the moment the viewer had reached (clamped to the film's end rather than dropped) and resuming playback if it was playing, since changing a src runs the load algorithm, which pauses and rewinds; a second switch before the first has loaded keeps the moment the viewer saw, not the fresh element's 0; a still clicked in the meantime wins over the carried moment; and the heading names the frame the player has actually decoded (`videoWidth`/`videoHeight`), naming none until it has decoded one, so it cannot misstate it again — including transiently, while the other file loads. The button is a plain action whose label says what the click will do, with no `aria-pressed` (a pressed state and a changing label contradict each other, and the pressed form would have announced the inverse of the truth). The web copy stays the default: the delivered file is three times the download. `ProductionFilm` is keyed by its case, so which file is playing, the frame decoded from it and a carried moment cannot survive into another case. `production-made.css`: the result header wraps rather than clipping, as it now carries up to two buttons beside the film's length and frame (measured in a browser against the real stylesheet at 320, 420, 520, 680 and 820 px: no overflow at any width, one extra row below 420 px only). `publish-recorded-run.mjs`: a film case's cover excerpt is encoded at crf 23, not 26 — a film case's cover is the only one made of film, where the other 22 are screen recordings of mostly still interfaces, and at crf 26 THE LONG CHORD's came out at 630 kbps, below the 945 kbps median of the recorded covers beside it; the web copy's frame and quality are named constants (`FILM_WEB_WIDTH`, `FILM_WEB_CRF`) with the measured cost of the current values written beside the encode, and the cache that skips the encode is named after the settings as well as the master, so raising either is no longer a silent no-op. Tests: `saas-production-film.test.tsx` (the web copy by default and the delivered file on request; the heading names no frame before one is decoded and the decoded frame after, for either file; the moment and the playback carry over; a second switch before the first loads; no `aria-pressed`) — the rewind a browser's load algorithm performs is done in the test, since jsdom does not, so the assertion about the carried moment is not tautological, and disabling the seek makes it fail. Not changed: the staged files themselves, named by this release exactly as before.
- Name no media provider in any message a user reads (2026-10-23, released as `saas-5cc10aa56d69`; owner 2026-10-11: on-screen model names, never the provider behind them). `media_real_person_rejected` read "（RunningHub 代码 1505）" and "(RunningHub code 1505)" — the generation service named outright, in both languages, in a message a user gets whenever a video node refuses a photorealistic person. It says "服务代码 1505" / "service code 1505" now: a support reference that names nobody. The comment above it still records which service the code came from. A guard in `saas-canvas-errors.test.ts` holds every message to the rule: it reads them evaluated, each code of `runErrorCodes()` in both locales through `runErrorText`, so a message built by interpolation, written in double quotes or joined from parts is covered, and then scans the rest of the copy in `canvasErrors.ts` and in `api.ts` — whose own table `canvasErrorMessage` and `runFailureText` fall through to for every code the first lacks, and which nothing was reading — from source with comments stripped whole (every `//` line and every block comment, so an apostrophe in one is not read as a quote). A Latin name must stand clear of Latin letters and digits, so "audio" does not name Udio and "sparkling" does not name Kling; a Chinese name is matched as written, because Chinese has no boundary to rely on. The boundary is deliberately Latin and not `[^\p{L}\p{N}]`: a Han character is itself a Unicode letter, so that form passed `（RunningHub代码 1505）` — one space from the string this change removes — and `用RunningHub生成时` and `这次由Seedream生成失败了` and `Tripo的 3D 模型` with it. Seven names the publisher's own list refuses were missing and are in now (ByteDance, Dreamina, Kuaishou, PixVerse, Shengshu, Nano Banana, Vidu, with 快手 and 生数). Checked live after the release: the served entry bundle holds `service code 1505` and no `RunningHub`.
- Run the media models in a workspace a platform administrator owns, as its catalogue and node setup offer them (2026-10-23, AwwO 本地版 0.1.0's every generation): a node's own run (`createRun`) and a canvas run's admission of each node (`admitGraphChild`) built the workspace's entitlement from the allowlist they read with their quota row and left its owner out, so without `AWWO_MEDIA_UNRESTRICTED_WORKSPACES` (AwwO 本地版 sets none) every image and video was refused `model_not_allowed`. Both now build it as `tenantModelEntitlement` does (`workspaceEntitlement`), reading the owner of an unrestricted workspace; another person's still needs the switch. The hosted site sets the switch, so nothing changes there. Found by the context-limit session's review. Test: `operator_workspace_test.go` (with the switch off, a Send and a canvas run of the operator's own media nodes reach the provider; another person's workspace cannot set one up, and one set up while the switch was on is refused when it runs, by its Send and by a canvas run); each path's old code fails it. AwwO Local 0.1.1 carries the fix.
- Take the canvas plans the gate refused for a slip with one safe reading, plan a large canvas on the operator's planner model, and send a request carried over from the workspace home with the reader's model named (2026-10-23, at the owner's 「需要决策就按照你的建议，就直接往楼下落地运行吧」). Of the 377 canvas plans of the 7 days to 2026-10-23 01:08Z, 71 failed `invalid_canvas_plan`: 40 of Claude Haiku 4.5's 298 and 31 of qwen3.8-27b-p6's 79 (the default model, which plans a request too large for the operator's planner model), and the share rose on 2026-10-22 to 19 of 54 and 26 of 53. Read on the host without their content (`.local/release/read-plan-slip-counts.sh` in the context-limit worktree, which counts each slip once a plan): Haiku's gave a new node its constraints on `add_node` (27 plans), its inputs under `inputs` (8, in three shapes), its model (7) or its outputs under `outputs` (3), and once named fields' sides in the plural (`inputs` and `outputs`, in one plan) and once typed an input field `image`; 15 of Qwen's put a note of plain text before the plan, about 10 were cut off before the plan's end, and the rest were broken JSON. Now `add_node` takes `constraints`, a task list like `set_task`'s, which the canvas gives the new node after the user's request, the node's first constraint that nothing replaces (shared requirement names expanded, an unknown one left out with a note, each once; a set_task's constraints on a node the plan adds come after the request too; past the task frame's limits (20 entries a list, 12,000 characters in all) the request stays whole, and of the plan's lists one is left out where the other fits beside it (the acceptance criteria kept, unless the constraints hold a shared requirement's text, the user's own words, by its name or written out), else both; a media node, which has no task requirements, takes neither list; what the nodes a plan adds were given and did not get, by add_node or a set_task after it, is said first, in at most four notes that always fit in the six the panel shows (`PLAN_NOTES_SHOWN`), each naming the nodes (five, the rest counted) and each node once with every list it lost: the media nodes given task lists, the nodes whose lists copied text the plan saw only in part, those whose lists did not fit, and the requirement names the canvas does not have; and the list of notes is no longer cut at 100, so the count of those the panel does not show is true: `canvasPlan.ts` `applyCanvasPlan`; the planning protocol, which names `constraints` among what a media node is not given, and `plannerInstructions` say so), and a page from before this release refuses such a plan, as the server did. `acceptPlan` reads `add_node.inputs` as the node's `inputValues` (an object of texts by field id, or a list of `{id, value}` pairs) or, for a list of whole input field definitions (id, label, type and required, a value only as text), as that many `add_field` steps right after it, their values set with `set_input` (`planNodeSlips`, `planNodeInputs`; the canvas updates a field the node already has to the definition rather than adding it twice); a side named `inputs` or `outputs` becomes `input` or `output`, and an input field typed `image`, `video` or `audio` a `file` (`planFieldSlips`). A model or an effort on `add_node` is still refused, since a plan changes a node's model only with `set_model`, which the instructions allow only when the user asks or a node failed because of its model, and the slip cannot say which; so is an output typed as a picture, which a text node cannot deliver, and so are outputs given on `add_node`, whose shape was not read. A plan behind a note of plain text is read, for `acceptPlan` and `validatePlan` alike (`planJSONBody`, `planAfterNote`): a note that holds no brace or bracket (none of the 16 plans behind a note in the week had one, and each began a line): the answer's first brace begins the plan, at the start of a line (after spaces too), its quotes repaired as an answer's own are, and it stands only when nothing but white space or a closing fence follows it; so a note after the plan, a second plan wherever the first is (in the note's line, after a carriage return, another space or a byte-order mark, in a list, its key's letters escaped), a truncated one, one at the end of the note's line, and a note with a list or an object of its own still fail. This reverses the rule of 2026-10-08 that refused a note before a fenced plan. Replayed against the 71 by a port of the final gate (`read-plan-rules-r5.sh`, which leaves the quote repair out), 46 would have passed: 30 of Haiku's, 16 of Qwen's. The operator's planner model now also takes a plan of up to 128,000 bytes of input (`defaultPlannerMaxInputBytes`, the most `AWWO_PLANNER_MAX_INPUT_BYTES` may say; production sets none) where it took 60,000: on 2026-10-22, 53 of the 108 plans were past 60,000 (canvases copied from the homepage cases are large) and planned on the default model, where 26 of them failed `invalid_canvas_plan`; the largest plan of the week, 108,904 bytes with the 6,212 of the instructions, fits. The daily ceilings (20 planner-model calls a workspace, 2,000 in all) still bound what the larger calls cost, a few cents each at Haiku's prices. And a request carried over from the workspace home now waits, at most 4 seconds (`HAND_OVER_MODEL_WAIT_MS`), until the canvas's palette and the reader's choice are read (`planNewNodeChoice`, the host's `componentModelRead`), so its plan is sized for the reader's model like one sent from the box; a palette that cannot be read, or the 4 seconds, sends it without naming one, as before. Tests: `planning_repair_test.go` (inputs read in each shape, a reserved ref renamed in the steps made for it, every shape without one reading refused, a model and an output picture refused; a plan behind a note, fenced or not, indented or pretty-printed, its quotes repaired, behind a note that quotes the key; a note after it, two plans wherever the first is, two bare plans, a truncated plan, one inside a truncated plan or object, inside a list or a truncated list, at the end of the note's line, a note with a brace, a list or an object of its own and a bracket line refused), `planning_fence_test.go` (a note before the block read, notes before and after refused), `planning_orchestration_test.go` (add_node's constraints admitted, malformed ones refused), `planner_model_test.go` (the new default), `tests/saas-plan-orchestration.test.ts` (the parser takes add_node's constraints; they follow the request, expanded, once each; past the limits the request stays whole, the criteria or the constraints kept where they fit; a media node's left out; what the nodes a plan adds did not get said first, from add_node and set_task alike, one note for each of the four kinds, five nodes named and the rest counted, past 100 other notes and within the six shown; a set_task's constraints after the request; the constraints kept over the checks where they hold a shared requirement's text), `tests/saas-plan-new-node-model.test.tsx` (a carried request waits for the reader's choice and names it; one whose choice is never read goes after the wait; sending it at once fails it). The protocol's two new phrases add 59 bytes, past two size guards with 5 and 11 to spare: `tests/saas-planning-budget.test.ts` now holds the planning context of its canvases under the 28,416-byte allowance less the 12KB it reserves (16,128 bytes; it said 16,000, and its seven-role canvas grew from 15,995 to 16,054), and `tests/saas-planning-recovery-storage.test.ts` gives the recovery journal 6,450 characters (6,400 before; the English journal grew from 6,389 to 6,421), as it was re-set on 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-15.
- Build the managed execution's core on Windows: its setup started `npx.cmd`, which Node refuses to start without a shell (CVE-2024-27980), so it failed at once; it now runs npx's own entry point under the same Node, as the npm launchers already do, and copying a local upstream checkout leaves its `node_modules` and `dist-server` out whichever path separator the filter sees (2026-10-21, found setting up AwwO 本地版).
- Tell the canvas assistant how much one node's answer holds, and have it split larger work into parts (owner 2026-10-22: 「单任务节点应该是有运行上限的，但是画布助手在规划的时候不知道这个限制，是不是应该给他的agent.md加个积极拆分任务的规则」). Of the 26 canvas-run nodes that failed in the 72 hours to 2026-10-22 14:38Z, 17 ended `output_limit` (the answer, with the model's thinking, outgrew the model's output limit), 16 of them on Claude Opus 5.5 after a median of about 9 minutes, in 5 workspaces. The planner's instructions said only that a node is one model call whose thinking counts against an output limit, never how large that limit is, and the model list it gets names none. A plan the canvas assistant requests now carries the node limits the workers publish now, after the canvas context and before the asker's personal settings and the request (`planning_limits.go`, `plannerNodeLimits`): for each model the workspace may run a node on, the most one answer holds in output tokens, thinking included (each worker's `/health` `maxOutputTokens`, which the API now reads per model as `piModel.MaxOutputTokens`, a value other than a whole number of tokens up to 2^20 read as unknown rather than failing the catalog; a worker that offers a model without a limit it can read counts as 16,000 for it, the instructions' own assumption, which the limits then say, so no model is sized past what is known of it; the least of openai-agents and Pi where both offer the model, since a node bound to a workspace Agent keeps that Agent's runtime while AwwO runs every other node on openai-agents where it offers the model, `nodeRuntime.ts`; today both give each model the same limit); the workspace default, which a node without a model runs on (`"default"`, openai-agents' own); and the run's time limit (`AWWO_RUN_TIMEOUT`). The page names the model the Agent nodes a plan adds without `set_model` take: the reader's choice for the canvas assistant, a DeepSeek one included, which the `set_model` list leaves out, or `"default"` where they run the workspace default (`canvasPlanning.ts` `newNodeModel`, a line of its own after the model list), once it has read both the canvas's palette and the reader's choice (the host's catalogue, `AssistantExecutionHost.componentModelRead`): before then, as a hand-over from the home page can be sent, and on the desktop, which has no palette, it names none. Those nodes then take the model the plan was sized for, as the plan frame names it from the request its run was made from (`newNodeModel`, read from the stored request's context, `canvasBridge.ts`; `canvasPlan.ts` `planNewNodeModel`), a resumed plan's and one another tab asked for too, not one the reader chose since (`assistantModel.ts` `planComponentModel`): `"default"` leaves them on the workspace default; a request that names none (stored before this release, or sent before those reads) gives its nodes the reader's choice now, read when the plan lands rather than when it was asked for, as before, as they do where the model it names is one they cannot take now (no longer offered or ready, or one the workspace's plan no longer includes, which `componentModelEntry` now refuses for every node a plan adds); and a model only a user may choose (DeepSeek) is taken only while the reader still has it chosen when the plan lands, since the privacy clause sends a request there only when it is selected. The workers are read only once the request is authorized, as every handler's effects are (`TestPostgresMutationRechecksAuthorizationAfterBodyWait`). Like the personal settings the limits join after the request's hash, so a retry once a limit changed is the same plan. Where the whole of them would take the prompt past its bound, or alone take a plan past the operator's planner model's input ceiling (`AWWO_PLANNER_MAX_INPUT_BYTES`, so they never move a plan onto the workspace's own calls), they go in a few words (the default's limit, under its own id too, the models whose limit is lower, at most 12 and the smallest first, and the least of the rest as the limit to take for every other model; with no default, the least of all as the limit to take for every model), and where even those would, not at all (a refusal from `createRun` then leaves room for them; the plan-bounds 413, made before they are read, does not); workers that publish no limit at all, or a deployment on personal model connections, add nothing. The instructions themselves grew by 1,930 bytes (4,282 to 6,212), which count against that ceiling (60,000 bytes by default, and production sets none): a plan within that much of it now runs on the workspace's default model, as an ordinary call, where it ran on the operator's planner model before; raising the default by 2,000 would keep the old boundary, which was left for the owner as a cost decision (raised to 128,000 on 2026-10-23, in the entry above). None of the 380 plans of the 7 days to 2026-10-22 18:00Z (49 workspaces, the planner model Claude Haiku 4.5) was in that band, nor within 2,000 bytes below it; 79 of them (21%) were past the ceiling already. The planner's instructions (`plannerInstructions`) now say how to use them: size each node's delivery before writing its brief and keep it within half of its model's limit, a sixth for code (the case pages' nodes spent 28,000-29,500 of 32,000 tokens on at most 16,000 characters of code, about a sixth of them on the code), two thirds for a node that only pastes parts in (about one and a half tokens a Chinese character, one for every three characters of English or code; a model the limits do not name sized by the limit they give every other model, else by the smallest they give, and 16,000 tokens where they give none); split anything larger (a long report or book, many chapters or scenes, many files or modules, a long list) by chapter, section, module or batch into part nodes that run side by side, each with its exact scope and its share of the user's totals, what they share given once (an outline node, or an @R requirement the context already lists), each as large as its node allows so the plan keeps within its operation limit (and the first parts planned, with what is left said, where more are needed); join parts only in a node whose joined delivery still fits one answer, otherwise let the parts be the result; review or rewrite long deliveries part by part; say briefly in summary how the work was split; size a node moved to the default model again for that model; split a page node's own code into code-module nodes past a sixth of its model's limit (about 16,000 characters on a 32,000-token model) rather than past a fixed 16,000 characters; and, since a page is still one node's answer with every part pasted in, keep a page that would not fit to what fits and say what was left out. Production's limits when this was written: 4,096 tokens for Gemini and the small Qwen, 16,384 for the default model and GPT-5.6, 32,000 for most Claude models, 64,000 for Claude Opus 5.5; read again on 2026-10-23, both runtimes give every model a limit, and an unrestricted workspace's limits name 48 models in 1,609 bytes, 12 of them below the default. A sandbox computer node, which a node opts into and which works in many model calls, is sized as one answer too, by the two runtimes' limits; its worker's own `/health` gives the same Claude limits (Claude Opus 5.5 64,000, read 2026-10-23), while the old JS worker on :8098, which no node runs on, still says 32,000 for it. Tests: `planning_limits_test.go` (the catalog field read only as a whole number in bounds; a plan's prompt with the entitled models' limits, the least of two runtimes, the default and the time limit, in its place and outside the hash, and with openai-agents down; the workspace default under an allowlist; the limits in a few words or left out rather than moving a plan off the planner model, kept by a plan past that model's ceiling anyway, and left out at the prompt's bound with the personal settings kept; in a few words, the default under both names, the models whose limit is lower and the least of the rest; at most 100 models, the least of the others said, and never one called "default"; a model a worker offers without a limit, the default's too, taken as 16,000 and said so, in the whole and in a few words; nothing without worker limits), `tests/canvas-planning-client.test.ts` (the new-node model's line, a DeepSeek one and `"default"` included, read back from its context; a plan marked with the model its frame names, a resume's too, and unmarked where no frame names one), `tests/saas-planning-recovery.test.ts` (through the bridge, a plan says the model its own request named, a resumed one the one its stored request named, not the one chosen since), `tests/saas-assistant-model.test.tsx` (the model the nodes a plan adds take: the one it was sized for, on the runtime AwwO runs it on; none for `"default"`; the reader's choice where it names none or one they cannot take now; DeepSeek only while chosen; never a model the workspace's plan does not include now), `tests/saas-plan-new-node-model.test.tsx` (on a hosted canvas: the reader's choice, or `"default"`, named to the planner, and none before the palette or the reader's choice is read; the node a plan adds on the model the plan was sized for, kept on the default when sized for it, and on the reader's choice when the plan lands where it names none; off a DeepSeek model the reader switched away from while it planned; applying the choice of the render that asked, or naming `"default"` before those reads, fails it).
- Name a model the operator's account has for 图片 · 高清, and price it by what that model charges (2026-10-22, at the owner's 「我全部同意」 and 「这是私有服务器，你继续吧，我的key就在上面」). X-tasy had revoked the API key the production API held: its free credits call, asked from the host, answered 401 `API_KEY_REVOKED`, while `media.env` had not changed since 2026-10-15 and the running API carried exactly the key in it. So every image and video node of that runtime failed `media_provider_unauthorized` at its first authenticated call from 2026-10-21 05:19Z to 2026-10-22 02:19Z: 31 runs in 5 workspaces, 25 refused at the submit, 5 at the reference upload and 1 on a resend, none of which created a task, so nobody was charged and 30 of them gave their free attempt back. The owner made a new key; the host proved it (200, 7,770.53 credits) and proved the old one refused before one line of `media.env` was replaced by a rename and the API restarted once on its own release at 07:12:20Z, which is a host change and not part of this release. Its account then listed 27 models and 7 of AwwO's 8: `model_db5a9f8c-…`, the Seedream 5.0 Pro that 图片 · 高清 named on 2026-10-10, was not among them, so that one model failed `media_provider_unavailable` instead (5 runs on production between 07:52Z and 08:10Z), and it is X-tasy's first image model, the one a new image node starts on wherever `AWWO_XTASY_ALL_WORKSPACES` offers them and Jimeng's are not granted. 图片 · 高清 now names `model_0c50c8be-…`, the flash model of the same family as 图片 · 全能, and keeps its id and its label, so the 61 nodes saved on it (26 canvases, 17 workspaces) and the stored official and epic workflows keep their model. Only 2K is offered: the model's own list names 4K as well, but a 4K generation is refused (`GEN_INVALID_PARAMETER`, "image area must be at most 4624220 pixels" — 4K at 1:1 is four times that area and 2K at 1:1 fits), and a setting that cannot generate is not offered; the 1K of the old model goes with it, which no saved node holds (36 hold 2K, 25 none) and none of the 76 runs since 2026-10-01 asked for. Nothing here is taken from that list, which is what offered the 4K the model refuses: each of the eight ratios generated at 2K, the widest (21:9) and the tallest (2:3) included, so the area limit does not reach 2K at any of them, and all eight charged the same 4 credits; and the model edited an uploaded picture in img2img, the one capability the id carries over that its family had never been generated with. Its price is three times those 4 credits, taken to the images' floor of 30, where the model it replaced earned 40. Measured through the API's own client by `TestXtasyLiveEveryModel`, which generated with 图片 · 标准多张 in the same run to prove the new key end to end — submit, poll, download and sniff: 379 KB `image/jpeg` in 17 s — and whose 4K attempt failed with its reservation released, charging nothing. That run also measured 图片 · 标准多张 at 16 credits where 2026-10-10 measured 9.6, so its 30 is no longer three times what it costs, though still above it (30 credits is $0.30 at a paid plan's rate, the generation $0.16); its own verified date is this run's, so the catalog does not read as though that price were still measured, and the rest of the catalog's prices, not revisited, are left for the owner with it. The live test now takes `AWWO_XTASY_LIVE_PROXY`, a loopback proxy (checked to be one) for a machine whose own exit the provider's edge refuses with a 403 that reads as `media_provider_unauthorized` (a block, not a key); `AWWO_XTASY_LIVE_PARAMS`, a node's params as JSON, to measure a setting that is not the default; and `AWWO_XTASY_LIVE_REFERENCE`, a picture to generate from, so that a listed img2img mode is proved by a generation. Params it cannot resolve now fail it instead of being recorded while it passes. Tests: `xtasy_test.go` (图片 · 高清 names the model the account has and no catalog model names the retired one; it offers 2K alone with 2K its default and the eight ratios that generated, by name; 4K is refused by the catalog before any generation is paid for; it still edits one reference picture and generates from text by default; its price at its own defaults is 30; and it is the first X-tasy image model, so a new image node starts on one the account has). With the backup released the same day, a generation on this model that failed `media_provider_unavailable` was already being made by RunningHub instead, so what this ends is the detour, not an outage: the model's own service makes its pictures again, at its own price, and `mediaBackupModels` no longer names the id after a model it does not name. It also narrows that backup in one direction: a RunningHub Seedream picture asked for at 1k now has no X-tasy backup, since 图片 · 高清 makes 2K alone and a backup makes what the run asked for rather than something sharper (`media_fallback_test.go` shows the refusal and keeps the 2k picture that still crosses). - Make a picture or a clip on the other media service when its own fails it for a reason on the operator's side, instead of failing the node (owner 2026-10-22: 「媒体模型失败就换runninghub,两个互为备选」; seen from 2026-10-21 05:19Z: X-tasy refused the key on the first call of every generation, 31 runs failed). A run is admitted with the other service's same model, or the nearest of its kind, frozen as its backup (`media.backups` in the run's snapshot; a canvas run reads it again when its node's turn comes), where that model makes the node's shape, sharpness, number of pictures, length and sound under its own names and spellings (`mediaBackupParams`; an automatic shape takes the backup's default) and the workspace may use it; a setting the run chose that no backup is known to make (a quality, its own negative prompt, a lossless format, a seed, the real-person switch) refuses them all. The backup makes the generation once, from the same words and references when it takes them all, read the same way (a single picture is X-tasy's videos' first frame and RunningHub's multimodal video's subject, so it goes to neither the other way: `mediaBackupFor`), with at least half of the run's time left, when the first service has no client, refuses the first send before any task exists (a new `rhError.NoTask`, which `refusedAnswer` marks for every definite refusal, RunningHub's 4xx, rate limit and flat refusal included, and `submitMedia` takes back after a resend), refuses a reference upload for a reason of its own, or says in the task's own state that it ended without a result (a new `rhError.Ended`: failed, expired, refused, final even when its code reads busy; X-tasy, which says what it charged, only when it charged nothing; a submission's answer naming such a task too), for a code in `mediaBackupCodes`. Nothing goes to the backup after a refusal that answered a resend, without an answer, while the first service only fails to say how its task is doing (a refused key or an error status while polling, a "no such task", which a key of another account gives for tasks still being made, an answer about another task, which also no longer refunds or fails this one: `pollMedia`), after the run's own time ran out, for results of a delivered task that could not be stored, or for a reference that could not be used (its stored file, or the picture itself refused); a refusal of the content (`media_content_rejected`, `media_real_person_rejected`) stays final, X-tasy's now on a 403 and on an expired task too when its code refuses the content in so many words, a word of content with one of refusal (`CONTENT_POLICY_VIOLATION`) and none about the account, a timeout or an outage (they read as the key's and as a lost result, as a 401, a 402 and the other codes of a 403 or an expiry still do: `xtasyModerationCode`). The canvas shows 「主通道暂不可用，已换用备用模型…」, then 「排队等待备用模型生成…」 and 「正在用备用模型生成…」 (`media_status` `backup`; `apps/web/src/saas/canvasBridge.ts`), and the result's record says `"backup": true` (`mediaBackupRecord`), which every view of the result shows as 「主通道暂不可用，这次由备用模型生成。」 (`MediaResult`), in a canvas run and after a reload too. The generation stays one, charged once at the model and price it was admitted on (`settleMedia`, `markMediaBackup`): the first route's refusal gives the free attempt back only once no backup is sent, so no other run takes its place meanwhile; one the first service never took is again unsent for the backup, so the backup's refusal (for its key, or for the request built for it) or a cancel before its send gives the attempt back; one the first service took keeps counting, and a charge it made stands (`firstCharged`, which a refund of the backup's task does not take back). What the first route's end gives back, its refusal's free attempt or its refund, is written only once no backup is sent, so the plan's credits stay reserved meanwhile; a refunded first task whose backup made nothing reads as refunded again (a canvas may run the node again). A run's own task that its submission's answer names as ended without a charge is refunded as a polled one is, with no backup too, so a canvas may now run such a node again. The run fails with what went wrong first, unless the backup refused the content (a refused real person is told as refused content: `mediaBackupFailure`). `runs.media_task` names the backup's provider and model, the first service's code (`backupFor`), task id (`firstTaskId`) and charge, and keeps the time the generation was first sent (or the run began), so a restart follows the backup's task on its service within the run's own deadline; a run's own task that fails after a restart moves to its backup (`resumeMedia`). A model whose service is not configured is still refused at admission. - Say which node a canvas run was refused for when one media node's own saved settings refuse the whole canvas (found 2026-10-22 by a code-reviewer pass over the catalogue repoint that narrowed 图片 · 高清 to one resolution). A canvas run freezes the model and settings of every media node in its scope before it starts (`graph_runs.go`), so a setting that model does not take refuses the whole run with 400 `media_params_invalid` — 「节点的生成参数不适用于所选模型，请在节点配置中修改。」 — and the refusal named no node: on a canvas the size of THE LONG CHORD's (305 nodes) that is a blind hunt. A node is saved only with settings its model takes (`mediaSetupProblem`), so such a setting is one that fitted when it was chosen and stopped fitting afterwards, because the model's own choices narrowed under it (an offer repointed to another generator, its id unchanged) or because the node arrived carrying another workspace's settings in a copied case. Two things happen now. The refusal carries the node's id in `details.nodeId` where that node's own saved state caused it (`media_params_invalid`, `node_setup_required`, `model_unavailable`, `model_not_allowed`: `mediaGraphAdmissionError` in `media_runs.go`), and the page puts that node's title in front of the service's copy (「“海报”：节点的生成参数不适用于所选模型，请在节点配置中修改。」, `refusedNodeMessage`); the deployment's own refusals (generation not configured, no room to store a result) name no node, and a node's own Send, whose caller chose the node, carries no details as before. Only the id travels: a node's title is the reader's own words and stays out of an API error, and the page owns the titles. And a run is refused before it is sent, naming **every** node in its scope that holds such a setting at once (「有 2 个节点的生成设置不被它的模型接受：海报、封面。请打开它们重新选择；如果打开这张画布之后模型有变动，刷新页面即可。」, `preflightGraphIssue`), so they are fixed in one pass rather than one refusal at a time, and the reader re-picks in each node's settings, where the offending parameter is already marked and its stale value still shown. The copy offers a reload too, because this page reads the models once, when the canvas opens, and nothing in it re-reads them while they are read successfully. Without a catalogue to judge by (a local canvas, a catalogue not read yet, a failed read) the settings are not judged on the page at all and the service refuses that run, naming the node. The run's own callback reads the catalogue through a ref, as it already reads the model palette: it does not re-create itself when the catalogue arrives, and read an empty one until a test caught it. **No setting of a node whose model stays is deleted for the reader**: an open canvas's catalogue is read once, when it opens, so a tab left open across a release that widened a model's choices holds a stale, narrower one, and dropping a setting by it would silently and permanently lose a choice the workspace accepts (a silent patch leaves no undo entry, and the autosave carries it up). The refusal is a warning the reader can clear — re-pick, or reload for a newer catalogue — and the same catalogue already decides what a node may be saved with, so this adds no judgement the page did not already make. A node moved off a retired generator's model still starts from its new model's defaults, settings included, exactly as before (`replaceRetiredMediaModels`, owner decision 2026-10-11): that model is a different one, and its settings are not the old one's to keep. Tests: `graph_media_test.go` (a canvas refused for one node's settings, and for its changed type, carries that node's id and not the other media node's; generation this deployment does not run, and a host that cannot store a result, name none; a node's own Send carries no details; nothing reached the provider); `canvas-media-nodes.test.tsx` (which nodes the preflight names, all of them at once in canvas order, and which it does not — with no catalogue, out of the run's scope, for a model this workspace is not offered, for a node holding no settings; and that a refused run stays refused rather than quietly becoming runnable); `saas-graph-runs.test.ts` (the node id read from a refusal, and none claimed from one that named none, an empty or non-string id, or a request never sent); `canvas-surface-messages.test.ts` (the titles in front of the service's copy in both languages, and the copy as worded where no node was named or the page no longer holds it); `saas-canvas-initialization-surface.test.tsx` (a run refused for such a node names it, is not sent, and leaves its settings exactly as they were; a node whose settings the workspace still accepts runs; and the node a sent run was refused for is named). A run's frozen canvas is written once, when it is admitted, so the canvas's observer reads its run whole at its first poll, keeps that canvas, and reads the run without it at every poll after, merging the one kept (`GraphObservation`): the merge sees what a whole read gives, and still checks a collaboration's frozen canvas against its admission and finds a cached ancestor's node in it; until the merge accepts a read, every read is whole, and after that the reads leave the canvas out whatever their outcome. Every other reader reads a run whole as before: the panel's first read of a run when it opens or one is picked, the 成果 receipt, opening a canvas, the evidence export and the scripts. A page opened before this release reads whole until it is reloaded, and an API from before it sends the run whole whatever the query says. A run is read whole by its own route (`GET …/graph-runs/{id}`, unchanged) where it is needed. The open panel reads the run it shows when it opens and when another is picked, then again only when the list says it changed (its status, last update, or a node's state or attempts: a node's output and run move only with them, a retry taking a node from running back to running after a wait no poll need see, so a film's run of hours is read once a step, not once a poll) and on every poll while it is a collaboration going on, whose turns the list does not carry; it reads none while closed, and opened again it shows what the list says until its new read (`GraphRunPanel.tsx`). The 成果 receipt reads the frozen canvas of the run it names once a page, for its models and whether the run covered the whole canvas (`CanvasRunReceipt.tsx`). Opening a canvas reads whole, at once, every run it may recover (those still going and the latest, at most 4), and recovers none if one of them cannot be read, as when the list could not be (`SaaSApp.tsx`). A run journal that lost its run's id takes it from Stop's answer or finds it in the list, and reads the run by it (`observeCloudGraph`). A page opened before this release, until it is reloaded: its run history shows steps by their ids, without outputs or model call records, and its receipt no models; a run whose admission it never heard back from (rare) it may settle without publishing its result (the run history keeps it, and a reload recovers it while it is the canvas's latest run), or, for a collaboration, keep showing as running. Tests: `graph_runs_test.go` (the list of a plain and a collaboration run, and the lookup by operation, carry exactly the summary's fields, each as the run's own read has it, the nodes by id and state in order, under 2 KB where the runs' own reads carry 16 KiB answers), `graph_retry_test.go` (during a retry the list's node carries its attempts, a node not retried none); `saas-graph-panel.test.tsx` (closed, the list alone every 5 s; opened, the run it shows read whole, again only when the list says it changed; a collaboration going on read on every poll; a retry the list shows only by its attempts read again; a picked run read once; opened again, only what the list says until the new read; while a read is pending, only the list's summary; a failed read says so and Retry reads it again); `saas-results-gallery.test.tsx` (the receipt reads its run once however often the poll comes, claims nothing from a canvas it could not read, and reads nothing for a copied case); `saas-graph-runs.test.ts` (an observation reads the run by the id the list or Stop gives); `saas-canvas-lifecycle.test.tsx` (a recovery publishes from the run's own read, not the list; one unreadable run recovers none, and the next opening both). Mutations: each of 14 fails a test.
- List a canvas's stored files to their end, not stop at the newest 500 (2026-10-22, at the owner's 「不用重录，继续做第二、三幕」: THE LONG CHORD's canvas has stored more than 630 files, and publishing its Episode I checks every file the case shows against AwwO's own listing). `GET /tenants/{tenantId}/canvases/{id}/artifacts` said `truncated` past 500 files but could not read the rest; a page with more after it now carries `nextCursor`, which `?cursor=` takes to the next page, signed like the tenant lists' cursors and bound to its reader, the workspace, the canvas and the moment the first page was read, so a file stored after that moment is in no later page. A listing is not a snapshot of the table: a text deliverable stored again while the listing is under way, or a file of a transaction that began before the listing, can be missing from it (a new listing shows it). The first page is the newest 500 as before, but files stored at one instant are now ordered by id descending, so where a page ends among them it can hold others of them than before. A query that does not parse is refused with 400 invalid_pagination, as the tenant lists refuse it.
- Let `npm run check:hygiene` read only what the repository holds, not output git ignores beside it (2026-10-22, found by the local edition's session). Once the managed execution's core was built (`apps/openmaus-worker/setup.ts` clones and builds it into `apps/openmaus-worker/.runtime/core`, which `apps/openmaus-worker/.gitignore` ignores), the check reported 600,795 carriage returns in 2,301 files there (such as `.claude/skills/verify-omb/SKILL.md`) and failed, though none of them is AwwO's: without paths it walked its default roots and skipped only `node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `coverage`, `.git` and `__pycache__`. In a git checkout (a root that holds its own `.git`) it now scans the files git lists under those roots (`git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`, each root matched whatever its case, as Windows and macOS find `Docs/` for `docs`): every tracked file, also one under a folder the walk skipped (none is tracked today), and a new file not yet added, unless git ignores it. As in the walk, it reads nothing through a symbolic link or junction below a root (Git for Windows lists files through a junction), and files come in the walk's order. Only a tracked file git itself reports absent, deleted from the working tree or left out of a sparse checkout, is passed over: any other listed file that cannot be found again fails the check as unreadable, as one whose name git cannot spell does (Git for Windows writes a lone surrogate in a name as U+FFFD), unless something really spelled with U+FFFD sits beside it, which git, and so the check, reads in its place (git cannot add the hidden file either, so the repository can never hold it). The check fails as a setup error (exit 2), and is never walked instead, when git cannot list the checkout (no git, a broken `.git`, a `.git` git does not take for the top of its checkout), when git warns as it lists (it warns and exits 0 for a directory it cannot open; its advice, such as a sparse index's hint, is turned off), when a default root is reached through a link (git lists the link, not the files behind it; named on the command line, the root is still walked) and when git lists a text file whose path is not UTF-8 (the name of a file the check does not read cannot stop it). The variables that tie git to one repository (those `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` lists, such as `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and the `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` that `git -c` exports, but not `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, which no git exports), which a hook or alias may export, are left out of git's environment, and so are those that change how git reads a pathspec or where its output goes (`GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS` and the like, Git for Windows' `GIT_REDIRECT_STDERR`, every `GIT_TRACE*`); trace2, which a configuration can turn on too, is turned off. Any other root, such as the `git archive` trees the release gates check, is walked as before, and so are paths named on the command line; the report says which listing it used (`listing` in `--json`: `git`, `walk` or `paths`).
- Settle a request its provider refuses as larger than its model's window as the size refusal it is, not as a failure of the model (2026-10-21, with the fix below: a request is admitted at an estimate 15% above every text measured, but a text unlike them could still pass a window). Such a refusal (Anthropic's "prompt is too long" or "exceed context limit", Bedrock's "Input is too long for requested model", an OpenAI-compatible provider's "maximum context length" or `context_length_exceeded`, and the others the Pi agent library knows: `apps/context-overflow.ts`, with a Python twin and shared cases) failed as `runtime_failed`: counted, charged at its input's estimate, run twice more on a canvas node and shown as the model's failure. The workers now tell it by the provider's own words inside the worker, never relayed (the Pi child; the Python worker's error classes; the Bedrock bridge, which reports it with the type `context_length_exceeded` and fixed words instead of AWS's message; a direct task's call, labelled `provider:<status>:context_length_exceeded`), and answer `MODEL_CONTEXT_LIMIT`. The API settles such a call as one that never began (not counted, not paid for), fails its run as `context_limit`, which a canvas node does not run again and the page explains, and ends a direct task as too large for its model (`computer_context_limit`). A worker answers so only for a refusal made before any work: the provider's HTTP 400, 413 or 422 to the call's one request, before any stream, in a body that is JSON and carries no work (no usage that counts anything, beside its error, inside it or one field down, and none of an answer). A refusal inside a stream that answered 200 may follow work that no one sees (the model's reasoning, which the API never sees of an ordinary run), so it stays the model's failure it was, as does one beside work, in a body that is not JSON or that the worker cannot read to its own end, after a retry (the Python worker counts its call's requests: the Agents SDK may send one again itself), or from a Bedrock model's other profile after the first one refused (the bridges then answer AWS's plain validation failure) (the Pi child reads the refusal's body itself, beside the SDK, since the agent library drops it; a direct task's refusal carries the detail `before-output`, without which the API takes no provider's label for one, so an older worker's is counted). The API never takes it for a call whose provider reported usage, nor for one that came more than 15 s after the API sent the call to its worker (as it already reads a refused call's charge: a refusal after a while may follow work), and neither the daily calls nor the operator planner model's ceilings count a call that never began. The Python worker's own refusal of a request larger than its model's budget, made before it calls the model but after its answer to the API began to stream, is `CONTEXT_LIMIT` now (it was `OUTPUT_LIMIT`, a model failure charged and run again) and settles the same way.
- Let a run, a canvas plan and a direct task carry what their model can really read, not one byte a token (owner 2026-10-21, 「继续做完」: step 4 of the context-limit fix). Every input budget compared UTF-8 bytes with a model's token window, which is always safe but refused far below what models read: Chinese runs three bytes a character, and a qwen3.8-27b direct task was refused at 28,416 bytes when its previous call had been 7,332 tokens. Each production model read 16 texts through the production workers on 2026-10-21; Chinese, English, code and Markdown ran at 2.1-6 bytes per token, base64, numbers, SVG paths, minified code and URLs at 1.02-1.8. So a text now counts its dense parts (digits, long unbroken runs, punctuation and symbols other than CJK and full-width ones, runs of more than 32 whitespace characters, scripts other than CJK) byte for byte and the rest at the model's measured rate, 15% denser than measured: `apps/context-estimate.ts`, with twins in Go and Python and shared test cases. The rates (36 Bedrock models in `bedrock-models.json`, the LLM Gate models in their worker settings) reach the API through each worker's `/health` (`proseBytesPerToken`); the API freezes a run's rate with its budget and counts its admission, its history, a team turn, a direct task's calls and a plan's `contextRoom` the same way the worker counts its own. A model nobody measured, and every run admitted before this release, keeps the byte rule. The fixed bounds of a run's prompt (128,000, which a canvas node's prompt with its files keeps too) and of a plan's canvas context (120,000) count UTF-16 code units, as the workers' transport counts them (Pi's `promptChars`), not bytes: Chinese takes three times more there, ASCII the same; a refusal's `contextRoom` stays in bytes of the context (at its own bytes per unit), and the page fits a hosted canvas's views in units and bytes.
- Ask Bedrock to stream Claude Opus 5.5's thinking as a summary on the Python worker, so that a call to it is not silent for minutes, and fail such a call that offers no tools after 3 minutes without a byte instead of 15 (owner 2026-10-21: 「确认」, to the proposal made with the Opus 4.8 limit below). Opus 5.5 always thinks, and as the bridge called it (no `thinking` setting: adaptive thinking, display "omitted") Bedrock sent nothing at all, not even `messageStart`, until its thinking ended. The opus55-stall session's read-only investigation the same day found that since the move to UCloud 40 of this worker's 183 Bedrock calls had failed silently (none of 1,201 on EC2), none of them still thinking at its limit: Bedrock never received 17; it finished 12 in 74-364 s whose answers stopped after their headers; and it ran 11 silently to their 64,000-token cap in 559-647 s, whose answers never arrived, while fully silent streams of up to 360.6 s were delivered. With `additionalModelRequestFields.thinking = {type: adaptive, display: summarized}`, which Bedrock accepted in all 14 probe calls from the host that sent it and ran on 10-21 (both profiles, `global.` and `us.`), the thinking streamed from 3.7-8.6 s into a call (8.6 s with a 110,668-token input) and no call was silent for more than 6.5 s, also two that thought for 3.2 and 3.5 minutes on a question that, asked without the summary, sent nothing for 192.5 s; calls of the same question took about as long as without the summary. The limit is still an empirical bound for a healthy call, not a guarantee. One summarized call of that question ended `content_filtered` after 35 s; among the 2,906 Opus 5.5 invocation records in production since 10-12 joined to their runs (517 on the Python worker, where a run is one call), none belonged to a run recorded as `model_refused`, which is how such a stop reads and which R-1 does not repeat, so that rate is read about a day after the release, and should it recur on ordinary tasks `SUMMARIZED_THINKING_MODELS` is emptied (which also brings back 15 minutes). Every Opus 5.5 call now asks for the summary (`SUMMARIZED_THINKING_MODELS`, `with_summarized_thinking` in `apps/openai-agents-python-worker/bedrock_bridge.py`), with or without tools and on either profile, and one that offers no tools waits at most 3 minutes for its next byte (`QUICK_FIRST_BYTE_SECONDS`; as a model of `THINKS_SILENTLY`, Opus 5.5 gets the short limit only while its command carries the summarized display, so taking it out of `SUMMARIZED_THINKING_MODELS` brings back 15 minutes too); a call with tools keeps 15 minutes, since Bedrock holds a tool call's input back until it is written. The summary crosses the worker as a count only, and node runs do not ask for reasoning activity, so what the API receives is unchanged. The long-silent answers should now arrive, those at the cap as `output_limit`, which R-1 does not repeat at 64,000 tokens a try; the lost requests and the answers lost after their headers are not prevented, but for a call without tools they fail as `provider_unavailable` after 3 minutes instead of 15 and R-1 runs their nodes again. The connection fixes the investigation proposed (a short deadline for the response headers with one retry, closing pooled connections left idle) are not part of this. Tests in `test_bedrock.py`: which models are asked, on both profiles and with the prompt cache; the per-call limits with and without the summary, with other thinking settings and with tools; the limit back at 15 minutes for a model no longer asked; a stalled Opus 5.5 call without tools failing at its limit while one with a tool waits the idle limit; and runs that stream the summarized thinking as a count before their answer and before a tool call. Nine mutants each fail some of them.

- Fail a stalled call of a canvas node to Claude Opus 4.8 after 3 minutes without a byte instead of 15, so that its node runs again sooner (owner 2026-10-21: 「按你的建议做第一个根因方案」, a shorter wait for the first byte, then 「按模型设限 + 试探」, a limit by model). From 2026-10-19 to 10-21 14:23Z 16 node calls on the Python worker got nothing back for the whole 15-minute idle limit before they failed as `provider_unavailable`; 12 of their nodes ran again 15 or 30 s later (R-1's retry intervals). Two were on Opus 4.8 (10-20), whose nodes then answered in 32 and 34 s, and 14 on Opus 5.5. Opus 4.8 does not think silently: none of the 5,341 of its calls that completed on the Python and sandbox workers from 10-12 took 3 minutes in all (the longest 123.5 s, its longest wait for the first text 48.8 s), so the limit, which bounds any gap between two reads and not only the first byte, is above every gap seen in a healthy call: an empirical bound, not a guarantee, since a healthy call silent that long would fail too. The two nodes of 10-20 would have answered about 4 minutes after their stalled calls began instead of about 16. Opus 5.5 keeps 15 minutes: it always thinks first and Bedrock sends nothing until it has, which may take its whole 64,000-token limit, 11 minutes or more, so a silent call may still be working. A call that offers tools keeps 15 minutes whatever its model, since Bedrock holds a tool call's input back until it is written, and models not measured keep it too. The limits are by Converse model ID without the inference profile's prefix (`QUICK_FIRST_BYTE_SECONDS`, `call_read_timeout` in `apps/openai-agents-python-worker/bedrock_bridge.py`); a call offers no tools when its command carries no `toolConfig` (no tools, or `tool_choice` none), both profiles of a call wait the same limit, and a run's shorter deadline still comes first. A cut call fails as an idle cut did: a 504 `ReadTimeoutError`, `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`, `provider_unavailable`. R-1 runs its node again only when the run produced nothing, its graph still runs and a retry is left (a call that wrote text and then went quiet for 3 minutes fails the same way but is not run again), each attempt a run charged on its own. A node's three attempts now end within about 10 minutes instead of about 46, so a Bedrock stall that lasts longer than about 7 minutes can fail the node, which a later attempt might have outlasted before. A call cut after 3 minutes without a first text is estimated at about 21,600 hidden tokens (120 a second before the first text) instead of the 65,536 cap. The Python worker only. Tests in `test_bedrock.py`, against real botocore and a local endpoint that stalls before and after its response headers: the per-call limits (profile prefixes, tools, `tool_choice` none, other models), a stalled Opus 4.8 call without tools failing at its limit while one with a tool and a call to Opus 5.5 wait the idle limit, the fallback profile asked with the call's own limit, and a run of either model ending as the service's outage long before its deadline; four mutants (the old behaviour, tools ignored, every model quick, the profile's prefix kept) each fail some of them.
