- Keep a long direct task (直接执行) working when its turn outgrows its model, and say so when even that cannot be done (owner report 2026-10-21, as below). A task's turn keeps every tool call and result it gathered, so its model calls grow; the first one past its model's byte budget was refused (by the API's model proxy, or by the worker's own measure, 413 `CONTEXT_LIMIT`), the broker passed that on as `MODEL_PROXY_FAILED`, and the task ended as `computer_execution_failed` (「任务在执行途中失败了（执行服务或一次模型调用出了错），没有做完。」), whose retry ended at the same call (2026-10-16: a qwen3.8-27b task's tenth call, at 7,332 tokens of input). Now such a call goes without the bulk of its oldest tool traffic (`computer_history_fit.go`), oldest first: an earlier tool result keeps its first 256 bytes (what a receipt says) and a note of how many more it returned, and an earlier tool call keeps its arguments' keys and short values (a path, a command), each value over 256 bytes replaced by a note; a result or arguments under 1 KiB stays whole, so a write's or a publish's receipt and the answer to a question the task may not ask are never cut, and each note says the call ran and its effects stand, to read again what it needs rather than repeat an action. The cut goes as far as the call needs and a fifth of the model's budget more, and the next calls keep it where it was while they fit, so that they start as the last one did (what a provider's prompt cache keeps) and the cut moves only once that room is used; a call that fits whole starts it over. The latest exchange (the last answer that called tools, its results and anything after them, the note of a task's last call among them), the task's words and every other text stay as sent, byte for byte. A call too large even then, or one checked only by the worker's measure (the call's JSON, 32 bytes a message, within the budget, `computerCallFitsWithin`), ends its task as `computer_context_limit` (`noteRefusal`, the first refusal kept), as does a turn going round in circles (`thrashesLocked`: two files that do not fit the model together would otherwise trade places until the task's calls ran out, each call paid): in a row of calls whose latest results bring back nothing but what the call before them lost (every copy of it cut by the fewest messages that fit: what goes only for the room the next calls get, or because the last call cut it, is not lost; the same read or list answering byte for byte, `resultPrints`: a command, a write, a publish or an archive may change the workspace and is something new every time, however alike its output), the same result a second time. Reading again what was lost, as the note asks, a changed result (an edit read again), a check run again after a fix with the same output, files that fit while the same one of them stays left out, and a result asked twice in one answer never end a task, and none of this is noted for a call the lease does not take (one still in progress, say), nor counted for a call that fits whole. It is a heuristic: a turn that also brings something new each time runs on to the task's call limit, as before. The API logs each such end, with its reason (size or going round) and the cut, but no content; its card says what happened and what to do (「任务要交给模型的内容超出了这个模型一次能读的量，没能继续。可以换一个上下文更大的模型，或把任务拆成几步、每步少带些资料分别发。」, whether at the task's first call or part-way) and offers no retry that would end the same way; the summary of an earlier task for the next one says it too. Refunds are as before: a call refused for its size was never the platform's fault (`direct_task_refund.go`). Tests: computer_history_fit_test.go (where each message and call is; what is left out and what never is, receipts and the latest exchange byte for byte included; where the cut stays and how far it goes; heads that split no escape or character; long argument values, not keys; when a result is the same again, what a call loses, and a turn going round in circles, not an edit loop; the first refusal kept; end to end, against a model worker that measures as the real one does: a 37 KB turn on a 28,416-byte model goes without its oldest traffic, one within the budget but over the worker's measure too, a call that fits whole starts the cut over, one over that measure even without its traffic is refused here, a latest exchange too large and a turn going round two files end their tasks as `computer_context_limit`, refused before any reservation, here and in the worker's own measure, none of them given back, and a build checked again after each of four fixes with the same errors goes on, as do three files that fit while the same one stays left out, two of them read back in turn), earlier_tasks_test.go, direct_task_refund_test.go, saas-task-endings.test.tsx.
- Let the canvas assistant plan on a large canvas instead of refusing it as too long (owner report 2026-10-21: 「用户遇到了上下文过长不执行的的情况」). Every plan sent the whole canvas (each node's brief, requirements, acceptance criteria and input values), the last ten turns and the selected knowledge, and a request over its model's byte budget was refused with 413 `context_limit` (「输入超出模型上下文限制，请缩短输入或减少历史内容。」, advice no control could follow: the canvas, not the history, filled it), a canvas context over 120,000 bytes with 400 `invalid_input` (「输入无效，请检查后重试。」). Production, read-only: on 2026-10-21 05:59Z and 06:00Z a canvas of nine nodes (67 KB of input values, 50 KB of requirements and criteria, 15 KB of briefs) was refused twice in 20 ms, and its owner stopped asking; its plan at 03:48Z had been 108,904 bytes, under the default model's 114,432. Now the refusal says how many bytes of canvas context the same request may carry (`error.details.contextRoom`, `planning.go` and `runs.go`): with space for the personal settings its size left out, which a shorter request carries again; on the operator's planner model where only its input bound kept the plan off it (its daily ceilings, now checked first, would let it run, and the workspace may use it: a DeepSeek one only where its allowlist names it, `plannerModelTakes`); 0 when the request, the files it names or the selected knowledge leave none. The page then sends a shorter view of the same canvas (`fitPlanningContext`, `canvasPlanning.ts`), up to three times, each shorter: every node, field and connection is still there and only long texts are cut, where the cut is shorter than the text, each saying how many more characters the canvas keeps (「…〔另有 N 字未显示，保持原样〕」), the conversation first, then the nodes the request is not about, and the nodes it is about (named in it, selected, or failed last time) last; a shared requirement keeps what the most generous of its nodes keep. A hosted canvas's context past the plan's own bounds is never sent whole; the desktop gateway, with bounds of its own, still gets the whole canvas. A plan made from a shortened view leaves what it showed only in part as it is (`applyCanvasPlan`: a persona, an input, a form value, a media prompt, a node's constraints, its own or a shared requirement's, and criteria), and writes text copied from a shortened one nowhere, titles, field labels (the input a connection adds included), help and placeholders too, each said among the adjustments with what to do (edit it in the node, or name the node), or, for a node the plan adds, that it was added without it; a plan made from the whole canvas writes such words as given. Which fields the view showed only in part go into the planning recovery journal with its request (`plannerRecovery.ts`), whatever their number, and the plan comes back saying what its request showed, those fields or the whole canvas, so a resumed run, or one another tab started, is applied as the request it was made from: a tab whose own view is shortened applies another tab's plan of the whole canvas as one, and a set the journal or the plan cannot read stops the plan (a malformed one is refused before its run is admitted) rather than counting as the whole canvas; the journal keeps a shortened request's entry as version 2, which a page of an earlier release, still open after a release, refuses rather than apply its plan as one of the whole canvas. The reply says the canvas was read in part. Only when not even an outline of each node fits does the assistant say so, with what to do: the canvas is too large (「画布太大，助手这次读不完…」), or the files, the knowledge and the request leave it no room (「这次要读的内容太多，助手放不下…」). Tests: planning_context_test.go (the room, exact to its 256-byte margin, given before any run; the plan's bounds, for the context and the whole prompt; no room left; the personal settings; the operator's planner model, and none of its room once its daily calls are used up or where the workspace may not use it; a run posted straight to the planner session keeps the plain refusal), saas-planning-fit.test.ts, four journal cases in saas-planning-recovery.test.ts (a resumed run, its entry version 2; a set past the old bounds, and a malformed one refused before admission; journals whose set or version cannot be read; another tab's plan of the whole canvas) and two canvas cases in canvas-planning-integration.test.tsx; each new case fails on the code without its part of the fix (24 mutants, all killed).
- Say what to do when a run fails, and say it in words on a node that failed in a run of the canvas (owner 2026-10-21: 「现在的版本，总会碰到：运行超时，请缩小任务范围后重试。报错时明确用户该做什么」). A timed-out run read 「运行超时，请缩小任务范围后重试。」, but from 2026-10-16 to 10-19 20 of production's 22 timeouts were a Claude Opus 5.5 call that had not written a word when its time limit came, some of their requests a dozen characters long, and 6 of the 12 nodes run again finished, in 64–255 s; 10 of the 22 were never run again. It now reads 「运行超时：模型迟迟没有给出结果。先重新运行，常常就能好；再超时就换个模型，或让助手调整画布。」 (one line of a wide node's failure note). The other copies of a run's failure that sent the reader to "restore the run state", "check the runtime configuration" or "make the task smaller" (a refused or unexpected answer of the execution service, a lost stream, output that could not be recorded or read, a model failure, output over the cap, the hidden thinking included, a service restart or another interruption) now say what happened and to run it again, choose another model, let the assistant split the delivery, reload the page or contact an administrator; a rate limit and an unavailable provider also offer another model. No such copy names "this node", nor does a delivery-format refusal's any more: the same words read under a team member's turn, whose model may be its own, and on every node of a collaboration that one turn ended. A node team's own limits (`team_timeout`, `team_turn_budget_exhausted`, `review_rounds_exhausted`) name the team setting to raise and its bound (「节点超时（秒）」 up to 1800, 「最多模型调用次数」 up to 64, 「最多轮数」 up to 8), and a reviewer's unreadable verdict, a member's unavailable tool, a turn or usage record that could not be saved and a delivery that could not be stored get words too; all showed as their code. A planning run that failed says so as the canvas assistant's, that the canvas has not changed and to send the request again (in parts when it was too large or out of time), rather than naming a node's model; a live interruption and a plan another page stopped carry no code, and read 「请求失败，请重试。」 there, as an interruption did on a node's own Send: each now says what happened. A node's own Send whose run was admitted but whose events could not be opened read 「无法连接运行事件，请刷新后恢复。」, and now reads as a lost connection: reload to see whether the run finished, else run it again. 「让助手调整画布」 sends what happened (what a copy says happened, a run's, the service's or an edit's, recorded as its code or as the copy a node's own Send recorded; the provider's or the render worker's own words whole), not the note's advice, and asks for another model or the work split for a timeout instead of the delivery narrowed; the planner is told what happened too, and the planner of a canvas on this device is told to give a node that ran out of time another model where it can set one, and else, as before, to split the work or narrow the delivery (in the bytes the old rule took: saas-planning-budget holds its context under 16,000). A cloud canvas run's node records its run's code, which the opened node's failure note (「上次运行失败：run_timeout」), the timeline, the badge, the assistant's reply and its fix request, the run history and the run details under a node's turn showed as it was: each now reads the code's copy, the run's or the service's, and keeps any other detail verbatim. A node's own Send that failed recorded only 「运行失败」, in Chinese whatever the page's language, so its failure note read 「上次运行失败：运行失败」 while only its conversation said why (Chrome on a local stack, a timed-out Send): it now records the words of the failed phase that ended its run, the copy above, which the note, the timeline, the badge and the assistant read (a failed phase another frame follows is the agent's own progress, on a canvas on this device).
- Keep THE LONG CHORD's Act I from going to digital silence under the census beat that has no music (SC08, 4:41–4:57; found 2026-10-21 by the session making the case's tutorial, and passed on by the owner). For 10.4 s and 1.4 s the act's sound was zero: every clip's own sound is muted, and reel 2 gives that beat no cue (the null fork, "No one hears a thing"), so the census cue faded out and started again with nothing between. The act's own timeline, which the operator writes, now carries the same cue as a quiet bed there, about 23 dB under that cue as heard in the scene, wired into the act's edit, so the beat is quiet rather than dead. Only the act's edit ran again (the case's 34th graph run); the reels and their editor agents are untouched, the picture is the same 8,241 frames, and elsewhere the sound is the act's as before, re-encoded. The case's record, stored canvas and media manifest are published again, and the new film (its web copy and the file as delivered) is staged beside the old one.
- Measure a canvas node's duration (`awwo_graph_node_duration_seconds`) on the database's clock, whatever the API's clock says against the database's (found 2026-10-21 with the fix below). The duration was the API's clock (`time.Since`) less the node's run's `created_at`, which the database stamps, so every duration was off by the difference between the two clocks: short by it while the database's clock ran ahead, which made a node settled within the difference of its run's creation negative (-0.65 s for a node of 3 ms, the database about 0.65 s ahead), and long by it while it ran behind. It is now the database's clock when the node settles less `created_at`, both read in one statement (`setGraphNode` in `graph_runs.go`), and never below 0. Test (`graph_runs_test.go`): a node's one observation, when it settles, lies between two readings of the database's clock just before and just after, less its run's `created_at`, which the test sets a second before the run's last update (the duration starts at the run's creation). Like the test below, it fails only where the two clocks differ (from Windows against WSL it failed 300 of 300 runs on the base code and passed 300 of 300 with this fix); on one clock, as in CI and production, the base code passes it too.
- Measure a run's wait in the queue on the database's clock, in the call ledger (`model_invocations.queue_ms`, which `GET /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/runs/{id}/invocations` and `GET /api/v1/admin/observability/invocations/{id}` report as `timingMs.queue`) and in `awwo_run_queue_duration_seconds`, whatever the API's clock says against the database's (found 2026-10-21 from a Windows test process against a PostgreSQL in WSL, whose clock ran from about a second behind Windows' to about a second ahead; production runs the API and its PostgreSQL on one host, so there the two read one clock). The wait was the API's clock (`time.Since`) less the run's `created_at`, which the database stamps, so every wait was off by the difference between the two clocks: short by it while the database's clock ran ahead, which made every wait shorter than the difference read 0 (a 13 ms wait read 0), and long by it while it ran behind. The wait now ends at the database's clock when the statement that claims the run has claimed it (`execute` in `runs.go`): a claim held up in its statement (by a lock, say) still counts as waiting, as it did, but the claim's commit, which the old reading came after, no longer does; it is still never below 0. Test (`invocation_ledger_test.go`): a run's `queue_ms`, and the metric's one observation, lie between its waits, on the database's clock, to the claim's start (its running event) plus a 50 ms hold a trigger puts in the claiming statement, and to its call's reservation. It fails only where the two clocks differ (from Windows against WSL it failed 298 of 300 runs on the base code, passing two while the clocks agreed, and passed 300 of 300 with this fix); on one clock, as in CI and production, the base code passes it too.
- Keep a file that lands in an opened node's inputs, its output form or its message box when a click comes before the render that shows it, including the click that opens another of the node's conversations (2026-10-21, found by the review of the fix that keeps uploads going in closed inputs; the canvas had the same exposure before it). A file's answer and the render that draws it come in separate tasks, and a click in between was handled against the node that render drew: a field added or removed in the structure editor (编辑字段结构 → 添加字段, 删除…), a requirement added to the output form (添加交付要求 → 添加到交付) or another conversation opened (新建 Session, 打开 对话 n) wrote back the field list, or the whole node, from before the file. The file was gone (in the inputs it waited again on its chip, 已上传，未加入; in the message box it stayed in view but not in the saved draft, so it went with a reload), and with a conversation opened so did a preview line or a draft the canvas wrote meanwhile. A file the canvas refused in one input field no longer comes in with another field's write made before the next render either: it waits for its 加入, as when it lands alone. Each change of the fields (a value, a name, a type, 必填) now touches only its own field of the list as the node holds it when the change comes, and a field added or removed only that field; a conversation opens from the node as the document holds it, the box's draft kept, as the box last changed it, with the conversation the box showed, and a draft the box did not change left as the document holds it; the canvas's checks still apply (no switch while the node streams). Not changed: 发布输出 publishes the form as the reader saw it. `ContractFields.tsx`, `NodeDeliverables.tsx`, `SessionTile.tsx`, `CanvasSurface.tsx` (a comment); tests in canvas-composer-attachments, canvas-contract-fields and canvas-online-sync-surface.
- Keep an opened node's delivery drawer open, at the delivery's share of the node's width, while the reader edits the node's inputs (2026-10-21, the owner's choice): in a node that had delivered, whose drawer had opened by itself beside the conversation, the first keystroke in a value of its opened inputs (输入) took the delivery back, as an edit of the inputs does (`invalidateOutputs`: it changes what a run is asked), and the drawer closed with it, so the inputs, which sit in the conversation's column, widened under the keystroke from about half the node to all of it (in Chrome at 1600 × 1000 from 517.5 to 1078 px, the field from 431.5 to 992 px). As an edit of the drawer's own form already does (the drawer's entries below), an edit of the inputs, their values or their structure, now starts or carries the edit in progress that keeps the drawer (`SessionTile`, updateFields beside updateDeliverables): the drawer stays as the reader has it, at the delivery's share (52 %; a node with a webpage requirement keeps a page's 62 % anyway), showing the conversation's earlier delivery as history (历史交付 · 未传递给下游) until the node delivers again, the inputs and the field being typed in keep their width and the focus, and nothing about the drawer is recorded. The edit ends as that one does (work starting, the node closing, a new conversation, the output form changed under it, a delivery back, which a run or a publication brings with its own share), and, as it is keyed by the output form, which an edit of the inputs leaves as it is, the share also holds through an undo of the inputs and through a keystroke in them the canvas refuses. A case recording (which an edit of the inputs leaves) holds nothing, a node with no delivery to take back starts no edit (there an undo still closes a drawer the reader opened by hand, as before), and a drawer that is not shown when the edit starts (closed by the reader, closed behind Configure, which a canvas on this device lays over the node at its own width, or beside a failed run's partial delivery) keeps no share; a delivery that something else takes back still closes the drawer that opened for it. As for the drawer's own form (the entry below), the canvas keeps the room of the drawer the tile holds in a node with no frame of its own (a stage too short for one, or in the hosted app one too narrow beside the Configure panel), where the node would narrow to a conversation's width once the delivery is taken back and the drawer held open would lie over the whole node, the inputs being typed in included, and it remembers the reader's close of that drawer. Tests in canvas-open-node-content: the drawer, its share, the field and its focus through two keystrokes; the share through an undo of the inputs and a refused keystroke; a run ending the edit and its delivery shown by the drawer's own rule; an edit begun in the inputs carried into the drawer's form and its publication, and one of the drawer's form that a refused keystroke left holding carried into the inputs; nothing held for a case recording, a refused edit or a node with no delivery (an undo closing a drawer opened by hand); no share for a drawer the reader closed or one closed behind Configure; a page's drawer held at a page's share, and at a conversation's once its html field is no page's; and in canvas-surface-fit, a node with no frame of its own keeping its 840 px, its drawer beside the inputs and the focus in the field through an edit of them, and the reader's close of that drawer remembered; and in canvas-composer-attachments, the drawer held through an input's file and an output's landing at the same moment, either first (the edit the drawer's form set first keeps its form). In Chrome on a local stack (the API and the hosted app, e514c9b3 with this change, a private PostgreSQL, no workers) at 1600 × 1000: through the edit the drawer kept its 560.5 px (52 % of the 1108 px node), the inputs their 517.5 px, the field its 431.5 px and the focus, and the server's document held lastOutput null and no deliverablesOpen; on e514c9b3 the first keystroke closed the drawer and widened the inputs to 1078 px. At 1600 × 470, where the node has no frame of its own (drawn at 46 %), it kept its 840 px and the drawer its place beside the inputs; on e514c9b3 the keystroke closed the drawer and narrowed the node to 560 px.
- Remember the reader's close of a delivery drawer an edit of its output form kept open, and keep that drawer's room in an opened node that has no frame of its own (2026-10-21, the two limits the drawer's entries below left, and a third). The tile now tells the canvas which drawer it holds open where the drawer's own rule (`deliverablesShown`) closes it (`onHoldDeliverables` in `SessionTile.tsx`, kept by `CanvasSurface.tsx` while the page is open and never saved), and the canvas counts that drawer as shown for a close. Its ✕ was compared with the rule, which already said closed (no delivery, nothing recorded), so nothing was recorded and the next delivery opened the drawer by itself again; the close is now recorded as the close of a drawer that opened by itself is (`deliverablesOpen: false`), so a later run's delivery leaves the drawer closed. A node opened without a frame of its own (a stage too short for one, 1600 × 280 say, or in the hosted app a stage of about 900 to 960 px with Configure open) is as wide as an opened node's minimum, 520 px, and the drawer's 320 px (`presentationNodes` in `nodePresentation.ts`, for the node drawn and for the camera `openPlacement` fits); once the edit had taken the delivery back, it narrowed from 840 to 520 px, the drawer the edit kept open lay over the conversation (the workbench under 740 px) and the camera refitted the node (beside Configure at 940 × 900, from 75 % to about 101 %). It now keeps the drawer's room, the drawer beside the conversation and the camera where it was while the drawer is held: until its close reaches the canvas (the node then narrows and is fitted again, as when a drawer that opened by itself is closed; a close the canvas refuses, while a paused recovery holds it, narrows it without a refit) or the drawer's rule shows it again (a delivery back beside the conversation). Where the rule hides a drawer even with a delivery (a narrow stage, a frame too narrow for both), the drawer is still held after the publication, so its close is remembered there too. A toggle during a run stays the tile's own, as before: it records nothing and changes nothing the canvas counts, so a drawer opened then is not counted, and closing the held drawer then leaves the node's size as it was, its drawer closed, as for a recorded drawer, until an open of it outside a run (asked of the drawer's rule alone, so it is recorded and the drawer shows, from 查看交付物 too) or a delivery back beside the conversation. And a keystroke the canvas refuses in the middle of the edit (`patchDoc` refusing it while a run of another lane reaches a node it feeds, say) no longer ends the edit, so the drawer keeps the delivery's share of the node, 52 %, instead of a conversation's 38 % for the rest of the edit: the edit goes on while the node is still the one that keystroke was made on (a refused first keystroke starts none, and one followed by anything else that changes the node ends it, as before). Tests in canvas-surface-fit (on a 1600 × 280 stage the node keeps 840 px, its camera, its drawer and the field's focus through the edit, and closing the drawer is recorded and narrows it; beside Configure on a hosted 940 px stage the node keeps its width and camera; a close that is recorded leaves the drawer closed after a run of the node delivers; a close during a run keeps the node's 840 px and records nothing, and an open after it is recorded and shows the drawer), canvas-open-node-content (the tile reports the drawer it holds and hands the canvas its close while still held; nothing is held for a drawer the rule shows, a recorded one closed during the edit or one opened in a run; the hold ends at the publication, with the tile and once the drawer is recorded open (as 查看交付物 records it), and lasts through a close during a run and through a publication where the rule hides the drawer; the share holds through refused keystrokes and ends with an undo after one) and canvas-node-presentation. In the app's Chromium browser pane, on the local canvas with the hosted look at a 1616 × 280 stage: before the change one keystroke in the form narrowed the node from 840 to 520 px and laid the drawer over 97 % of the conversation, and its ✕ recorded nothing; with it the node kept 840 px, the drawer 414.9 px beside a 383 px conversation and the field the focus, the ✕ recorded `deliverablesOpen: false`, and a later delivery opened the node with its drawer closed.
- Keep an opened node's message box and the row under it (the model, 用户须知) whole beside its inputs left open across a run (2026-10-21, in Chrome on built apps; built on the fix that keeps it whole below a failed run's note above replies). Inputs opened before a run or a message stop taking the column once it starts, and inputs opened while one is going never take it, but they kept their floor (min(160 px, 35%)) beside the conversation's (min(160 px, 45%)). With the heading and the floors of the task card and a failure note, those floors are more than any short chat column holds (without the note, more than one under some 372 px holds), so the composer ran past the node with no draft at all, in every look. Measured in the developer view below a failure note, with no draft or a short one: by 61 to 69 px at 1280 × 720 and 1280 × 800, 62 to 67 px at 1366 × 657, and 62 to 69 px in a 294 px column (with no draft the floors alone run 69.2, 67 and 77.2 px over; where the page had scrolled the node's body, by up to 15 px with no draft, as in the 294 px column in every look, and 26 px with one long line, the composer was cut by that much less). After a message, without a failure note: by 13 to 23 px with no draft, and up to 34 px with one long line. Taller columns were cut too: by 17.8 px at 1440 × 740 and 31.6 to 35.1 px at 1366 × 768, and where the composer is taller than the conversation's floor (160 px: the default look's composer is 163.5 px, the custom terminal look's 160.5) by 3.5 or 0.5 px even at 1440 × 900 and 1536 × 864. With ten lines, the caret scrolled the node's body by up to 72 px, its heading out of view. Now the inputs give way. Where the column cannot hold every part at its floor (the heading's min-height, a failure note's, the task card's, the conversation's and the drawer's own), the drawer's floor drops, down to its own padding, and its fields scroll in what is left. The conversation, whose replies are what the run brought, keeps its floor and never cuts its composer: its floor is its flex basis, it never shrinks, and its minimum is its content, in which the replies count for nothing. A column that holds every floor keeps the drawer's floor, so every column whose composer fitted lays out as before. `apps/web/src/canvas/awwo-node.css`; a test in `canvas-open-node-content`. Checked in Chrome on the built app with and without the change, on a local stack with stand-in workers, over 308 configurations of the state: seven looks, light and dark, four drafts, after a failed run or a message, 294 to 768 px columns at eight window sizes from 1280 × 720 and 1366 × 657 to 1920 × 1080, and with a rework note, a file in the composer, a node without inputs or the task card expanded. The composer is whole in 269 of them, against 29 on the base build, and those 29 are laid out the same, every part to 0.05 px. 48 states the rules leave alone (the inputs opened after a run or beside replies, no inputs open) are laid out the same as well. Rebased on production's code, 82 of these configurations were measured again on production's build and this change's, and lay out as they did on the first two, but for one ten-line column on production's build that the caret scrolled 1 px further. Still cut, by less than before, all with a ten-line draft unless noted: below a failure note in the 334 px column of 1280 × 720 and 1280 × 800, by 1.5 to 5.5 px of the composer's bottom padding (the row under the box inside); in a 294 px column below a failure note, by 40 to 45.5 px (from 48.9 to 54.4, where the base build scrolled the node's body by 69 to 72 px, and now nothing scrolls); with the task card expanded, by 12 to 13.5 px at 1280 × 720 and 1 to 2.5 px at 1366 × 657; with a file in the composer, by 40 to 41.5 px and 29 to 30.5 px; and beside a rework note, which keeps the conversation's own rules, by 35.7 to 37.2 px and 30.75 to 32.25 px, and in a 456 px column below a failure note, with any draft, by 8 to 13.5 px of padding (from 39.6 to 45.1).
- Move the focus to the side panel's message box, not to a box a task card above it holds, when an opened node hands itself to the canvas assistant with 让助手修改 (or 让助手调整, when the assistant cannot take the fix now) (2026-10-21, named in the review of the first-plan fix below). Its request goes into the composer as a draft, but the focus went to the panel's first text box, and a task that asks the reader something draws its answer box above the composer: what the reader then typed went to that task. Test in canvas-assistant-routing: 让助手修改 on an opened node with such a task in the conversation.
- Move the focus to the canvas assistant's message box when a reconcile pressed in this page (核对上次提交) finds its task (2026-10-21, named in the review of the first-plan fix below). The reconcile's box goes with its button, and the focus with them; it moved only where the task took the conversation from the welcome to the side panel, so with the assistant closed, where the welcome keeps the conversation, or in the side panel, it stayed on the page. The managed-execution host now lists every task confirmed on the canvas, once per submission with its first answer, and says which answered a reconcile pressed in its page (`here`: that reconcile's own answer, or another page's announcement of the same task while it waits). The canvas links each listed task's request and moves the focus once for each new entry that is `here`, to the box of whichever holds the conversation, the welcome or the side panel, unless the reader has put it on another control meanwhile. It held one confirmation at a time before, so one that another came after before the page drew it was never linked; a later answer to a listed task changes nothing, so it never takes the focus back. A start another page of the canvas confirms or announces (each page announces every task it starts) moves the focus only where its task takes the conversation out of the welcome, as before, and only for a request in this conversation; a confirmation the host already listed when the canvas opened moves none. Tests in canvas-assistant-routing: a reconcile pressed in a closed welcome and in the side panel, each with a task that asks something; a start another page confirms for a request given up here, in a closed welcome; a confirmation listed before the canvas opened, also when another joins the list; a task another page announces with no request here, with the assistant closed and open over the welcome (nothing focused); a reconcile's task and another's listed before one draw (both linked, the focus moved); and another task joining the list after a reconcile moved the focus (not moved again). In saas-assistant-execution: a reconcile's confirmation is `here`, as is another page's announcement while it waits; a later answer to the same submission (its own request, another announcement, in the same draw or after) changes nothing; two confirmations before one draw are both listed, whether the reconcile's own request then finds its task or fails; and an announcement after a reconcile that ended unconfirmed is not `here`.
- Move the focus to the welcome's message box when the canvas assistant's own undo or plan empties the canvas and takes the conversation back from the side panel to the welcome (2026-10-21, named in the review of the first-plan fix below). Undoing the first plan with 撤销本次更改, or a plan that removed every node, empties the canvas, and the side panel went with its last node, and with it the control that had the focus (its undo button, or its box while the plan was made); 画布助手, which has the focus where the reader closed the panel while the plan was made, went with the last node too. The welcome's box came up idle, so the focus stayed on the page and a keyboard user had to find the box again. It now goes to the welcome's box, unless the reader has put it on another control meanwhile. A canvas emptied by hand (a deletion, Ctrl+Z) leaves it on the page, where the canvas's keys work: in the box, Ctrl+Z would undo the box's typing, not the deletion. The way back, such a plan undone from the welcome, moves it to the side panel's box, or to 画布助手 where the reader had closed the panel a task kept open on the emptied canvas. A reader who closes the side panel is still handed to 画布助手, and closing it no longer names the welcome's first text box, which it could not reach: the panel is drawn only with nodes or tasks, and 画布助手 stays with either. Tests in canvas-assistant-routing: the first plan undone, with one of the canvas's earlier tasks asking the reader something above the welcome's composer; a plan that removes every node, with two frames passing before the welcome is drawn, and with the panel closed while it was made; a focus the reader moved to 查找 Agent meanwhile, left there; that plan undone from the welcome, with the assistant open and closed; the canvas emptied by hand, after which Ctrl+Z on the focused element brings the node back; and the side panel of an empty canvas with a task, closed by the reader (the focus on 画布助手).
- Keep the keyboard's focus and every upload of an opened node's inputs when the inputs close (2026-10-20, seen in Chrome with a Playwright probe; the rework note beside the opened inputs now says to close them, 关闭输入后查看). Closed from their own button (收起输入) while it had the focus, the inputs unmounted it and the focus fell to the page's body: it now goes to the control that opens them again (输入 in the chat heading, or in the sessions list), and where there is none to the message box, else the first control below them that takes it (the opened inputs hide the empty conversation's starter prompts, which take no focus then), else the node's own menu button (更多节点操作), without scrolling anything; a click that focused nothing (as in Safari) leaves the focus where it was. Closed any way (that button, the 输入 toggle, or the template guide, which takes their place), the inputs unmounted their fields, whose upload boxes end every upload they hold when they unmount (`ComposerAttachments.tsx`), so a file still uploading into one of them never landed, and nothing said so. Closed inputs whose fields still hold an upload (going, uploaded and waiting to be added, or failed and not dismissed) now keep those fields mounted, hidden under another class (`awwo-input-held`, so none of the drawer's layout rules apply: in Chrome every box of the opened node but the toggle's icon is where it is with nothing held), until the last one is a file in its field or dismissed: the upload goes on; opened again, the inputs show it as it goes. The toggle keeps its name and is described by every state the inputs hold (输入：文件仍在上传, 有文件等待加入, 有文件上传失败, together where several are), its icon the one that most needs the reader (a failure in the error colour, then a clock, then a turning icon), and a live region in the chat heading tells a screen reader of a failure or of a file waiting to be added, also while another file still uploads. A run asking for its inputs while their fields showed their structure mounted the fields anew too, and the hold needs the fields to change mode in place (the template guide's 编辑, or the toggle opening held inputs on their values): the node now keeps the fields' mode (`editingSchema` on `ContractFields`). In the inputs (`holdUploads`), a finished upload keeps its chip until its file is in the field, so a file the canvas refuses as it lands (an edit that would clear a result a node downstream is running on) is no longer lost: it waits on its chip for its 加入 (a later edit of the field, or taking another file out of it, does not add it). A file that landed while its input was locked (a reply streaming, a run of the node, the canvas's lock) was refused by the input and dropped too; added on its own once the lock ends, it would change the inputs behind the reader's back, which clears what a run of them made. Such a file, and one whose upload a lock came and went during, now waits on its chip (已上传，可编辑时加入, then 已上传，未加入) with a 加入 that adds it once the input can be edited, and says so (adding it changes the inputs: this node and the ones after it need a new run); pressed from the keyboard, it hands its focus to the added file. The node's own runs are not held back while an input uploads: a run then goes without the file, which waits for its 加入. Two files that land at the same moment, in two fields or in one, no longer drop one another: every write of a box is built from the value it last drew plus the files its writes added since (in the message box and the canvas assistant too, where the first was dropped), and a file its owner refused (a node's locked outputs, a view-only message box) or an undo took out is not written again by a later edit. An input's file and an output's (交付物 → 编辑输出表单) landing at the same moment, as closed inputs go on uploading, do not drop one another either, nor bring back a result published by hand that the input's change made stale: the inputs and the deliverables each change only their own part of the node, which the canvas applies to the node as its document holds it (`onPatchNode`), not to the copy the card last drew. Not changed: closing the node itself, or its card leaving the view, still ends an upload in its inputs or its message box and drops a file waiting for its 加入. `ComposerAttachments.tsx`, `composer-attachments.css`, `ContractFields.tsx`, `SessionTile.tsx`, `CanvasSurface.tsx`, `i18n.tsx`, `awwo-node.css`; tests in canvas-composer-attachments.
- Give an opened node's message box the keyboard's focus back when the reply sent from it ends, and when another lock of the box that began while the composer had the focus ends (seen 2026-10-20 in Chrome 155 on a built app: after a message sent from the box the focus stayed on the page through the reply and after it, so a keyboard user had to find the box again to answer). The box is disabled while its node works (任务执行中，结束后可继续对话。), Chrome drops a disabled control's focus to the page, and nothing brought it back, as the canvas assistant's box does for itself. The box now takes it back in the commit that enables it again, if the composer had the focus when it locked and the focus is lost by then; a message sent with the button puts the focus in the box first, so the button, which an empty box disables, has none to lose (Safari gives a pressed button none at all). A reader who turned elsewhere meanwhile keeps the focus where they put it: a press or a focus outside the composer (in the reply, to copy from it; on the canvas; on another node), Escape, Tab or a key that moves the canvas's camera (Ctrl+1 to a waypoint, Ctrl+0; AltGr's digits too, which the canvas reads so), a wheel outside the node, a click into a preview's frame, or a selection on the page; typing, editing chords and the browser's own keys do not count. On a phone or a tablet, where the box's keyboard would come up over the reply, nothing moves the focus. A lock that hides the focused control of the composer itself (用户须知, while the canvas locks the box) takes the hand-back with it, and the canvas assistant moving a lost focus to its own controls first wins. The canvas does not scroll to show the box, and nothing more can be sent from it until the reply is in.
- Keep an opened node's message box and the row under it (the model, 用户须知) whole in a short chat column below a failed run's note above replies (2026-10-20, in Chrome on built apps at 1366 × 657 and 1280 × 720; built on the fix that keeps it whole beside the opened inputs or a rework note). There the conversation keeps a lower floor than above replies alone (150 px in a 334 px column, 1280 × 720 beside the assistant), which a ten-line composer (176 to 181.5 px) outgrew: the panel was held at its floor while the failure note and the task card shrank, so with ten lines the model and 用户须知 ended 10.75 to 18.25 px below the node at 1366 × 657 and 15.7 to 23.2 px at 1280 × 720, in every look (with one long line, 8.7 to 10.7 px in the custom terminal look at 1280 × 720), and focusing the model picker from the keyboard scrolled the panel by 16 to 19 px and still left it 0.2 px cut (the default look at 1280 × 720). A column whose composer fits the floor lays out as before. Not beside the opened inputs, beside a rework note or in a media node, which lay out as before. `apps/web/src/canvas/awwo-node.css`; a test in `canvas-open-node-content`. Checked in Chrome on the built app with and without the change (the base build is production's), on a local stack with stand-in workers: 112 configurations (seven looks, light and dark, four drafts, both sizes): the composer whole in 112, against 78 on the base build, and every one whole there laid out the same (to 0.05 px); a failing node without inputs 24 → 32 of 32, an expanded task card 24 → 32 of 32, a composer holding a file 8 → 24 of 32; of 78 that fit, every element's computed style and box as before but the declared properties; 88 states the rule does not match (no conversation, replies without a failure note, a rework note beside replies) identical; a 428 px column (1440 × 740), a 456 px one (1366 × 768) and 1920 × 1080 laid out as before. A column of 440 px or more is not short, and beside its opened inputs the conversation keeps its content's height, so an open note counted its findings in full: at 1366 × 768 (a 456 px column) the composer was cut in every look, by up to 97 px with an empty draft (its bottom edge 130 px below the node's body) and 61 px with ten lines, the row under the box (the model, 用户须知) by up to 85 px, and typing scrolled the whole column, heading and inputs out of view; likewise at 1366 × 800 (up to 97 px), 1536 × 864 (44 px) and 1440 × 900 (4.3 to 8 px in five looks of seven), and with replies, short findings, an expanded task card or a file in the composer. The note measures whether its drawn findings push the composer's bottom edge (its bottom padding included) below the column, before the page is painted (`useCutsComposer.ts`; the column's own overflow is no measure, its panel reaching 57 px below its composer there): after every render while they show, the node's size coming through one, and, while they wait, on a change of size in the column or any of its parts, a font that finishes loading, or a change of what they draw (their text, the language, the opened node's look), so they show again once the column has room (a taller window). Checked in Chrome on built apps (production's bytes, the short column's fix on them, and this change; a local stack with stand-in workers): 808 configurations: in columns that are not short (362: seven looks, light and dark, an empty and a ten-line draft, six window sizes from 1366 × 768 to 1920 × 1080, a closed and an open note beside the inputs, with replies, short findings, an expanded task card or a file) the composer is whole in 356 against 250 on production’s build, and beside the opened inputs an open note’s composer in every one (at 1366 × 768 none on production’s build, at 1440 × 900 4 of 14); every configuration whole on production’s build is laid out the same, to 0.05 px; the short column’s own sets (446) lay out exactly as on its fix; and no frame was painted with the findings beside the inputs where they do not fit, or with the composer cut, through a press of 查看, a window made smaller and larger, and the inputs closed and opened.
- Keep the width an opened node gives its delivery drawer while an edit of the drawer's form has taken its delivery back (2026-10-20, found with the fix below: once the drawer stayed open, the first keystroke narrowed it from a delivery's share of the node, 52 %, to a conversation's, 38 %, in Chrome at 1600 × 1000 from 561 to 410 px, and publishing widened it again). The drawer's share follows what the node mostly shows (`openContentOf` in `apps/web/src/canvas/nodePresentation.ts`), which with the delivery taken back is its conversation. A delivery an edit of the form took back now keeps its share while the edit lasts, as the canvas keeps the delivery's room in the node's frame: until the form is published (the new delivery has its own share), the node closes or starts work (a run, a message), or the form or the conversation changes under the edit (an undo, a new conversation, an edit the canvas refused). An edit of the node's inputs, and the same form read back from elsewhere (another tab's save, a setup adopted from the server), leave it. A node with no delivery to take back, a case recording (which an edit leaves), a node the edit makes a page (a webpage requirement) and every run take their own share as before, and a node with no frame of its own narrows as the entry below says. Editing the form takes the node's delivery back until it is published again, as the form says (「修改字段会使已有产出失效，填写完成后重新发布」, `invalidateOutputs`; a case recording stays), and a drawer that opened by itself for that delivery (`deliverablesShown`, since 2026-10-15) closed with it. An edit made in the drawer (a value, a field, 添加到交付) now leaves it open as the reader has it, its editor and the focused field with it, and records nothing about the drawer: after the publication it opens by itself for the new delivery wherever the drawer's own rule shows it, and a later run or a reload finds it as before. It stays open as the reader has it until they close it (which is not remembered: a later delivery opens it again), also through an undo, a new conversation, a run, a stage that narrows and a publication on a stage where the rule would hide it, and a delivery that something else takes back (a run's start, an output upstream replaced) still closes the drawer that opened for it. Where the opened node has no frame of its own (a stage too short for one, or in the hosted app one too narrow beside the Configure panel), the node narrows to a conversation's width once the delivery is taken back and the camera refits it, so the drawer lies over the conversation until a delivery is back or the reader closes it. - Count a model call that has just completed in the admin observability summary's default day (`GET /api/v1/admin/observability/summary` without `from` and `to`), whatever the API's clock says against the database's (found 2026-10-20 with the fix below; production runs the API and its PostgreSQL on one host, so there the two read one clock). The day ended at the API's clock (`time.Now()`) and the summary's `asOf` was lowered to it, while the database stamps a call's end (`completed_at`), so while the database's clock ran ahead, calls that had just completed were missing from it. The default day now ends at the database's clock, read in the summary's own transaction (`adminUsageSummary` in `usage_api.go`), and `freshness.asOf` is that reading, in UTC; a summary asked for with `from` and `to` is unchanged. Test (`usage_api_test.go`): a call stamped as the ledger stamps one, just before the summary is asked for, is counted, and `asOf` is in UTC and lies between two readings of the database's clock.
- Count a model call that has just completed in the usage metrics' 24-hour and 30-day windows (`awwo_usage_window_*`), whatever the API's clock says against the database's (found 2026-10-20: the snapshot test failed from a Windows test process against a PostgreSQL in WSL, whose clock ran up to about a second either side of Windows'; production runs the API and its PostgreSQL on one host, so there the two read one clock). The windows ended at the API's clock (`time.Now()`) while the database stamps a call's end (`completed_at`), so while the database's clock ran ahead, a call that had just completed was left out until the next snapshot a minute later. They now end at the database's clock, read in the snapshot's own transaction (`readUsageWindowSnapshot` in `usage_aggregation.go`), and `awwo_usage_snapshot_timestamp_seconds` reports that cutoff; the snapshot's age (`awwo_usage_snapshot_age_seconds`) is measured on the API's own clock from when it read the cutoff, so it is never negative and does not move with the database's clock. Tests (`usage_aggregation_test.go`): the cutoff lies between two readings of the database's clock, and the age between 0 and the time the test has taken since it began reading.
- Count every node a canvas run still has to make in the canvas assistant's Next card, its pictures, 3D models and assembled pages with its Agents, and run them all from it (seen 2026-10-20 on the live site in English: a draft copy of the PALLWARD case opened with 71 nodes, and the card said "3 node(s) have no result yet." with "Run the 3 node(s) left (at least 3 call(s))", where 48 had none). A copy carries its Agents' text deliveries only, and the card, written before canvas runs began to generate image, video and 3D nodes (2026-10-12), left those out, as it did assemble nodes and edits: PALLWARD's 10 concept pictures and 33 3D models, its Assembly and its First pass page. So it offered to run the three Agents alone, which spends their calls on an asset manifest and two fix passes without the files they read, and it hid that a real run makes every picture and model again. The flagships' copies, whose assemblies make their files on the first run, were miscounted the same way: Umber, Backprop and Errand read as done, Roost as 4 nodes left of 6. The card now counts every node without a result as the results view does (a blank output and a failed run's capture are none): "48 node(s) have no result yet, 43 of them media node(s): a run generates their files, one generation each, from today’s allowance or the plan’s credits.", and offers "Run the 48 node(s) left (43 generation(s), at least 4 call(s))", which runs those 48 and the review they feed. Every run it offers or starts from the conversation, failed nodes run again included, quotes its generations (one for each media node) and its calls over what that run executes, and "continue" with nothing it can start says why (the card's advice, or that what is left cannot run on this device) instead of that every node has a result. A failed picture, 3D model, assembly or edit is explained like a failed Agent, and one the workspace may not make today (its or its plan's generations or edits used up, the service's free calls or the plan's credits, or a paid plan needed: `media_quota_exceeded`, `model3d_quota_exceeded`, `model3d_motion_plan_required`, `free_capacity_exceeded`, `credits_exhausted`, `edit_allowance` and the like) is said in the refusal's own words, which say what lifts it, with the plans first where a plan lifts it (not the service's own edit limit) and, for an Agent out of the plan's credits, the default model, rather than a rerun the same refusal would meet; it is not run again when the conversation says it failed. The card matches a refusal by its code, which a cloud run's node records as its detail, and by its copy in either language, which a node's own Send records, where it compared the run errors' copy alone, so a hosted canvas's quota and premium refusals reach those advices at all. An assembly's empty input, an edit without a timeline (its "Fill in" opens the edit's settings) and a media node's own fields are listed with the inputs a run needs, as the preflight refuses them. On a canvas on this device, which sends every session node to its Agent and generates nothing, the card counts those nodes as Agents, leaves out edits and assemblies that deliver a file (only a cloud run makes them), and offers no run that would reach one, which would fail there and clear what follows, nor of a node fed by one that has no result, and a whole run only while none of them has a result it would clear; its run of some nodes takes an out-of-scope form's fields as they are now, as a cloud run does, instead of blocking a node whose form never ran.
