- Stop the first open of a large hosted canvas, and a drag on it, from being counted as an update loop (React error #185, "Maximum update depth exceeded", seen once on 2026-10-19 on the first open and drag of a 142-node canvas, the operator's PALLWARD doubled, 5.2 MB). Every tile restores its history on open, in a synchronous render of its own, and reported its transcript's last line from an effect of that render; each report wrote the document and rendered the whole canvas again, and a run of them back to back went past React's limit of 50 nested updates (on an English open of a canvas last seen in Chinese, its 86 image and 3D nodes rewrote their lines). Now the tiles' lines are written together, in one write 120 ms after they pause and at least every 600 ms, and at once before a run, a node setup or a planning request; a tile renders again only when what it shows changed (its inputs, the wiring, its geometry and its callbacks keep their identity); the canvas's plan revision, a hash of the whole document, is worked out once per document instead of on every render and save; an opening canvas mounts its tiles, wires and displays once its stage has measured itself, so only the tiles its first camera shows read their histories; and the planning recovery is read once the document settles, not on every frame of a drag (until then nothing resumes what was read for the document before). Measured on a local stack (this tree's API and database with the canvas's real sessions and messages, an instrumented production build, headless Chrome at 6x CPU): with a drag while the histories load, React's nested-update count peaked at 3 (45–48 before; with every tile's line stale, 51 and the error before), in a 30 s drag too; tile renders went from about 14,500 to about 660, and the canvas settled in about 26 s instead of 156–201 s. The palette's search reads only loaded transcripts, so a phrase from a node the opening camera does not show is found once that node has been on screen. Tests in canvas-open-load, saas-canvas-preview-setup and saas-canvas-plan-recovery-settle.
- Keep a canvas run with many videos from references from exhausting the API's memory (incident 2026-10-20 03:14:18Z: a canvas run that started 37 of them at once took the API past its 512 MiB cap, the kernel killed it and systemd restarted it about 5 s later; the database shows that only that run's own 37 runs were interrupted, and none had been sent, so nothing was charged). A run uploads its references one file at a time, each read whole and copied into the upload's body (RunningHub takes files of up to 10 MB, X-tasy, Jimeng and Tripo up to 20 MB), and nothing bounded how many runs did so at once. At most four runs now upload references at a time across the API (`referenceUploadSlots` in `media_refs.go`), for every provider: a run waits for a slot as long as its context lets it (a stopped run stops waiting, reading and sending nothing), holds it while its references are read and sent (and while X-tasy prepares one, or Jimeng waits for its own command slots), and frees it when its uploads end. A run that waited until less than half of the media timeout is left is not sent: it ends as busy (`media_provider_busy`), unsent and so uncharged, and a canvas run tries it again, instead of sending a task it may not see through and being charged for it. The upload's body is sized once. Generations and their prices are unchanged. Tests (`media_refs_slots_test.go`): twelve runs of two references at once never have more than four uploads in flight and every run gets its ids in order; failing runs give their slots back; a run whose context ends while it waits sends nothing; the send-too-late rule.
- Let the small records an earlier release left in localStorage (planning conversations, run journals, recovery and presentation records, page repairs, reviewed drafts, the version) leave it once the canvas store holds them and their bytes have not changed for a day (2026-10-20). The store copied them in and left them in localStorage for good, because a page of that release might still read and rewrite them; a heavy planner user's copies (up to 60 messages per canvas) could fill localStorage, and a full localStorage still stops planning, whose recovery record is written there. A page of that release still working on such a record rewrites it, which takes the new bytes in and restarts the day; bytes such a page writes after a record left (it reads none and may save an empty planning conversation) are never taken over what the store holds. This works both when a canvas opens and in the idle sweep of the others; the store keeps every value.
- Show a media input that has no file yet as a note in the page's language, not as the Chinese instruction its agent reads (found 2026-10-20 in the review of the fix below that says what a node's inputs lack in the page's language; on every fresh copy of a media case, whose media nodes start empty: in English, Neon City's "Full-screen brand page" opened on its inputs showed, under "Using published output from “Opening shot”", the value 「Opening shot」这次没有生成出视频文件，没有可以引用的路径：…, and so did its other three media inputs, and PALLWARD's 33). When an image, video, 3D or audio node, or an edit, has made no file and feeds a text input (the soft wire of `isSoftMediaFeed` in `apps/web/src/canvas/ports.ts`), that input's value is the note that tells the agent to do without it (`mediaMissingText`, the text the API writes too). `prepareNodeConversation` (`apps/web/src/canvas/nodeConversation.ts`) now also marks such an input with what the node makes (`mediaMissing`), and the inputs form shows it with no value and, instead of "Using published output from …", says "No image file from “Hero” yet. If it makes none, this node goes on without it." (「“Hero”还没有生成出图像文件：若最终没有生成，本节点照常进行，不用它」); an HTML input, which refuses the note (and a list of files too), only says there is no file yet and leaves the reason to its alert. What the agent reads does not change: the input's value, the message and the API's prompt are as before, word for word. Tests in canvas-node-conversation, canvas-contract-fields, saas-soft-media and saas-production-copy (every media case's media-fed nodes, and Neon City's page opened in English and in Chinese). In Chrome on the built app with this change and without it (cc42d703), served side by side on one local API with stand-in Pi and Agents workers, on a draft copy of Neon City made through the home page's case dialog: the base build's "Full-screen brand page" showed the four Chinese notes as values under "Using published output from …"; the changed build shows the note above in English (and in Chinese on a Chinese page), empty values, no alert and no Han character in the English panel.
- Keep the magnifier of the skill library's search fields at the left of their box on the settings page (Settings → Skills, its "Search skills" and the skills.sh search): the settings centre stacks a label's content, so since 2026-10-18 the icon stood centred above the box (seen 2026-10-20 in the signed-in check of 「从 skills.sh 查找」).
- Let an earlier release's document cache of a hosted canvas leave localStorage once that release's run record of the canvas is over a day old (2026-10-20, the last of the 「本机存储空间已满」 problem). The canvas store copies such a run record in and leaves it in localStorage, where a tab of that release may still read it, and while any such record was there it kept the canvas's document cache (0.6 to 6 MB) in localStorage too, and the legacy sweep left the canvas there: a canvas whose old tab closed in the middle of a run kept its cache in localStorage for good, even after it was opened in this release. The protection is for a tab of the earlier release still running a node or watching a run over that cache; such a tab removes its record when the run ends, and none runs or watches one for a day. Now only a record that started less than 24 hours ago (a start ahead of the clock included) holds the cache, and a record without a readable start time holds nothing (that release read such bytes as no run). A canvas with an unsent draft is still left to its own opening.
- Start a short entry's text at the left of the skill library's list: the library's buttons centre their content, so a pick whose title and description were short sat in the middle of its row.
- Read the YAML of a SKILL.md written for other agents when a workspace imports it: a description folded over several lines (`description: >`, `|`) or continued on indented lines, a quoted value with its escapes, and a list of tags (`- html` lines, or `[html, data]`). An imported skill's description was the single character ">", and continued lines were dropped. A nested key such as `metadata:` is still skipped with its lines. What such a file says beyond what the library holds no longer refuses the upload: tags AwwO does not know are dropped and a description over 1,024 characters is shortened at a word (a member's own fields are still checked as before). Built-in skills keep the strict one-pair-per-line form.
- Say what a node's inputs and outputs lack in the page's language, and nothing while a wired input waits for its upstream (seen 2026-10-19 on the live build saas-5d72d6c98927 in English: in a draft copy of the Roost case, "Turn 1: Wren gathers the facts" opened on its inputs showed the red line 「The recorder」为必填项。 under the field that said "Waiting for usable output from “Turn recorder”"). The contract checks (`validateContractFields` and `parseContractOutput` in `apps/web/src/canvas/nodeContracts.ts`) wrote their messages in Chinese only; they now read them from the canvas dictionary in the reader's language, and the inputs and outputs forms, a publication's errors and an invalid result's note pass the page's language (the run engine's own Chinese notes, which quote them, keep them word for word). And the inputs form checked every field once any upstream had no usable output yet, so a wired field, whose own value is empty, was "required": like a run's preflight and the Next card, it now checks a wired value when it arrives, and the field keeps its note that it waits for its source; once every upstream has delivered, a value that does not fit its field (an output the upstream left out, say) is named beside the output it came from. Tests in canvas-contracts, canvas-contract-fields, canvas-node-conversation, canvas-deliverables and saas-production-copy (the Roost copy's Wren node opened in English). In Chrome on the built app with and without the change, on a local stack: the base build showed the Chinese line on the Roost copy's Wren node, the changed one only the waiting note; emptying its required "Task and boundaries" says “Task and boundaries” is required., and the Chinese page reads as before.
- Read the rest of a workspace's canvas list on every visit when the browser forgets its copies of canvases deleted elsewhere, instead of at most once a day (owner 2026-10-19: 「改成每次都读」). The signed-in re-check of that sweep (`saas-5d72d6c98927`) found that in a workspace longer than one page (52 canvases) the copies of canvases deleted after the day's whole-list read stayed until the next one. The canvas list now hands the sweep its first page's cursor, and the sweep reads on from it in the summary view, 200 a page (a list cursor stays valid across views and page sizes): one read on every visit, the whole list of a workspace of up to 250 canvases, and only the canvases past the first page. A list longer still is read on past that one read at most once a day, as before; past 10 pages, or on any failure, nothing is swept. The earlier release's record of its daily reads (`awwo.canvas-store.swept.v1`) is removed. On a local stack with the real API, a 55-canvas workspace's home read the rest in one request (`view=summary&limit=200&cursor=…`), asked the server only about the two canvases deleted through the API (404, forgotten), and kept a canvas past the first page that the browser held without asking about it.
- End a direct task (直接执行) only once the model call it still has running has been cut and settled by its own handler, whatever ended it (owner 2026-10-19: every ending, a stop's too). The proxy that serves a task's calls learns that a call was given up on only when its connection goes, while the broker's report of the task's end, a lost stream, an event the API refuses, the user's stop, the task's time limit or an API shutdown reached the run's end with nothing to order the two: the run's end settled any call still running as one its run left open (class restart, `worker_lost`, charged its reserve), after which the proxy's own settling, which charges a cut call by its bytes and its time (`creditCharge`; at $2 / $10 a million tokens, ten minutes of hidden reasoning is 99 credits against a reserve of 12), found nothing to settle. Each ending now takes no more calls, cuts the one still running and waits up to 6 s for its handler to settle it, as project runs already wait for theirs; a call its handler cannot settle in time is settled as left open, as before. A call its handler settles is recorded as the cut it is (status failed, class timeout; one cut before it was sent, as never sent), a stop's too, where the run's end recorded the run's own status (cancelled, after a stop). Refunds do not change, nor does the daily total but for a call cut before it was sent (on a personal connection), which now counts as never sent. The same race made `TestPostgresDirectTaskGateTimeoutsAndLateErrorsAreRefunded` fail now and then ("gone: the ledger reads restart|0").
- Forget what the browser keeps of hosted canvases the server has deleted (owner 2026-10-19: 「把删除画布残留的副本也清掉」). Deleting a canvas from this browser's list already forgot its copies, but a canvas deleted elsewhere (another device, a teammate) or before that kept them, and the canvas store took an earlier release's localStorage copies of deleted canvases into IndexedDB, where they stayed (4.2 million characters for eight deleted canvases in one profile, found by the signed-in production check of the canvas-storage release). Once a workspace's canvas list is read and the page is idle, `apps/web/src/saas/canvasStorageEviction.ts` looks at the canvases this browser keeps copies of that are not in the list (the whole list is read first when it runs past its first page, at most once a day) and asks the server about each (at most 50 read and 20 asked a time, from a random start, the rest on later visits). A canvas the server answers 404 for is forgotten, its editor's and reader's copies in IndexedDB and localStorage alike, except its unsent drafts, which its page still offers for export. The canvas store's new `forgetIdle` does that alone with the canvas (under its Web Lock, taken only when no tab holds it), so a canvas open in any tab is left and not asked about, and what is removed is decided on what is read while alone with it. Any other answer, or storage that fails, stops the sweep until the next visit, and a browser whose tabs cannot share the store is not swept. Tombstones of canvases forgotten more than 30 days ago are dropped on the way. Only keys of canvas ids the API makes are taken for canvases, never the workspace's own facts under the same prefix. In Chrome on a local stack (one profile, two tabs): of three canvases opened and then deleted through the API alone, the plain one lost all four of its keys, the one with an unsent draft kept only the draft, and the one a second tab had open was left untouched and not asked about until that tab closed, when it went too; an earlier release's localStorage copy of a canvas long gone went, and the canvas still there kept its copies.
- Keep an opened node's message box and the row under it (the model, 用户须知) inside the node in a short chat column before its conversation starts (2026-10-19, in Chrome on the live build at 1280 × 720 with no conversation yet: a draft of three lines pushed that row 12.5 to 45 px below the node and ten lines 41 to 47 px, in every look; at 1366 × 657 ten lines did too, and at 1280 × 720 two lines cut WorkBuddy's 用户须知 and a custom bubble or flat style's model by 1 to 4 px). A chat column under 440 px draws its message box as one line that grows as one types, but the conversation kept its share of the column and its empty conversation 56 px, so the growing box pushed the composer out of the conversation, which clips it. With no conversation yet, the conversation is now never shorter than its composer and the empty conversation's padding (its flex basis is its content, in which the empty conversation's own content, size-contained, counts for nothing): the empty conversation gives way first, then the task card and a failure note above it, which scroll in what is left; where less than 20 px of the empty conversation would show, its content is not drawn (no sliver, and no blank scroller for Tab to stop on), unless one of its starter prompts has the keyboard's focus. A closed rework note counts with its one line; beside an open one the conversation keeps its share of the column (its empty conversation still gives way), and the note keeps its toggle, which the empty conversation used to cover once the note was crushed. A conversation with replies, a tall column, the template guide and opened inputs that take the column keep their layout. `apps/web/src/canvas/awwo-node.css`; a test in `canvas-open-node-content`. Checked in Chrome on the built app with and without the change, on a local stack with stand-in workers (an engine, a model picker and real conversations): 280 configurations (the default, Codex, WorkBuddy and Claude Code looks and custom bubble, flat and terminal styles; 1920 × 1080, 1366 × 657 and 1280 × 720; light and dark; an empty box, two lines, a long wrapping line and ten lines; with and without a conversation). In a short column with no conversation 64 of 112 fitted before and all 112 fit, each with the composer's 8 px bottom padding to spare, and the layout changed only where the composer already ran past its conversation (16, by that padding); the other 168 lay out exactly as before.
- End a Bedrock call on the Python OpenAI Agents worker that sends nothing for 15 minutes as the service's failure, so a canvas node runs again (owner 2026-10-19: 「第4条做吧」). From 05:19Z to 07:37Z five Claude Opus 5.5 nodes of one canvas each made one call that gave nothing back for its run's whole 25 minutes (no usage; prompts of 2–14 KB) and ended as `run_timeout`, which is not run again; run again by hand, the same nodes answered in 64–164 s. The bridge's botocore read timeout was the run's deadline; it is now the stream's idle limit, 15 minutes (`BEDROCK_STREAM_IDLE_SECONDS`, as `BEDROCK_STREAM_IDLE_MS` in the TypeScript bridge; a shorter run deadline still comes first), above the silence of a working stream: Opus 5.5 thinks before its first word and Bedrock sends nothing until it is done, yet of the 3,384 Opus 5.5 calls completed on the three workers from 10-12 to 10-19 the longest wait for the first token was 436 s, none over 600 s. Such a stall (botocore's `ReadTimeoutError` while the response is awaited, urllib3's inside a stream) is a 504 `ReadTimeoutError` from the bridge, logged as `bedrock_call_failed`, and reads as `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` (provider_unavailable), which R-1 runs again when the run produced nothing; it does not turn to the model's other profile. A stalled call is charged as before (its estimate, at most 65,536 hidden tokens), and each attempt R-1 makes is a call of its own. Tests drive real botocore against a local endpoint that stalls, before and after the response's headers, with and without a fallback profile.
- Let the Pi worker's runs on its default model plan without thinking (`AWWO_PI_DISABLE_THINKING=true`; owner 2026-10-19: 「qwen 规划也关掉思考」). A plan the operator's planner model may not take (over its input bound or a daily ceiling) runs on the default model, qwen3.8-27b-p6 on the LLM Gate, which Pi registered as a model that does not reason, so it sent its chat template no switch and the model thought anyway: since 2026-10-16, 12 of its 25 plans failed, with 10,479 output tokens on average and at most 16,384, the whole cap (on 10-19 five cut at about 430 s and four that failed their checks). With the switch, the default model's runs send `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}` (a payload hook in `apps/pi-worker/pi-task.mjs`), as the Agents workers' `AWWO_OPENAI_AGENTS_DISABLE_THINKING` does; only a Chat Completions default model on the LLM Gate (named, or by its URL) takes it, any other value stops startup, and `/internal/computer-model` calls keep their per-call `thinking` option. The switch is for the model: it is to be turned off when the default model is no longer a Qwen-style one.
- Fit the Claude Code look's message box in a short chat column (2026-10-19, at 1366 × 657 and 1280 × 720: the box's bottom border and the row under it, 用户须知 and the model, fell outside the opened node). A chat column under 440 px draws the other looks' box as one line that grows as one types, with its "+" inside it at the left, but leaves the terminal layout out, whose ">" prompt starts the line there; so that layout kept its "+" row over a 64 px box, and the row under it ended 17 to 34 px below the node. In a short column the terminal layout's box is now one line that grows as one types as well, with its "+" inside it at the right, beside the send button; the prompt keeps the start of the first line, and the text stops before the "+". Taller columns, media nodes and every other look are unchanged. `apps/web/src/canvas/node-view-styles.css`; tests in `canvas-node-view-style`. Checked in Chrome on the built app, with and without the change, on a local stack with stand-in workers: at 1920 × 1080, 1366 × 657 and 1280 × 720, light and dark, empty and with two lines of text, with and without a conversation, with and without the "+", in the Claude Code look and a custom style with the terminal layout, every short box fits with its model and 用户须知 (without the change none with a "+" and no conversation did; a draft of three lines or more with no conversation yet still pushes that row out at 1280 × 720, as in every look), and the prompt is never on the "+" and sits where a ">" typed into the box sits, as before; every other look, and the terminal layout in a tall column, gives every element of the page the same computed style and box as without the change.
- Save a big hosted canvas once per drag, and let a draft its page left with a save out be restored onto that save (found 2026-10-19 by the signed-in production check of the canvas-storage release, on a 142-node 6.3 MB canvas). A drag rewrites the whole document on every frame; on such a canvas a frame, or a pause in the drag, took longer than autosave's fixed 450 ms wait, so one 900 ms drag sent five 6 MB saves one after another. `apps/web/src/saas/autosavePace.ts` makes autosave wait while a pointer is held down (at most 10 s) and, after a write, for a quiet spell that grows with the document (450 ms and 200 ms more per million characters) and follows the writes' own pace (twice the gap between the last two, at most 4 s); an edit made while a save is out goes once its burst is over. A run or a node setup still saves at once. Leaving the page right after a drag left a draft based on the version before the save that was out, and the server stored that save after the page was gone, so on the next opening the draft looked like a conflict and could only be exported. A draft written while a save is out now records it (`sending`: the version it built on and the hash of the document sent); when the cloud is one version on and holds exactly that document, the draft is restored onto it, and the recovery page says so. A draft that holds exactly the cloud's document no longer asks to be recovered (it is removed when no other tab has the canvas open). In Chrome on a local stack with a 142-node 4.5 MB canvas: a slow drag (eight moves 700 ms apart) sent 6 saves before and 1 after; leaving with a save out left the draft export-only before, and after it restored, the cloud then holding the last edit.
- A Claude call on Bedrock that its inference profile refuses before anything streamed is asked once more through the same model's other profile, global or US (owner 2026-10-19: 「线上如果claude global区域的无法访问就用us区域的，互相作为备选」). On the morning of 2026-10-19 the global profile of Claude Haiku 4.5 answered `ServiceUnavailableException` 17 times (17 failed planner and assistant runs, from 02:07Z to 05:26Z) and the global profile of Claude Opus 5.5 refused 3 calls with `ThrottlingException: Too many tokens per day` (a daily quota the account's other Bedrock users share), while the US profiles answered. Each Claude entry in `apps/bedrock-models.json` names its `fallbackTarget` (`us.` for a `global.` target; either direction is allowed, and only another profile of the same model). The bridges (`createBedrockFetch` in `apps/bedrock-bridge.ts`, `BedrockConverseTransport` in the Python worker) send the same request to it, once, on the same client, when the first profile refuses the call for capacity or quota (`ThrottlingException`, `ServiceUnavailableException`, `InternalServerException`, `ModelNotReadyException`, `ServiceQuotaExceededException`, also as the stream's first event); never after anything streamed, never for any other failure, never a second time. A model without a fallback target is called exactly as before. The Pi, JS Agents (and sandbox) and Python workers pass it on (runs and the Pi worker's managed calls), and log each fallback and each failed Bedrock call as one content-free line (`bedrock_profile_fallback`, `bedrock_call_failed`: model ids, the error name, its status, and `upstream`: true for AWS's answer or the way to it (the connection, the credentials), false for the bridge's own refusal), which the Pi worker had no way to log before. Every Bedrock child builds its bridge with one helper (`childBedrockFetch`). The workers' IAM user may call the US profiles of the catalog's Claude models since 2026-10-19 (policy versions v4). `scripts/bedrock-catalog-check.py` checks fallback targets too.
- Start the message box's first line with the Claude Code look's ">" prompt, beside the text (2026-10-18: it sat on the box's "+" at every window size). Since a node's message box takes files (2026-10-11), its "+" has a row of its own above the box, but the terminal layout still drew its prompt at the row's top, where the box itself used to begin, so the prompt covered the "+" and sat 33 px above the line it marks. In the terminal layout the row is now a one-column grid, the "+" over the box, and the prompt is placed in the box's own grid area: it stays beside the first line with a "+" and without one (a canvas that is not a cloud canvas takes no files). The "+" keeps its place; the box loses the 6 px a line of text left under it; the other looks are unchanged. `apps/web/src/canvas/node-view-styles.css`; tests in `canvas-node-view-style`. Checked in Chrome on a local stack at 1920 × 1080 and 1366 × 657, light and dark, empty and with text, in the Claude Code look and a custom style with the terminal layout: the prompt is never on the "+" and sits within 1 px of where a ">" typed into the box sits, as it did before the "+"; the default, Codex, WorkBuddy and custom bubble and flat looks draw their message boxes pixel for pixel as before.
- Keep hosted canvases in the browser's IndexedDB instead of its localStorage, and let a canvas save carry 8 MiB (owner 2026-10-18: 「扩大容器，满足给所有用户储存画布。消解这个报警」). localStorage holds about 5 MB for the whole site, and each opened canvas kept its document there, a draft of it while a save was pending, its sync proof and its run records, never removed: a 1.9M-character canvas (PALLWARD, 69 nodes) filled it nearly alone, so autosave paused behind 「本机存储空间已满」, and the first opening of a large canvas could take the page down with "Setting the value of … exceeded the quota". `apps/web/src/canvas/canvasStore.ts` keeps a hosted canvas's storage (its document and backup, drafts, sync proof and version, run journals, recovery records, planning conversation and page repairs) in memory once the canvas opens, served synchronously as before, and writes it to IndexedDB (`canvasStoreIdb.ts`, a share of the disk) shortly after each change and at once when the page is hidden or left. Every write is its own IndexedDB version and never reads first, so the write on leaving the page can finish. Tabs of a canvas send each other their writes over a BroadcastChannel and see them as `storage` events; a tab opening a canvas asks the tabs holding it (counted through a shared Web Lock) for writes not stored yet; Lamport stamps and tombstones make every tab and IndexedDB settle on one value; a write a tab never stores (it crashed) is stored by the tabs that received it. What earlier releases left in localStorage comes in by kind, since a tab of that release may still be open: drafts move and leave localStorage once IndexedDB holds the record of their move (the hashes of the bytes taken in, written with them); the document, its backup and the sync proof come in as one group, decided by the document, never over a document this release wrote since and never while a run record of the canvas is in localStorage (a running tab saves only over the document it last wrote), the document then kept as an export-only draft when it may hold edits that tab never synced; the small records that tab reads and rewrites are copied and stay, and the version keeps the larger number; recorded bytes are leftovers and never overwrite what was written since. Other canvases' keys come in while the page is idle (`saas/canvasStoreSweep.ts`), alone with each canvas under its Web Lock, except a canvas with an unsent draft or a run record; reader copies (`<canvas>/read-only`) are dropped and now stay in the page's memory only. Deleting a canvas removes what the browser kept of it. Where a browser has no IndexedDB, the canvas keeps using localStorage, and a full localStorage on the first opening keeps the copy in memory and shows the warning instead of failing. A write IndexedDB refuses (a full disk) pauses autosave behind the same warning. The API's canvas create and save take bodies up to 8 MiB (`maxCanvasBodyBytes`; the largest canvas was 90% of the general 2 MiB) and validate and store eight at a time, each holding its turn only from the end of its body to the start of its reply; at most 32 wait for a turn, one waiting 10 s is answered 503 `canvas_save_busy`, and the page sends that edit again up to three times. Every other request keeps 2 MiB, and every list page also ends at 8 MiB of items. A save reply without the saved canvas counts as a failed save, and one over the limit says the canvas is over 8 MB. The website's nginx lets the canvas routes through up to 9 MiB, with the /api location's other settings.
- Draw each node's bar and elapsed time in the execution timeline (执行时间线) during and after a cloud run (seen on the owner's live stream 2026-10-18: every row showed an empty bar and 「—」, the running one too). The bar is drawn only from recorded times, and none reached it: a cloud graph's nodes carried no times, and each poll set the rows from the run journal, replacing the times the page had stamped. A graph run's nodes now carry `startedAt` (their current run's admission) and, once settled, `endedAt` (its end), read from the runs themselves (a collaboration node's from its turns' runs; none while a node waits for its next attempt); the journal keeps them through a reload, and the timeline keeps the times it recorded, stamping only transitions it saw.
- Show the "AwwO was updated" notice above an open dialog, where it can be used. A modal dialog (a case's, the tutorial's, a preview's) makes the rest of the page inert, so the notice of 2026-10-18 showed blurred behind it, and its Reload and "Not now" could not be clicked until the dialog closed (seen on production in a case dialog). A popover shown above the dialog would stay inert too, and a fixed box inside it moves with the dialog's scroll and transform. While a modal dialog is open, the notice now sits inside the one on top (the one holding the focus, else the one opened last), shown as a popover in the top layer above its content and in the interface's language; it goes back above a dialog that reopens itself, and when that dialog closes it is the page's own box again. The tutorial's "could not load" dialog no longer restyles it. A browser without popovers keeps it a plain box inside the dialog. `apps/web/src/saas/StaleBuildNotice.tsx`; tests in `saas-stale-build`. Checked in Chrome on the built app with a later release simulated: inside the case dialog the notice is on screen and takes real clicks, "Not now" leaves the dialog open, and once the dialog closes the notice is back on the page and its Reload reloads.
- Save the open canvas, then offer a reload, when a tab opened before a website release cannot load a part of its build (2026-10-17: in such a tab, Umber's "Copy example to my canvases" said the case's run recording could not be loaded, `case_record_unavailable`). A release moves the site to a new build; a tab opened earlier keeps running its own and fetches the rest of it lazily (a case's dialog and record, the tutorial, the previews, the 3D and PDF viewers), each a hashed file of its own build, which the site no longer served. On such a failure (Vite's `vite:preloadError`) the page now asks `/saas.html` which build the site serves (uncached, 10 s); when that page's entry script is not its own, a notice says AwwO was updated, saves the open canvas first (done when the server has every edit) and only then offers Reload. Nothing reloads by itself, and "Not now" hides the notice until another part fails to load. A node inspector that holds changes the canvas does not have yet holds the reload as well, a save that takes over 20 s offers "Try saving again", and a save that fails points to the canvas's own message and its local copy. The reload buttons that a case's run record and the tutorial for new accounts already showed for such failures save first too. `apps/web/src/saas/staleBuild.ts`, `StaleBuildNotice.tsx` and `apps/web/src/canvas/unsavedEdits.ts`; tests in `saas-stale-build`, `saas-lazy-load-failure` and `canvas-inspector-lock`. Checked in Chrome against real builds behind the production nginx config and a real API: in an old canvas tab whose tutorial chunk was gone, the notice saved a held edit before it offered Reload, and the reload landed on the new build with the edit; with a save that fails, it offered no Reload.
- Stop running a canvas node again by itself after its run timed out (owner 2026-10-18: 「超时不再重试」). A run_timeout is a run's own deadline: all 17 of the 21 days to 2026-10-18 lasted 600 s or more, and R-1 had run 5 of them again, each a full wait and a full charge more. A connection the Python worker cannot open within 5 s reads as `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` (provider_unavailable), which stays retryable and, ended within moments, unbilled. The JS worker still reports undici's 10 s connect timeout as a deadline.
- Give a run on the Python OpenAI Agents worker up to 25 minutes (2026-10-18 customer report: a node on Claude Opus 5.5 failed with run_timeout at 600 s before it had written a word). `AWWO_OPENAI_AGENTS_TIMEOUT_MS` accepts up to 1,800,000 ms (the JS worker's bound) and production gives 1,500,000; the OpenAI client's timeout follows the run's deadline instead of the SDK's 600 s, and the SDK's `APITimeoutError` reads as `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`. The old worker refuses the new value, so the code and the env line switch and roll back together (docs/awwo-bedrock.md).
- Estimate a call cut before its first text up to the 65,536 output tokens a model may write per call (the model catalog's `MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`; Claude Opus 5.5 may write 64,000), not 32,000; a test keeps `maxHiddenTokens` equal to the catalog's cap.
- Keep a direct task's answer when one of its tool calls slipped (2026-10-18). The pinned OpenMaus core refuses a turn's final answer once any tool result was an error, so a task whose model asked for a missing file, corrected itself and finished still failed. A workspace call that failed with the workspace as it was (a wrong path, a missing file, a directory, a symbolic link, a refused permission, `inputs/` written to, too large, a task's 16 files or 8 MiB already published) now comes back as an ordinary result that says it did nothing (`failed: true`, a fixed code and sentence; `published: false` for publish and archive); everything else stays an error. A `read` keeps its whole result within the 50 KiB the core passes on, says `truncated: true` before its text, and a `write` no longer echoes the bytes it wrote. A call whose arguments do not match its tool's schema is refused by the core itself and still ends the turn.

- Stream a direct task's Chat Completions calls through LLM Gate, so that a long answer is no longer cut off at Cloudflare's limit of about 100 s. Cloudflare in front of the Gate closes a response that sends nothing for about that long, and a call sent with `stream: false` sends nothing until its last token, so a direct task's call that wrote or thought for longer failed with a 524 (or a 504) however good its answer would have been. `providerComputerRequest` (`apps/computer-model.ts`) now sends a Chat Completions call to the Gate with `stream: true` and `stream_options.include_usage`. The Gate is told by its URL (`https://api.clawhunt.site`, so a Gate profile labelled `openai`, as older configs do, streams too) or by the label `llmgate`. `handleComputerModel` gathers the stream with `gatherChatStream`, as the Bedrock path does, into the same one completion: the text, the tool calls, the finish reason and the usage.
  - Hidden reasoning (`reasoning_content`), comments and empty `data:` lines (keep-alives) are passed over and never forwarded. A Gate that answers a streamed call whole (an error in a 200, or no stream) is read as before.
  - `gatherChatStream`, the Bedrock path's too: it stops reading at `[DONE]` (a gateway may hold the connection open after it); it reads `"error": null` as no error and a `code` or `message` in place of choices as an error frame; it joins a tool call sent whole without an index by its id, and a tool call keeps the id and name it was given (an empty one says nothing, a different one breaks the call); a streamed refusal (OpenAI's `delta.refusal`) is kept, so it is refused as one read whole (`answer`/`refusal`) and never forwarded. A line cut across many chunks is read in one pass (it searched the open line again for every chunk), and no open line may pass 1 MiB. A connection that breaks after the answer's finish reason, with no line half read, keeps the answer: only its usage and `[DONE]` were still to come. An answer gathered from a stream, Bedrock's included, is held to the 512 KiB of an answer read whole (`answer`/`size`): over the 2 MiB the API takes back it was charged by an estimate of its bytes.
  - A stream that closes before its end is named by its silence first (`streamClosed`): `stream:closed:idle` when it had sent nothing for 90 s or more, as Cloudflare's cut of a silent response ends it; `stream:closed` for any other close, one a provider or a gateway made at once. The detail says how: the socket's code when the connection broke off (`UND_ERR_SOCKET`), `end` when the stream ended without a finish reason; the silence goes to the worker's log line (`quietMs`), never the reply. The Gate's error frame (an `error`, or a `code` or `message` in place of choices, as a moderation stop) is its error inside a 200, named as one read whole is (`provider:200:<its code or type>`), so the Bedrock rule for `stream:error:` never reads it. What the stream itself said wrong is `stream:<detail>`: `stream:unfinished` (`[DONE]` without a finish reason), `stream:shape` (a malformed chunk), `stream:content`, `stream:tool-calls`, `stream:size` (more than a stream or one of its lines may carry). The worker's own wait for the next byte running out stays `network:UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT`, a cut while it streams stays a cut (499), and before the stream begins a failure reads as before (`provider:<status>`, `network:<code>`).
  - Anthropic Messages, Responses and every other provider are sent whole, as before. A personal LLM Gate key streams as the operator's does (its binding is the Gate's own address).
  - Pi's own canvas runs have always streamed their Gate calls this way (pi-ai, with `include_usage`). On 2026-10-07, Pi runs of 215 s whose first visible token came after about 206 s of qwen's thinking came through the Gate, so a Gate stream stays open while qwen thinks (its thinking streams as `reasoning_content`). Not shown: a model that thinks without streaming anything (GPT's hidden reasoning on Chat Completions) sends no bytes unless the Gate sends keep-alives, so the edge can still cut it; that close is `stream:closed:idle`. This code has not yet run against the real Gate, but a probe there (2026-10-17, the owner's go, two qwen calls with the operator's key) showed the shapes it reads: the thinking streamed as `reasoning_content` for 417 s with no silence over 0.74 s, usage came in its own `choices: []` chunk, and tool-call deltas carried their index (the first its id, type and name). The Gate's edge refuses Python's default User-Agent with a 403; the workers send Node's.
  - Refunds (`computerProviderFault`, `computerModelFailure` in `computer_model_proxy.go`): with the platform's credentials a streamed Gate call cut by the edge's idle limit (`stream:closed:idle`) gives its call back, as the same edge's cut of a call sent whole (a 524) does under the owner's rule of 2026-10-17 (below). That is the refund session's reading of the rule (2026-10-17), for the owner to confirm. A stream closed at once (`stream:closed`) gives nothing back: a task's own words can bring one about (a moderation stop, a parser failing on the model's output), and a task that fails gives back all its calls. With personal credentials no stream failure gives anything back (a personal Gate key streams too), and a call the task's own side gave up on stays a cut.
  - Refunds, late errors: a Gate error inside a 200, a streamed call's error frame or an error in a 200 read whole, gives its call back when it names the provider's capacity or the operator's own access (`overloaded_error`, `rate_limit_error`, `rate_limit_exceeded`, `insufficient_quota`, `insufficient_user_quota`, `permission_error`), as its status would have sent whole: once a stream began, a late overload can only come as a frame, so the owner's rule for late Gate errors no longer depends on whether the call streamed (`computerCapacityKinds`; the refund session, 2026-10-17). A server error (`server_error`, `api_error`), the Gate's catch-all `bad_response_status_code` and a moderation code give nothing back, as another 5xx gives nothing back. Verified: the label table (an overload in a 200 refunded, a moderation stop not, neither on a personal connection), a task whose streamed call ended in an overload frame and one stopped by moderation in `TestPostgresDirectTaskGateTimeoutsAndLateErrorsAreRefunded`, and the Gate's Anthropic-style overload frame reading `provider:200:overloaded_error` in the managed-execution suite.
  - Verified: the managed-execution suite 31/31. New tests: a Gate stream gathered from 11-byte pieces with reasoning, keep-alives, a tool call and usage; which calls stream; a tool call without an index; a 900 KB line in pieces and 15 MiB without a line end; a stream read to `[DONE]` and no further, error frames in place of choices, a tool call that keeps its id and name; twelve broken streams and their log lines, without provider text (an idle close and one at once, `[DONE]` without a finish, a Gate error frame and a moderation stop, a streamed refusal, a gathered answer over 512 KiB among them); a stalled stream cut by its time limit and by a cancel, each after its first frame; a personal Gate connection that streams. Also the Pi worker 67/67, the OpenAI Agents worker 194 (10 skipped), the bridge and catalog 33/33, user models 5/5, the OpenMaus worker 13 (5 skipped) and `tsc -p apps/tsconfig.computer-model.json`. Go: the stream labels in the label table of `TestComputerFailureCodesAndLongFileNames` (the platform's credentials and a personal connection), and three new endings in `TestPostgresDirectTaskGateTimeoutsAndLateErrorsAreRefunded`: an idle close gives its call back, a close at once and a call its task gave up on (once its worker held it) give nothing back; the whole `internal/app` suite (631 pass, 2 skipped, in WSL; the four tests that read `apps/web` pass from the Windows tree). GitHub CI not run (owner 2026-10-07).
- Send a direct task's thread to every model provider at its user turn, not only to Bedrock. The managed-execution engine opens every task's thread with its own greeting, an assistant message before the user's (`Hi, I'm AwwO workspace. What would you like me to do?`), which Converse refuses; on 2026-10-16 (15:26-15:42Z, the owner's workspace) kimi-k3 and claude-sonnet-5 through LLM Gate failed each task's first model call within about a second, before any model work, while qwen3.8-27b took the same request. `threadOpening` (formerly `bedrockOpening`, `apps/computer-model.ts`) now moves the greeting's text to the end of the system prompt for Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages and Responses as it did for the Bedrock bridge, keeping one system message (some chat templates take no second one). That the greeting is what those two models' gateway refused is the likeliest reading of the timing, to be confirmed by the log lines below once the Pi worker carries them. Verified: a new test sends the production opening through LLM Gate on the Pi worker, Anthropic Messages and Responses (each provider sees one system prompt, then the user); the Bedrock opening test now expects one system block; `node --test apps/computer-model.test.ts` 19/19 on its own commit, 23/23 with the diagnostics below.
- Say why a direct task's model call failed, by kind only, in the worker's reply, in the worker's log and in the API's log. Until now the Pi worker answered most refusals with a bare code (`PROVIDER_ERROR` for any LLM Gate failure, a rejected answer, a fetch that failed) and logged only Bedrock call failures, and the API logged only `computer_model_failed`, so on 2026-10-16 nobody could tell why kimi-k3, claude-sonnet-5, Opus 5.5 and qwen3.8-27b calls failed.
  - `apps/computer-model.ts` gives a provider failure a reason: `provider:<status>[:<type>]` (the provider's own error code or type when it is a label, e.g. `provider:400:context_length_exceeded`, `provider:524`; an error inside a 200 too), `network[:<code>]`, `body` (a 2xx that is not JSON); an answer that does not hold is `answer` with a `detail` naming the check (`finish:length`, `finish:content_filter`, `refusal`, `empty`, `tools-mismatch`, `tool-name`, `tool-args`, `size`, …); a Bedrock stream that broke is `stream:<detail>` (`stream:error:429:throttlingException` for an AWS failure after the stream began, `stream:error:api_error` for the bridge's own refusal); a cut call (499) says `timeout`, `disconnected`, `stopping` or `cancelled`; a refused request names its check (`completion:pending`, `completion:tool-result`, `body:size`, `catalog`, …). Every refusal is one log line, `computer_model_rejected`, with the runtime, run, model, status, code, reason, detail and ms (and the measured bytes and the limit for `CONTEXT_LIMIT`); it replaces `computer_model_bedrock_failed`. Never provider text, the call's messages or a key. A provider error's body is read for its kind only, at most 16 KiB for at most 2 s, and a call cut while it is read stays a cut (499).
  - The API logs `managed model call failed` for each call its worker refused or did not answer: the run, the call's number, the runtime and model, the worker's status and its labels (only label-shaped values are kept) and the ledger code (`computerWorkerError`, `logComputerCall` in `computer_model_proxy.go`).
  - The ledger reads the new labels (`computerModelFailure`, `computerProviderFault`) and counts as the platform's side (refundable): a provider behind LLM Gate refusing our key or our quota, missing the model, throttling, out of service or out of the edge's reach (401, 404, 429, 503, 529, Cloudflare's 521-523, 525, 526 and 530, a 403 that names the operator's quota or permission), however long the call had run; a Gate call cut by a time limit on its way (a 408, an edge's 504 or 524, the worker's HTTP client limits) and a Bedrock model's own time limit after its stream began, which the owner ruled the platform's timeouts on 2026-10-17 (Cloudflare cuts a Gate call that sends nothing for about 100 s, and a call sent whole sends nothing until its last token; Chat Completions calls through the Gate stream since the entry above); the provider out of reach before the request was sent (a connect error); a 2xx that is not JSON; an AWS outage after a Bedrock stream began (throttling, a quota, the service unavailable or not ready, an internal error); and a worker that stopped under the call (transport). Not refunded, because the task's words or the model's own answer can bring them about: a bare 403 or another 5xx, a reset without an answer, a refusal of the request, an error inside a 200 (unless it names the provider's capacity, above), a model whose own output broke a Bedrock stream (`ModelStreamErrorException`), the bridge's refusal of what the model sent. With personal credentials the provider, its key and its quota are the user's, so none of its failures is refunded. The Bedrock rule before a stream begins (`bedrock:<status>:<type>`) is unchanged.
  - Verified: the managed-execution suite 23/23 (new: a provider's statuses, an edge timeout, an error in a 200, a socket reset, eleven answer checks, the four cuts, a provider that stalls on its error, the admission details and their log lines, all without provider text), the Pi worker 67/67, the OpenAI Agents worker 194 (10 skipped), the bridge and catalog 33/33, user models 5/5, the OpenMaus worker 13 (5 skipped), `tsc -p apps/tsconfig.computer-model.json`; Go: `TestComputerWorkerErrorKeepsOnlyLabels`, the label table in `TestComputerFailureCodesAndLongFileNames`, three new endings in `TestPostgresDirectTaskEndingsRecordTheirRefund`, `TestPostgresComputerModelProxyLogsWhatTheWorkerAnswered` (eight worker answers, the protocol and transport endings among them), `TestPostgresDirectTaskGateTimeoutsAndLateErrorsAreRefunded` (a 524 and a late 503 give their calls back), and the whole `internal/app` suite (a Linux binary in WSL, 4 shards on a private PostgreSQL 16 in RAM; the four tests that read `apps/web` run from the Windows tree); `go vet ./...`. Reviewed by Claude code-reviewer and security-reviewer subagents (Codex out of credits until 10-22); their findings (a stalled error body, personal connections, a Bedrock model's own broken stream and the Gate statuses a task can bring about counted as the platform's) are fixed above. GitHub CI not run (owner 2026-10-07).

- Ship the preview fonts' licenses with the native app too (third-party notices follow-up 2026-10-16). The native build (`apps/web/vite.config.mjs`, `npm run build`), whose output the desktop app (built by the `desktop-windows` release workflow) and the root Docker image ship, bundles the same 26 preview font faces as the hosted one: the canvas's artifact preview loads `src/canvas/previewFonts.ts`, which inlines each face as a data: URL in a script chunk of its own. None of those chunks started with a license. The native build now registers the hosted build's `inlinedFontLicences` too, so each of them starts with the license of its font's family, unchanged, and the build fails when a face would ship without it; both configs take each face's license file from `familyLicences` in `apps/web/scripts/font-licences.mjs`, by `src/canvas/previewFontList.ts`. The native build ships none of the hosted app's own fonts (Mona Sans), so it needs no plugin for them; pdf.js's fonts, which it bundles too, are not covered here. `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` says both builds carry the licenses. `tests/native-font-licences.test.ts`, in the native test list, runs the native config on the preview fonts and React and checks each face's chunk for its license, that the config's own chunk groups still apply, and that no other chunk starts with a license or a line break.
- Ship the whole fonts of the three preview font families whose names are reserved (owner decision 2026-10-16: ship the original fonts, Playfair Display at full size; Mona Sans has its own entry below). Orbitron, Playfair Display and Press Start 2P, each with its own name reserved, shipped to running previews as Latin subsets, which are Modified Versions under the SIL Open Font License (OFL-FAQ 2.6) and may not use a Reserved Font Name, yet pages name them by it, and a preview supplies them only under it. Each is now the whole font as Google Fonts releases it for its project in `google/fonts` at `bf7c667a`, converted to WOFF2 with nothing else changed (fontTools 4.57.0's woff2.compress; OFL-FAQ 2.2.1): Orbitron (16,028 bytes, was 11,800; Google Fonts' variable port), Playfair Display and its italic (106,440 and 103,728, were 38,404 and 38,804; built from the designer's sources) and Press Start 2P (29,920, was 12,512; the 2016 update of its designer's 2.14), each with the OFL.txt beside it there, unchanged, so Orbitron's license now states the Reserved Font Name its font declares, which Fontsource's left out. Decoding each file gives back every table of the original byte for byte, except glyf and loca, which WOFF2 rebuilds with every glyph the same, and head, whose checksum and one flag WOFF2 sets; an empty signature stub, which WOFF2 carries none of, is gone. Text looks the same: every character the subsets had keeps its outline and advance at every corner and midpoint of the fonts' weight axes, and in Chromium every ASCII pair, the line metrics and drawn lines are identical; characters the subsets lacked (Cyrillic, Greek, Vietnamese and symbols such as ★ ♥ † ‰) now come from these fonts instead of a fallback. `tests/canvas-preview-fonts.test.ts` reads each preview font's own copyright notice and glyph count (`tests/woff2-font.ts`) and fails when a family that reserves a name ships fewer glyphs than its whole font or a file named as a subset, or its license leaves out a name the font reserves; the byte pins in `previewFontList.ts` and `tests/saas-font-licences.test.ts` and the notices follow the new files.
- Ship the preview fonts' licenses with the hosted app (third-party notices follow-up 2026-10-16). Running previews of delivered pages get 17 brand font families from AwwO: 26 Latin subsets in `apps/web/src/canvas/fonts/`, under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, each family with its own license beside its files, which `src/canvas/previewFonts.ts` inlines as data: URLs, one script chunk to a face. The hosted build shipped no license text with them: each face carries only its copyright notice and a link to the license in its own name table, which OFL-FAQ 1.10 calls legally sufficient but strongly recommends against, and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` did not mention the fonts. The build now starts every chunk that holds one of them with the license of the font's family, unchanged, as a comment (an output banner, added after minification, which strips comments, and covered by the chunk's hash; other files change only where they name those chunks), and fails when a font of that folder has no license (each face takes its family's, by `src/canvas/previewFontList.ts`, never another family's), ships in any other file (also one copied into the output, such as from `public/`), or in none (`inlinedFontLicences` in `apps/web/scripts/font-licences.mjs`). The notices name the families, their source (Google Fonts' subsets, byte for byte as the Fontsource 5.3.0 packages ship them, checked against the registry's tarballs), the licenses and the three Reserved Font Names: "Playfair Display" and "Press Start 2P", which their licenses declare, and "Orbitron", which the copyright notice in Orbitron's own font file and Google Fonts' license of it declare, although its Fontsource license leaves it out. The API image and the native release archive carry the 17 licenses with the other notice files. `tests/saas-font-licences.test.ts` pins the licenses to Fontsource's bytes, runs the hosted build config on the preview fonts, checks each face's chunk for its license and that no other chunk starts with one or with a line break, and covers the refusals, also in real builds (a preview font emitted as a file, shipped nowhere, or copied in from `public/`).

A canvas fits its overview once the stage's first size arrives (it can arrive late, as in a tab opened in the background); a node opened before that kept its camera, and closing it glided back to the camera the canvas started with: with none saved, the app's default, which may not show the graph at all (pre-existing, left from the review of the sidebar fix). The two files it replaces were Google Fonts' subsets, which the SIL Open Font License counts as modified versions, and a modified version may not use the name the license reserves ("Mona") without the copyright holder's written permission. `apps/web/src/saas/design/fonts/mona-sans-wdth-wght.woff2` is GitHub's `googlefonts/variable/MonaSans[wdth,wght].ttf` at the commit Google Fonts serves it from (version 2.000, the file the subsets were cut from), compressed to WOFF2 with its font data unchanged, which the license's FAQ allows to keep the name; its license is now GitHub's `OFL.txt`. Text looks the same: every character the subsets covered has the same outline and advance, and Chrome draws Latin text and digits pixel for pixel alike. Only where Latin Extended letters meet Latin ones, which used to come from two files, is kerning now applied across them. One 171 KB file now covers the characters of the 98 KB and 33 KB subsets, and draws ‰ as well, which they lacked.
- Ship Mona Sans's license with the hosted app's fonts (third-party notices follow-up 2026-10-16). The hosted build emitted the two Mona Sans font files the design tokens name but not the SIL Open Font License beside them in `apps/web/src/saas/design/fonts/`, which asks that every copy of the fonts carry it, and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` did not mention the fonts. The build now writes `LICENSE-mona-sans.txt` beside the font files it emits, and fails when a font of that folder would ship without it (`apps/web/scripts/font-licences.mjs`; `tests/saas-font-licences.test.ts` runs the hosted build config on the fonts). - Ship the third-party notices with the API image and the native release archive (open-source intake follow-up 2026-10-16). The image held only the binary and the archive only AwwO's own `LICENSE`, although the binary embeds built-in skills adapted from MIT and Apache-2.0 sources and links Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause and MIT Go modules. Both now carry `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, `LICENSE`, every license and notice file the notices name and the new `third_party/go-modules/`, at their repository paths: the image under `/usr/share/doc/awwo-api/`, the archive under `licenses/`. `third_party/go-modules/` holds the license, notice and patent files of the Go standard library and of the 36 modules the binary links on linux/amd64, copied unchanged from the module cache by `scripts/awwo-go-licences.ts` after checking each module against `backend/go.sum` (whatever build tags, experiments or amd64 level the caller's environment sets), including the licenses below a module's root that cover a linked package or a file it embeds (client_golang's gddo code) and those beside it (yaml's `LICENSE.libyaml`, the `NOTICE` and `PATENTS` files), and the READMEs there that grant a license or name one that no license file above them grants (fiat-crypto's BSD-1-Clause is the README of Go's `nistec/fiat`; perks' and goautoneg's repeat their licenses). A compiled or embedded file whose own text grants a license, for code its module took from elsewhere, or names one that the license files of its directory and those above it do not grant, in that variant (an SPDX expression; a license named in prose, before "license", after "licensed under" or a "License:" label, or in capitalized words before "license", where a BSD clause count or an Apache version, in the name, after it or on the next line, must match; a copyleft, content or font license; a bundled script's `/*!`, `@license` or "Released under"; even wrapped across comment lines), gives the comment or literal that holds it, as a lexer for its kind of file finds them (`//` and `/* */` with string literals, `#` with triple-quoted strings, `<!-- -->`; a `/*` inside a string opens none, and an escaped quote or backtick ends no literal), or its run of comment lines, with the copyright notice above it, or the whole file when it has none there or is plain text, byte for byte, as `<file>.notice` (33 files: Lucent and Vita Nuova's MIT notice in Go's `runtime/memmove_amd64.s`, the Sun and Cephes notices in 20 of Go's `math` files, fiat-crypto's BSD-1-Clause in two of its crypto files, the public-domain dedications of SLEEF and the Rijndael reference code, protobuf's well-known types, client_golang's copy of beorn7/floats); finding them is heuristic: a file that took code from elsewhere under its module's own license, or names another license in words the script does not know, is not found. Every file copied there (58 distinct texts, all read for this change) is pinned by its SHA-256 to the licenses a reviewer recorded, which the README's labels come from, so a new or changed text stops the script with a hint (what it reads like, or the copyleft term or advertising clause it mentions) until someone has read it, and a linked object file stops it too; so is each file a reviewer left out, which the README lists with why: Go's own README, whose Creative Commons license is the Gopher image's, and BoringSSL's license, for an object the binary never links without cgo. `npm run check:go-licences` fails when that directory is stale; the image build fails when it builds for another target than linux/amd64, or when the binary's Go toolchain or modules (path, version and `go.sum` hash, from `go version -m`), or Go's `LICENSE` and `PATENTS`, differ from it; the release build uses the toolchain modules.txt names (GOTOOLCHAIN), runs both checks and refuses to build while the notices name a license or notice file it would not carry or the commit lacks. The bundle is never written or read through a linked directory, a hard-linked file is replaced rather than written through, and `.gitignore` no longer drops its files (`runtime/` matched Go's `src/runtime`). `scripts/awwo-saas-release.test.ts` covers the bundle on a fixture module cache (nested, embedded and in-source licenses, their directory scope, READMEs, files left out, go.sum tampering, unreviewed and stale texts), exact writes and linked directories, the real module cache against a real build under a hostile `go.work`, the notices' references in document order (backticked, in table cells, as link targets, and bare names beside the path before them in the same paragraph, list item or row; also missing ones), the archive copy (identical on every run) and the image's copies and build context.
- Open a node clear of the canvas assistant's sidebar. In the hosted workspace on a screen up to 1280 px wide (any workspace up to 900 px), the sidebar lies over the board's left edge while the stage still spans the window. An opened node, and the overview, were fitted to the whole stage, so with the assistant open the node's left third sat under the sidebar: the first words of every line of its task card and its acceptance criteria could not be seen. Found on production 2026-10-15, in a signed-in check of that day's canvas-assistant release. Fits now measure how much of the stage's left edge the sidebar covers (`sidebarCover`: its layout width, without its entrance slide; nothing where it takes its own room beside the stage, is closed, or leaves no room for an open node at a readable scale, as on a phone where it spans the stage) and place the open node and the overview in the part right of it; a saved camera the canvas opens on is kept only if that part shows the whole graph (simple mode opens the assistant with the canvas), and no overview is fitted over a node opened before the stage's first size arrived. That part can be narrower than the 900 px below which a stage opens nodes in its narrow layout (on the production stage of 1232 px, 834 px are left beside a 398 px sidebar); the narrow layout stays a narrow stage's, so beside the sidebar a node keeps its frame, sized to that part, rather than turning into the 520 × 380 card zoomed in with its delivery over the conversation; the narrow layout takes the part's width on a narrow stage, and also where that part has no room for an open frame. Where Configure raises the board above the sidebar (the hosted app at 900 px and below), nothing is covered while it is open, and 查看全部节点 and 整理布局, which close it, fit the board as it is afterwards; where that part has no readable room for a node beside Configure, the node opens as without the sidebar, clear of the panel in use. Showing or hiding the panel refits the overview and an open node, like a rail toggling, as long as the camera is still the one the app set; a refit meeting the camera on its way back from a closed node judges where it lands (also in the instant between the glide's last frame and the render showing it), and saves the camera it returns to, never a frame on the way, as the operator's (nothing when that camera was the app's own). Verified: twenty-three cases in `tests/canvas-surface-fit.test.tsx`, six of them on a fake clock (beside a sidebar the frame fits the part right of it; with no sidebar the corner stays where it sat; a sidebar spanning the stage, beside it, or leaving no readable room is not counted; one mid-slide is measured where it lands; the assistant opening over an open node moves it clear, and closing gives the stage back; the overview recentres right of it; a saved camera with the card under the sidebar is not kept, and a node opened before the first size keeps its camera; the refit mid-glide and after the last frame, the camera saved as before, the operator's camera saved when its own save was still waiting (also between the glide's last frame and its render), the app's not saved; with Configure raising the board a configured node keeps clear of the inspector, and 查看全部节点 and 整理布局 fit the board without it, and beside Configure with no readable room left the node keeps clear of the inspector; at the production size the node keeps its frame layout, 778 px wide; on a narrow stage, or beside a sidebar leaving no room for a frame, the narrow layout takes the part's width at 100 %), twenty-six of twenty-seven mutants of the fix caught (the last is equivalent: wherever Configure raises the board, a configured node already opens as without the sidebar); ten adversarial review rounds, each round's findings fixed and tested; in a browser on the local stack at 1244 × 900 in both modes, 1920 × 1080, and 880 × 900 with Configure and 查看全部节点.
- Open a node with what it was given and made in view, in either mode (owner request 2026-10-15: opened nodes did not show their context in full, and developer mode's own views read poorly). An opened node kept its saved card size (at least 520 × 380, plus a 320 px delivery drawer) and opened zoomed up to 125 %, so a page's preview was about 294 px wide and a long brief or prompt was cut to a few lines. It now opens at 100 % in the room its content can use on the stage: a page up to 1680 px wide, a delivery 1440, a picture, clip or 3D model 1200, a conversation 1100, at most 1100 high, less the Configure panel's room while that floats beside it, its frame and its camera taken from one measurement. It takes its new room when the stage changes shape, Configure opens or closes or its first delivery arrives, while the camera is still the one it opened with (never one the reader zoomed or panned); a node resized larger by hand keeps its size. Its delivery drawer takes the share of the width its delivery needs (a page 62 %, a document 52 %, a picture or clip 48 %, a conversation 38 %) and is open once the node has delivered unless the reader closed it there (now remembered: closing a drawer that had opened by itself used to be dropped, and toggling it no longer widens or moves the saved node), though never by itself where it would cover the conversation (a narrow stage, a frame under 740 px) or beside a failed run's partial delivery; a hand resize of an open node resizes its open frame, a view choice like the camera, to any size (also below the size the node was saved at) and kept while it stays open, instead of saving a screen-fitted size into the node; a delivery that is code (a module, a constant, a data literal, JSON, a stylesheet, markup, Python) reads as monospace code with every line kept, where Markdown ran it into one paragraph (a module that opens with a comment, an interface, a call with a template literal or a tile map with `~~~` rows included; an answer that fences its code, lays out Markdown or quotes code in its sentences stays Markdown). The top of the conversation says what the node was asked (its task, the model it runs, its acceptance criteria and how many constraints it follows; one line while its inputs are open), with 「让助手修改」, which starts a request about it in the canvas assistant's composer, and a failed run says why, with 「重新运行」 and 「让助手调整」. The simple view can open a node's inputs to fill them in (without their field structure); conversations read 对话 2 rather than "Session 2"; a written input, a media prompt, a persona and each task requirement grow with their text instead of being cut mid-line; Configure says what the persona is for; the task card offers 展开 whenever its clamp hides text (measured, not guessed from its length), and a display opened from a card is placed beside the card and clear of an open node's frame; an opened node's conversation keeps room for its message box, the task card, a failure note and the inputs giving way first. Verified: `canvas-open-node-content` (new, in test:saas), `canvas-surface-fit` (refits, Configure and camera ownership), `canvas-node-disclosure` and `saas-assistant-orchestration`, the new cases mutation-checked (42 mutants, all but one caught: the local test canvas cannot show whether 「继续运行」 with nothing left started a run, only that it says so); screenshots of eight case canvases in both modes at 1920 × 1080 and 1366 × 768.
- Choose the runtime every node runs its model on automatically, and never show it (owner decision 2026-10-15, after every node of the case tutorials had to be switched to “OpenAI Agents JS” by hand in developer mode). The server already set up a node with no runtime on openai-agents, but the web showed an unset node as Pi in its Configure panel and saved Pi once a model was picked there, listed every model once per runtime in a node's model picker (the Pi entry first; choosing an effort in Configure now also moves a node set up on another runtime to the one whose levels it offers, where saving kept Pi and node setup refused a level only OpenAI Agents has, while a team keeps its runtime and is offered only that runtime's levels), and gave the nodes the canvas assistant adds the assistant's own runtime, which for a Bedrock model is always Pi (only the Pi worker serves Bedrock to the assistant's direct tasks). On Pi a Bedrock call that has sent nothing for 300 s is cut off and a reply cut at the output limit reads as a runtime failure; Claude Opus 5.5 thinks longer than that before it writes. Now `nodeRuntime.ts` runs a model on openai-agents wherever a ready worker offers it, on Pi only otherwise (the Bedrock models without tool support), and that choice is made everywhere a model is chosen: a node's model picker and the model rail list each model once, the hosted Configure panel picks a model and its reasoning effort (in words: 低/中/高 …) with no runtime control, the case copy dialog names models without a runtime, and the assistant's nodes take its model on the node runtime. A canvas run also sets every node it executes up on that runtime, whatever an older canvas saved (a message typed to a node keeps its conversation where it is), and falls back to Pi when openai-agents is not ready for a model. Teams, workspace Agents and media nodes keep their own. The runtime is named “OpenAI Agents” where it still appears (the team editor): production serves it with the Python SDK worker. Verified: `tests/saas-node-runtime.test.ts` (new), a run that sets a Pi node up on openai-agents and leaves a Pi-only model on Pi (`saas-canvas-initialization-surface`), and the updated picker, shelf, copy-dialog and assistant-model tests.
- Show each picture a delivered page names in the 成果 (Results) studio: every image node calls its first picture `image-1.jpg`, and the studio matched a page's `<node id>/image-1.jpg` by the file name alone, so every chapter, colour or scene of such a page showed the first image node's picture (seen on production 2026-10-15 while re-recording the Neon City tutorial: all three chapters showed Rooftop garden, although the page names three different files). The studio now picks a page's files as a node's own preview already did (`pickCanvasFile`: the node folder first, then the name), and no longer answers a page with itself once its real name is known.
- Give a free image, video or 3D generation back when its provider never took the task (owner decision 2026-10-15, after a user's 「图片和视频额度就1次呢，没法试用诶」 and a day of refusals: X-tasy turned the operator's key away from 2026-10-14 ~23:30 +08 until the new key at 02:21Z, and Video · Standard has answered `MODEL_NOT_FOUND` since). A free generation now spends the workspace's media allowance, its daily total and the free ceilings once it is sent to its provider (`submitted_at`, set just before the request) unless the provider refuses it outright for a reason on the operator's side, creating no task (`provider_refused`, `refusedAnswer`: an error answer to the submission naming the operator's key, its balance, a model the provider no longer has, a request the service built wrong or the credit ceiling; X-tasy, Tripo and RunningHub), or while it is still queued or running, so concurrent admissions still hold (`generationCounts`, migration 029). Such a refused generation, or one whose run ended before it was sent, cost nothing and gives its attempt back; one refused for its own prompt or settings keeps counting, so a refused prompt cannot be sent again and again for free, and so does a submission whose outcome is unknown (a timeout, a lost answer, a cancel or a restart while it was in flight), a refusal that answered a resend (X-tasy sends again after an answer that never arrived, so an earlier send may have made the task; the HTTP transport no longer resends a submission by itself, so every resend is counted) and a generation the provider accepted, even if it failed or was refunded afterwards. Marking a generation sent locks its run and checks that it is still queued or running, so a cancel and the submission cannot both pass.

A saved node on either moves to All-round or Ultra HD batch Pro the next time its canvas opens (`RETIRED_MEDIA_MODELS`), with that model's default settings; recorded runs are untouched. A copy of a homepage media case now starts its clip on All-round, with the case's own 16:9, 5-second, 720p, silent settings, instead of on Video · Standard (`productionWorkflows.ts`; the cases' recorded runs and their pinned canvas text are unchanged).

A row put its node, the inputs it still needs and its 「去填写 / Fill in」 side by side, and the node's column (`minmax(0, auto)`) grows to its title's full length before the inputs' `1fr` column gets any room, so a long node title took the whole row: in developer mode's 330 px panel “Frontend: pixel platformer page with keyboard controls” left “API contract” a 0 px column, 191 px tall, and simple mode's 420 px panel did the same.
