Checked in the local SaaS dev server at 1920×1080 (developer mode: every row's inputs on one line, 197 px wide in English and 189 px in Chinese; simple mode: 287 and 279 px), at 1280×800, 768×1024 and 375×812 in developer mode (English), and with a label that has no break opportunity (it wraps inside its column); `tests/canvas-assistant-next-steps.test.tsx` checks the rule, as jsdom has no layout.
- Give three.js r128's missing CapsuleGeometry to every running page that uses it, under any name. The preview and the case dialog added it only where a page wrote `THREE.CapsuleGeometry`, so a page that reaches the library through an alias (`const T = THREE`, then `new T.CapsuleGeometry`) stopped at its first capsule: the Mars mission control case stayed black in AwwO, and the car plant drew its capsules as cylinders, unlike its cover. The pre-release check of the new cases found it; their own browser checks had supplied the addition to every page.
- Run the canvas assistant's direct tasks on Bedrock models for real: after the change below went live (2026-10-12 22:17Z) they still failed, in about 200 ms (22:23Z, Opus 5.5 and Haiku 4.5). The cause was the request, not the process: the managed-execution engine opens every task's thread with its own greeting, so its first request is the system prompt, an assistant message (`Hi, I'm AwwO workspace. What would you like me to do?`), then the user's message, and Converse requires a conversation to open on a user turn, so the bridge refused it before any network call (`The conversation must start with a user message`). Qwen took the same request. A Qwen direct task asked to list what preceded its user message showed the shape on production (22:43Z); the bridge refusal reproduced locally, and the same request without the greeting answered from a workstation through Bedrock (Haiku 4.5, `max_tokens` 32000, the seven workspace tools). The Pi worker's Bedrock request for managed execution (`bedrockOpening` in `apps/computer-model.ts`) now carries such an opening's text as context at the end of the system prompt and starts the conversation at the first user message; an opening that called tools is left as it is and still refused. Verified: a new managed-execution test (the production shape reaches Converse at its user turn with the greeting in the system prompt, later calls of the task replay their tool turns, an opening with tool calls is refused by kind before any request), 18/18 managed-execution tests, and the Pi worker and bridge suites (88 pass; the Windows-only http-boundary test cancelled as before, the child test skipped below Node 24).
- Run the canvas assistant's direct tasks on Bedrock models, Claude Opus 5.5 included: on production every one failed within milliseconds (2026-10-12, 14:47-15:07Z: Opus 5.5 and Haiku 4.5 on the Pi worker, while Qwen tasks and Opus 5.5 components ran), though the same request through the same bridge and SDK worked from a workstation against real Bedrock. The one difference from a Bedrock run, whose calls work, was the process: a run's calls are made in an isolated child, a direct task's were made in the worker itself, with its whole environment and Node options in reach of the AWS SDK. A managed-execution Bedrock call is now made in an isolated child too (`apps/pi-worker/bedrock-call.mjs`, `bedrockComputerCall` in `runner.mjs`): forked with no Node options and only `workerEnvironment`'s variables, it gets the credentials the worker resolved and the one request over private IPC, gathers the stream into one answer and exits; an abort stops it. A failed call now says why by kind only, never with provider text, in the worker's reply (`error.reason`, e.g. `bedrock:403:AccessDeniedException`, `stream`, `child-exit:1`) and in one log line (`computer_model_bedrock_failed`). Verified: 5 new worker tests (the child's environment and arguments with AWS, proxy and `NODE_OPTIONS` variables set in the parent; failure reasons; abort stops the child; the real child module; the call in process over a fake Converse SDK), the 3 managed-execution Bedrock tests through the new call, and the whole Pi worker suite. This was not what made those tasks fail (the entry above has the cause); the isolated call stays.

Every one of the 27 videos carries notes, 31 in all, from the day's audit of every video against this changelog: the 17 build videos' Configure step (AwwO has picked an Agent node's runtime itself since 2026-10-15, so an agent's Configure has no runtime menu, and Claude Opus 5.5 offers no effort there; each agent may take 25 minutes since 2026-10-19; and the canvas assistant can set each agent's task, acceptance criteria and model instead); the EV plant digital twin and Neon Circuit racer cases, rebuilt on three.js r186 with a 3D model node (2026-10-15); what the canvas assistant's card says on a fresh copy of Umber, Backprop and Errand (one, one and two nodes without a result, not none), Roost (six, not four) and PALLWARD (48, 43 of them media nodes, not three) since 2026-10-20; THE LONG CHORD as Episode I (2026-10-22): 298 nodes over 93 graph runs, and a copy with 282 pictures, clips and sounds to make again, about 64,000 credits of media by `mediaCreditsFor` over the case canvas's own settings (more than six months of the Max plan and more than any plan makes in a day), where the video says 104 and about 24,000; and in the four how-tos the links between a direct task and a plan for the canvas, gone since 2026-10-19 (a correction in words hands a request over), and the code how-to's recap on refunds (a platform time limit gives back only the call it cut, since 2026-10-19). What the how-tos show of the free plan holds until the promotion ends on 2026-10-29. Verified: `saas-academy` (every note inside its video, in order, dated no earlier than the recording, in both languages, naming no provider; THE LONG CHORD's count against its case's record, and its credits, months of Max and a day's generations recomputed from `plans.go`'s price table and plans; the dialog lists the notes in English and Chinese, plays from a note's time and brings the video into view, keeps the focus there, takes a play() without a promise and a refused play, and plays nothing for a video that did not load), and in Chrome on the dev server with the staged motion files: English and Chinese, 1440 and 390 wide, a note's 7:06 played the video from 426 s, and the notes' text, date, heading and times at no less than 11.3:1, 6.7:1, 11.3:1 and 13.9:1 in every appearance style.
- Add a built-in skill that gives a node real prop measurements, `physical-props` (owner request 2026-10-23: put a public simulation-grade asset library to use in AwwO). Scenes and layouts fail on numbers rather than on shading - a forklift drawn the size of a car, a rack a person could step over - and a node has no network, so a warehouse floor, robot cell, production line, shop or office was placed on figures the model chose, unless someone had handed it real ones (the web reader can). The skill carries 26 measured rows (footprint, height, mass and rigid-body count: a 1.36 x 3.73 m counterbalance forklift 2.17 m high at 1730 kg over 32 bodies, a 1.21 x 1.00 m pallet, a 3.10 x 0.70 x 2.50 m shelved rack bay, a 1.17 m conveyor against a 0.99 m packing table, two grippers, two robots, and the loose props down to a 0.2 kg carton), says one scene unit is one metre and which footprint number is the long side, and asks for every lane, pitch and lift to be arithmetic from the props placed and written into the delivery (a forklift lane at 1.36 m plus the clearance stated on each side; two 1.21 m pallets and 0.68 m of upright across a 3.10 m bay, overhanging its 0.70 m frame by 0.15 m each side, so the aisle is measured from the load; a floor level and two 0.80 m beam levels in a 2.50 m bay, leaving 0.59 m of load on the lower two, 0.69 m on the top and 0.10 m spare; the 0.18 m lift from table to conveyor). It is as strict about what the table does not carry - no clearance, load capacity, reach envelope, turning radius or payload rating - each of which a node must name as its own assumption or as a figure to source, never derive from a size: that a 2.16 m arm stands taller than a 1.81 m top deck, or the 1.52 m collaborative robot shorter than it, says only where each bounding box ends, since an arm reaches above its own height when extended; the grippers' 6 kg and 14 kg classes are their makers' ratings read off the asset names, and what the table does settle is that either lifts the 0.2 kg carton or the 1.9 kg crate and neither comes near a 62 kg pallet, so pallets move by jack or forklift. It says mass is the asset's own figure and not a weighing, names two rows whose figure is plainly high for the real object and leaves the reader to judge the rest, requires any correction to be said out loud, and requires a bill of materials in the delivery naming each prop's holder and licence (owner decision 2026-10-23: attribution belongs in the delivered document, never in AwwO's interface). The figures are the ones a public search service returned for those props on 2026-10-24, from a pinned dataset revision, figures only with no asset, texture, metadata text or page text copied, so nothing of that library is distributed with AwwO and no licence text travels with the skill: its `attribution` is empty, as for every skill AwwO wrote itself, and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` carries the provenance and each row's holder and licence instead. `skills/README.md` now states that third case (facts only, whatever the source's licence), which it did not cover. The built-in library now has 33 skills. Verified: `TestBuiltinSkillsAreValid` (the format, the 7,588-byte body under the 8,192 limit, the Chinese labels, no hidden text), `npm run check:skill-licences` (unchanged, since no source text is adapted) and `npm run test:saas:engineering` (49 pass). One adversarial review raised 14 findings, the blocking one being that an earlier draft concluded a reach from a height in the very item forbidding it; every finding is answered above or in the skill.
- Run AwwO 本地版, the local edition: the hosted product's own services on one computer, for one person, with their own keys (2026-10-21; owner: 「复刻线上awwo的所有内容，开始开发本地版」, then 「开始」). `npm run setup:local` downloads what is missing (Node.js 24.22.1, checked against its release's SHA-256 values; PostgreSQL 18.4 on Windows, pinned to the archive's SHA-256), installs each service's packages as its hosted image does (workers without dev packages or install scripts) and the Python worker, builds the API, the hosted web app and the managed execution's core, and, with Docker running, the workspace image; `--staged-videos` also brings the Academy's videos and THE LONG CHORD's film, each checked against its SHA-256. `npm run local` starts PostgreSQL (127.0.0.1 only), Pi, the Python OpenAI Agents worker (the JavaScript one when Python is not usable), the managed execution and the render worker where this computer can run them, the API in personal-key mode, and a web server that does what the hosted nginx does (`/api/v1/` only, its headers, its 404s) under a name of the data folder's own (`awwo-<instance>.localhost`, which awwo.localhost sends the browser to), so a session cookie reaches no other local server or instance; it keeps the data folder private to its account (on Windows an access list for its SID and SYSTEM alone, read back by SID; elsewhere mode 700; a folder of another account, or one with other content and no `local.env`, is refused), never makes the vault key again for an existing database, runs one runtime per data folder and keeps setup from replacing what a runtime runs (locks of the operating system's, which go with their process, so none is ever left to take over), gives the owner a workspace on the first start, and speaks the JSON-lines contract `apps/macos/AwwOLocal.swift` already has for a desktop window. Each service runs under a wrapper that ends it, and what it started, when the runtime goes away, so a killed runtime leaves no service holding its port or working on, and ends what a service started and left running when it exits by itself; a required service that stops ends the runtime. A stop ends the API first and in order, on Windows too (its stdin closes), then the workers, the instance's workspace containers and PostgreSQL, and reports a database or containers that did not stop. The sandbox runtime is not offered: the API refuses it with personal model connections. A contract test runs the built API on the settings of every optional-service and media-key combination. `docs/awwo-local-edition.md`; `npm run test:local`.
- Stop the API in order when its standard input closes, with `AWWO_STOP_ON_STDIN_CLOSE=true`: the same stop as on SIGINT or SIGTERM, for a supervisor that has no polite signal to send a console program (AwwO 本地版 on Windows), so a media submission in flight still records its task id (2026-10-22, review of the local edition). Without the setting nothing changes. Test: `backend/cmd/api/main_test.go`.
- Give AwwO 本地版 its own shape in the same web app (2026-10-22; owner: 「开始 M2 … 循序所有内容」). The API takes `AWWO_EDITION=local` (it needs personal keys, refuses ClawHunt sign-in and checkout, and names the data folder, `AWWO_LOCAL_STATE_DIR`) and `AWWO_REGISTRATION=closed` (any deployment: `/auth/register` answers 403 `registration_closed`); `/auth/options` and `/auth/me` say the edition, `/auth/options` whether accounts can be made, and `GET /api/v1/local` (platform administrators, local edition only) tells where the data is and which optional services run, with no key or token. The web app then shows 设置 → 本机 in the place of 用量与计费 (the data folder and how to back it up, providers.env, the services and what each needs, the version; links to the plans or invite pages open it), offers no plan anywhere (the upgrade card, the Opus 5.5 invitation, the usage meter and the canvas's upgrade step stay out), hides the sign-up and the administration links, offers the tutorial without requiring it, offers no invitation (no one could accept it), and in 数据管理 imports the file the hosted site's 导出我的数据 saves: one new workspace per active workspace in it, then each canvas through the API, one at a time, each first detached from the hosted workspace (its nodes' agents, sessions, threads, workspace skills and every delivery or value naming its files or media are cleared, so the nodes are set up afresh on their first run; plain text deliveries stay), with what the API refused listed and the import ended by an ended session or an API that stopped answering (a cut-short export or one from a newer AwwO is refused; generated media and uploads are not in the export, and the page says so); the deletion request becomes a note on deleting, or copying, the data folder. A forgotten password, with no mail to recover it by, is replaced by `npm run local -- --reset-password`: a new one in local.env and admin-credentials.txt, set on the owner's account as the API starts (`AWWO_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_RESET=<reset id>`, the local edition only, applied once per id), which ends the account's sessions; a start that fails before the API leaves the next one to finish it. Closed registration is refused beside ClawHunt sign-in, whose first sign-ins it could not stop. The hosted site, where the edition is unset, is unchanged but for the two new fields. The local runtime sets all three and builds the web app without a ClawHunt main-site link. Tests: `backend/internal/app/edition_test.go`, `apps/web/tests/saas-local-edition.test.tsx`, `scripts/awwo-local.test.mjs`.
- Install AwwO 本地版 on Windows: **AwwO Local** (`apps/windows-local`, a Tauri window with an NSIS installer for the signed-in account; 2026-10-22, owner: 「开始 M2 … 然后要替换线上的本地版下载」). The installer carries the runtime and everything it runs (its own Node.js 24, PostgreSQL 18.4 with the Visual C++ runtime beside it, the API, the hosted web app, Pi, the JavaScript OpenAI Agents worker and the renderer) and keeps the account's data apart, in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\store.clawhunt.awwo.local`, so an update or an uninstall leaves it. The window starts the runtime with its protocol (`--events --stop-on-stdin-close --parent-pid`, `--shell windows`), shows its progress, opens AwwO at the address it reports (and, at the first start, `admin-credentials.txt`), keeps only that address and its own status page in the window (the status page at its own navigations alone, by a token of its process in the address, and never in a popup; other addresses and mail addresses open in their program through the Windows shell's handler, not a command line), shows the error a runtime stopped on, and stops the runtime in order when it closes (after four minutes it ends it and the PostgreSQL it left). Its AwwO menu restarts, opens AwwO in the browser, the data folder and the logs (a folder with no secret in it), and resets the sign-in password. `--quit` asks a running window to stop and exit, or stops the database an ended run left: the installer's hooks use it before an update or an uninstall, wait until nothing runs from the installation, then remove the old files whole; they refuse an installation folder outside the person's profile and %LOCALAPPDATA% (one elsewhere takes its drive's permissions, under which other accounts may change its programs) or past 80 characters, or one whose path holds % or ! (PostgreSQL starts its server through cmd.exe, which reads them), and at every start, before it runs anything of the payload, the window refuses an installation, payload, code or build folder another account may change, read where it really is (a junction's target), and a link at any depth of the payload (whoami and PowerShell given 60 seconds each; a pass kept for the run, a refusal checked again at the next start). `npm run package:local` assembles the installer's payload (what the hosted images run, laid out as a checkout; workers' packages installed as their images install them, without their dotfiles, type declarations, source maps, and, where a path would pass 170 characters, a `dist-es` that the package's exports keep Node.js from loading, which is then loaded to prove it), refuses one that holds private configuration, a link, a path too long for Windows, a relative import it does not hold or a program import a fresh Windows would not have, starts its own runtime on a scratch data folder with `--smoke`, and builds the installer, in a folder of its own with `--out` for a checkout too deep for makensis. With `AWWO_LOCAL_SHELL=windows` (the local edition only) `/auth/options` and `/api/v1/local` name the window, and the sign-in page and 设置 → 本机 name its menu where a checkout's person would run an npm command. The runtime now takes its folders without a Windows `\\?\` prefix (from which PostgreSQL's programs cannot find each other: every installed start failed so) and runs PostgreSQL's tools with English messages (in Chinese Windows' code page they read as mojibake), gives them a path that is not ASCII in its short (8.3) form when the volume keeps one, as the window gives its pg_ctl (they get their paths in the system's ANSI code page, a character it has not as "?"), and makes the cluster's own databases SQL_ASCII and AwwO's UTF-8 from template0, checked so at every start: initdb writes its share folder's path into SQL it runs, which a UTF-8 database refuses unless it is ASCII, so on a Chinese account's %LOCALAPPDATA% every first start failed. It refuses, naming the folder, a path that PostgreSQL's shell would read (cmd.exe's % and !, /bin/sh's $ ` " \), and says what to do when PostgreSQL does not start from paths that are not ASCII. The payload carries PostgreSQL's server alone (its programs, their libraries and data files, and of its modules those the server loads itself: PL/pgSQL, Snowball's stemmers, the encoding conversions, replication's, the event log's), without any extension (AwwO creates none, and some carry code of others under terms of their own, as uuid-ossp's OSSP uuid, fuzzystrmatch's Perl-licensed dmetaphone and pgcrypto's parts do), contrib's two programs oid2name and vacuumlo, its programs' translations (the runtime runs them in English), its Perl, Python and Tcl languages, what extensions are built with, StackBuilder with the wxWidgets and curl only it loads, and ICU's test plugin, and with every module its catalog files name (`$libdir/…`), carries Visual Studio's VC++ runtime when it is as new as the tools that built PostgreSQL (with none here that new, only a build to test, `--test-build`, carries System32's), leaves out the workers' packages built for other systems and the coding agent's clipboard, which no worker uses, and carries its licences, stopping on any it cannot find: AwwO's notices as the hosted release carries them (the Go modules' checked against the API it carries); each of the workers' npm packages', listed in `licenses/npm/NPM.md` (permissive licences only), those a package does not ship taken from its README or its repository (`third_party/npm-packages`, by `scripts/awwo-npm-licences.mjs`); those of the 245 crates the window's program links, with Rust's standard library's and the WebView2 SDK's (`licenses/apps/windows-local/`; `third_party/rust-crates`, by `scripts/awwo-crate-licences.mjs`); PostgreSQL's, with the notices of the code of others in its own source (regex, pg_dump, Snowball's stemmers, the Unicode tables, Ryu, md5, sha1, sha2, src/port's BSD and ISC files…), as Debian's postgresql-18 package lists them and as the headers of 18.4's own files have them (NOTICES.txt, made from the source release checked against its published SHA-256), each of its libraries' own from its release, MinGW-w64's runtime notices for the three DLLs its GCC built and the programs zlib is built into (`build/pgsql/LIBRARIES.md`; EDB's notices lack ICU's licence and zstd's copyright line; `third_party/postgres-windows`, by `scripts/awwo-postgres-licences.mjs`, each DLL checked by its SHA-256, the modules in lib by who made them, PostgreSQL by its `postgres -V`) and the GNU source releases of libintl and libiconv, under the LGPL (setup:local downloads them, checked against their SHA-256s); Node.js's. The fetching scripts take a file only when it is of the licence its package names, by words of the licence's own text (the first fetch had taken a repository's Apache licence for an MIT package), record where each came from in PROVENANCE.json, and check their folders with `--check`, as the packager does before it carries them; a build to test's installer is named `…-setup-TEST.exe`, and `--keep-payload` takes only a payload this packager assembled from the same commit with no change in the checkout. Every Node.js service, and the Node.js programs it starts, refuses a module whose real path is outside AwwO's own folders, the code, the build and the data folder (`scripts/awwo-local-module-guard.cjs`, however the module was reached: a package's folder above them, a junction, a main pointing elsewhere, an imports map; loaded by NODE_OPTIONS; pi-worker, openai-agents-worker and openmaus-worker, which start their runs, the core and its MCP shim with no Node options, give them the guard alone when the runtime names it, `AWWO_LOCAL_MODULE_GUARD`, unset on the hosted site): Node.js looks there for a package's absent optional dependency, and any account can make `C:\node_modules`. The uninstaller's 「删除应用程序数据」 removes the data only once a second prompt naming it is answered Yes, and the installer does not downgrade. Found by the install tests and fifteen rounds of two reviews: Tauri's resource globs flatten a folder and its paths lose their drive letter, makensis reads no path past 260 characters, Tauri's own installer ends a running app at once, and initdb stops on a Chinese installation folder. Not in the installer: the Python worker, the Academy's staged videos, ffmpeg and the workspace image (直接执行). Tests: `scripts/awwo-local-package.test.mjs`, `scripts/awwo-local-licences.test.mjs`, `apps/windows-local` (`cargo test`), `backend/internal/app/edition_test.go`, `apps/web/tests/saas-local-edition.test.tsx`, `scripts/awwo-local.test.mjs`; docs: `docs/awwo-local-edition.md`, `apps/windows-local/README.md`.
- Read web pages and the skill registry through a proxy on this computer, with `AWWO_WEB_READER_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<port>` (development only, as AwwO 本地版 runs; providers.env takes it), as strictly as directly: the site's name is resolved here, every answer must be a public address (a fake-IP answer, 198.18.0.0/15, or a name this computer cannot resolve is refused too, since neither says where the site is), and the proxy is asked for a tunnel to that address (`CONNECT ip:port`, IPv4 first, the next address when the proxy cannot reach one, the exchange bounded to 10 s), never to the name it would resolve again by itself; TLS still checks the site's name, and the proxy is the only address dialed. A proxy setting is checked as exactly `http://127.0.0.1:<1–65535>` (no leading zeros), by the API and by providers.env. In the local edition the skill registry then says what kept skills.sh out of reach (`skill_registry_network`) instead of "try again later"; the hosted site's answer is unchanged. Unset, nothing changes, and no proxy variable is ever read (2026-10-22, for computers that reach some sites only through a local proxy; review: the first design let the proxy resolve the name again). Tests: `backend/internal/webread/proxy_test.go`, `backend/internal/app/edition_test.go`.
- Label a workspace container with its AwwO instance when the worker is given one (`AWWO_WORKSPACE_INSTANCE`, label `awwo.workspace-instance`), so that instance can remove what a stopped worker left on a Docker daemon others share (2026-10-21, for AwwO 本地版, which removes its own at every start and stop; review of the local edition). Without the setting nothing changes; the managed execution's broker passes it on.
- Reach the DeepSeek API as a third operator platform beside LLM Gate and Bedrock (2026-10-21; owner: 「看下这个，我们应该怎么融入到awwo中，帮我们节省成本」, then 「其他我全部允许，开始吧」). `AWWO_PLATFORM_PROVIDERS` takes `deepseek` in the API and in the Pi, JS and Python workers (canonical order `llmgate,bedrock,deepseek`). A profile whose provider is `deepseek` reaches only `https://api.deepseek.com` with Chat Completions, only with operator credentials, and in Gate-only mode only where the policy names `deepseek`; its key is read only from `AWWO_DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` (a DeepSeek profile names it, a DeepSeek default model reads it instead of the worker's own key variable, no other profile may name it, and a DeepSeek key that is another profile's key stops startup, with or without a DeepSeek profile). A DeepSeek profile cannot enable `structuredOutput` (DeepSeek has no `json_schema`), cannot list thinking levels when it switches thinking off, and on the JS worker lists no level but `none`; anything else stops the worker at startup. Health declares the platform as it does Bedrock, and the API refuses a DeepSeek model outside a worker's declared list or behind a Gate-only claim. The API offers DeepSeek models only explicitly: to a workspace whose model allowlist names them or that a platform administrator owns, never to a workspace only because it has no allowlist (the privacy clause does not name DeepSeek; whether users' work may go there is the owner's decision), so for now only the operator's own workspaces see them (`tenant_models.go`, `explicitOnlyProvider`); a DeepSeek planner model (`AWWO_PLANNER_MODEL`) plans only where the workspace may use it, elsewhere the plan runs on the default model, and a picture never moves a run onto one it may not use (`runs.go`, `vision.go`); and the last gate before every model call checks a DeepSeek call against the live allowlist and owner again, whoever pays for it, so a grant withdrawn mid-run stops the next call (`teams.go`). A profile that switches thinking off sends DeepSeek its own `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` instead of the chat-template switch it ignores (Pi now takes the switch on a DeepSeek profile, and `AWWO_PI_DISABLE_THINKING` on a DeepSeek default model). Managed execution streams DeepSeek calls, and takes the effort `none` as DeepSeek's no thinking where the profile lists it. In the two tool loops that call a model many times (managed execution, and the sandbox's project execution), DeepSeek runs without thinking: its API wants every earlier reasoning of a tool loop sent back with each later call, which neither loop keeps; a thinking level a call asks for there is refused, never dropped, and a profile's default level is dropped. The Python worker now asks every stream uncompressed: DeepSeek compresses a stream whenever the client accepts it, and the worker's usage tap reads raw bytes, so every live DeepSeek call failed `MODEL_PROTOCOL_ERROR` before; it follows no redirect from the DeepSeek API. Nothing changes until the settings name `deepseek`, except that the Python worker asks every provider for an uncompressed stream from the moment it is deployed. Verified against the real DeepSeek API from the real Pi, JS and Python worker code and from managed execution. On the hosted planner's own prompt, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash's plans applied cleanly in 5 of 5 scenarios, at 1/3 (thinking) to 1/6 (no thinking) of Claude Haiku 4.5's cost. See `docs/awwo-deepseek.md`.

A video plays in the dialog beside what it shows and what comes up next. A case's video opens its case in the case library on the page ("Open the case"), which then shows every case and gives the focus back to the case's card; on a page with no case library it is a link to the workspace's home page with the case open, as a homepage case now opens from `?case=<id>` too (`caseLink.ts`, `ProductionCases.tsx`). The videos (1.39 GB) are in no release: each is staged once on the host under `/showcase/staged/academy/<first 16 hex digits of its sha256>.mp4`, which the dev server serves from `AWWO_STAGED_SHOWCASE`; only the four how-tos' posters ship (`showcase/academy/`), a case's video showing its case's cover. Act I (5 min 43 s, 1680×720 at 24 fps, with dialogue in sync, a score and 31 English subtitles) was made on the live AwwO in the operator's workspace by one canvas of 109 nodes over 33 graph runs: 33 pictures, 45 clips, 20 takes and 6 score cues; two editor agents (Claude Opus 4.8), who wrote the reels' timelines; and three edit nodes, which cut the reels and joined them. A recorded case's canvas is the run's own document, stored beside its record (`apps/web/src/saas/production-canvases/<case>.ts`, pinned by `canvasSHA256` over `recordedCanvasText.ts`), not a workflow compiled from tasks, because its briefs and timelines name files by node id. A member's copy is that canvas, made only while it still hashes to the record (`recordedCanvas.ts`), with nothing pre-filled. The copy dialog says that the copy's first run makes every picture, clip and sound again, and that the sync sheets and the act's timeline were measured on the case run's clips. No release carries the film. The web copy (43 MB) and the file as delivered (151 MB) are staged once on the host under `/showcase/staged/<case>/<sha16>.mp4`, checked by their SHA-256, never overwritten and listed; nginx already serves that path from its store of earlier website files. The dev server serves them from `AWWO_STAGED_SHOWCASE` (`apps/web/scripts/staged-showcase.mjs`). Tests: `saas-production-film`, `saas-staged-showcase`, and the film case in `saas-production-runs`, `saas-production-copy` and `saas-production-cases`. Docs: docs/production-cases.md, Film cases.
- Find a skill on skills.sh, the open directory of agent skills, and import it into the workspace's skill library (owner 2026-10-19: 「把这玩意装给awwo」, of vercel-labs/skills' find-skills). find-skills itself cannot be a node skill: it has an agent run `npx skills find` and `npx skills add`, and a node's model has no shell or network (a sandbox computer has both, but a skill installed there would stay in that run's sandbox), so the library does what it describes. `GET /skills/registry/search` asks skills.sh's public search as its command-line tool does, `GET /skills/registry/preview` reads skills.sh's copy of the skill, the security reviews skills.sh publishes and the source repository's license and stars on GitHub, and `POST /skills/registry/import` saves SKILL.md's text as a workspace skill through the checks an uploaded file gets, with its source and license recorded (migration 041, `tenant_skills.attribution`, kept through edits). Only the text is kept: the files that come with a skill are listed, never stored or run, and the preview says when a skill expects to run commands; a skill whose text is over 12 KiB or holds hidden characters is refused, and so is an import whose text, license, notice or README files or repository license changed since its preview (`skill_registry_changed`, after which the page reads it again). Many skills there are not open (Anthropic's document skills declare themselves proprietary, all rights reserved; many repositories have no license file), so a skill is imported as it is only when its SKILL.md declares, at the top of its frontmatter, a permissive license AwwO recognizes (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC and the like; every item of a list the same one), or declares none and GitHub recognizes its repository's license as one, and nothing else in it speaks of terms: no other key naming a license or terms (nested, `licenses:`, `license-file:`, `Terms of Use:`, `restrictions:`), no comment or other key's value that reads as terms, no license file of its own under any name (`LICENSE2.txt`, `COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.md`, `COMM-LICENSE.txt`, `ACME_EULA.pdf`, `ACMELicense.pdf`, `LEGAL.md`, `TERMS.md`, `ACME_TERMS_OF_USE.md`, an `ACME_TERMS.md` that reads as terms (a glossary does not), a translation such as `LICENSE.cs`, any file of `LICENSES/` or `legal/`, a license-named file a folder down outside asset folders such as `fonts/`, `data/` and `templates/`, a plain `LICENSE` in `docs/`; a text can carry a permissive license's words and terms of its own, and names of code such as `license_check.sh` do not count), no line of its body or of its folder's README (in any language) that names its license, copyright or terms (a heading, also after an emoji or a number, a label such as `**License:**`, `License – …`, `Legal:` or a link, a table cell, "Licensed …", "Terms and conditions", `© 2026`, `Copyright Acme`, in markdown or HTML), no SPDX line, "all rights reserved", "commercial or non-commercial" use or license terms in its prose, and notice files (NOTICE, COPYRIGHT, third-party notices) that only credit. A declared license that forbids reuse (proprietary, non-commercial, no derivatives, confidential, CC BY-NC or BY-ND) makes it restricted, and so do such terms in a license or notice file, read there as phrases (a proprietary license, non-commercial use), with the any use a permissive license allows ("for any purpose, commercial or non-commercial") set aside, and not in a GNU license's text, which names proprietary programs among what it governs (a notice carrying one asks). Texts are read with what draws nothing left out (hidden formatting characters, soft hyphens, variation selectors) and every run of white space, a line break or a no-break space as one space, and markdown with the markup between its words (emphasis, entities, tags) left out and its code blocks, as CommonMark reads them, set aside as examples. Any other skill, proprietary, unlicensed, copyleft or unconfirmed, is imported only once the member has read its terms (every license and notice file is shown) and confirmed they may use it (`licenseConfirmed`, else `skill_registry_license_unconfirmed`), and its attribution says so (`skill_registry_license.go`). Only the API asks (`backend/internal/app/skill_registry.go`, through the web reader's public-address client, as `AwwO-Skills/1.0`); each answer is read within one of the server's four request slots and cut to copies of what a member is shown (at most 64 KiB of a SKILL.md, 16 KiB of each license file, 100 file names), then cached (a search 1 minute, a skill 5, a repository 6 hours, reviews 30 minutes; an expired repository answer stands in for up to a day while GitHub cannot be reached or its allowance is spent, and any other answer leaves the repository unchecked); the server follows one redirect, between skills.sh and www.skills.sh. An account's registry requests count against 20 a minute what they fetch (a search 1; a preview or an import 1 for each of the skill, its repository and a preview's reviews that the caches do not hold and the service has not asked AwwO to wait for, at least 1) and run at most two at once, a preview reading the repository and the reviews one after the other; the server asks the two services 120 times a minute (burst 30), and a 429 or GitHub's spent allowance stops the asking for as long as the service says, at most an hour. A preview reads the skill first, so an id skills.sh does not have asks GitHub nothing; a reply to an older pick is dropped in the page, and while an import runs the library's other controls and Escape stay closed, and a dialog the browser closes itself opens again. Off unless `AWWO_SKILL_REGISTRY=on`; the library's 「从 skills.sh 查找」 appears only then, to members who can edit (`apps/web/src/saas/SkillRegistry.tsx`). skills.sh's terms allow reasonable use of its public API and encourage caching; its robots.txt disallows crawling `/api/`, and AwwO asks only when a member searches or picks a skill.
- Make a speaking shot: a video node takes voices, and the video made from references moves the speaker's lips to them (M-1c, 2026-10-19; owner: 「RunningHub已充值，继续做完直接上线」, for THE LONG CHORD). A video node has a third input, 「声音参考」 / "Voice reference" (`audio`, several wires), for audio nodes' results; a canvas run puts their file lines with the pictures', each kind in canvas order, and the words call them @Audio 1..3 (`graph_contracts.go`, `graph_media.go`, `apps/web/src/canvas/ports.ts`). The wire is a hard one: a voice node that failed holds the video back. 「视频 · 多图参考」 / "Video · From references" (`rh.seedance-2-multimodal`) takes up to three (`audioReferences` in the catalogue), wired or attached to its message as MP3 or WAV: each is uploaded to RunningHub's file store like a picture (under a neutral name) and sent in the task's `audioUrls` beside its `imageUrls` (`runningHubAudioField`). A voice a video cannot use refuses the generation at admission, before anything is counted or paid for, so a speaking shot is never made without its line, with a code and message of its own, 「声音参考用不了」 / "The voice reference cannot be used" (`media_voice_unavailable`, never retried): on that model, a fourth voice, a type other than MP3 or WAV, one over 10 MB, one under 2 s or over 15 s or voices over 15 s in all (RunningHub's limits, each read from the file's own headers: a WAV's data chunk over its byte rate, an MP3's Xing/Info or VBRI frame count or else its bytes over its bit rate, `media_voice_length.go`), or a voice with no picture beside it (RunningHub reads a voice only beside a picture); and a voice wired into a video whose model, the one the canvas run froze from its bound agent, takes none, or a voice node that delivered no voice (`wiredVoicesUsable`). An audio file attached to the message of a model that takes no voices is left out, as any file it does not read is, so a song attached for the mood still never refuses a video. The clip RunningHub returns carries no sound of its own when the node's sound is off (the operator's probe: picture only, 6.04 s at 24 fps), so an edit lays the same take on its dialogue track. The model also offers its real-person switch, 「真人模式」 / "Real people" (`realPersonMode`, sent off unless a node turns it on, as leaving it out behaved): without it RunningHub refuses a photorealistic person (code 1505), which refused THE LONG CHORD's character shots on 2026-10-19, and that refusal now has its own code and message, which says to turn the switch on (`media_real_person_rejected`). Its `verified` date is 2026-10-19, from the operator's two probes (6 s at 480p from two pictures and one voice; the second sent the request exactly as the API does, the switch without `conversionSlots`, whose documented default is all slots). Voices and the switch change neither a generation's credits nor RunningHub's rate ($0.60 for those 6 s, its 480p rate). The voice port's guide says what the node's model does with voices and their limits, and names the models that take them when it takes none; the composer of the model that takes them says an attached MP3 or WAV is a voice; an audio node's result guide names the video's voice input and an edit's sounds. Rolling back the API leaves a canvas with a voice wired in, or with a node whose switch is on, refused as a whole when it is run (the earlier graph check has no such input, nor the earlier catalogue such a parameter), and a video already queued with voices fails at its upload, uncharged; rolling back the website drops those wires at the next save. The composer notes of the subject-reference model now say that any other file attached stops the generation (as it did since 2026-10-17: leaving it out would renumber the pictures), where they said such files are not used. Tests: `media_voices_test.go` (new: a Postgres canvas run uploading a picture then a voice and sending them in imageUrls and audioUrls with the switch on, then refusals unsent: a voice without a picture, a voice wired into the text-only video, a voice node that failed; the freezing rules; the prompt's lines and the graph's wiring rules; the 1505 code), `media_voice_length_test.go` (new: MP3 constant and variable bit rates, MPEG-2, tags, WAV, and what has no length), `runninghub_refs_test.go` (the catalogue entry, the request with voices, the catalogue's refusals, the voices' upload names), and the web's port, wiring, composer, guide, settings and error-text tests.
- Join a canvas run's clips, sounds and pictures into one film (M-3, migration 040; owner 2026-10-19: 「继续往下做吧」 and 「RunningHub已充值，继续做完直接上线」). A canvas could make pictures, clips, voices, music and sound effects, but nothing joined them. A new node, 「剪辑」 / "Edit", takes a timeline (`awwo.timeline/1`: an agent's answer wired into its timeline input, or written on the node) and the clips, sounds and pictures wired into it, and the render worker makes the film with ffmpeg (`apps/render-worker/edit-*.mjs`; the API's side in `backend/internal/app/edits.go`, `edit_worker.go`, `edit_outputs.go`): cuts, crossfades and dips to black, pictures held, HTML title cards; dialogue, music and effects placed by time or anchored to a shot, levelled, ducked under the dialogue, muted in silences and brought to the film's loudness and true peak; subtitles. Every piece is checked to the frame and joined by stream copy, in one colour description (BT.709, limited range, each piece converted from its own). The node delivers the film like a generated clip, with its subtitles, a report and stills for a vision check, so a later node takes it. Every input is opened as the container its own bytes show, from local files only; the worker gets only stored files the nodes wired in produced. A workspace runs one edit at a time and 40 a day (400 site-wide, UTC day; the platform's failures are not charged), and an edit runs only in a cloud run. Migration 040 adds `edit_jobs`, the allowance's ledger. The worker's edit routes are its own release, switched after the API's: until then an edit fails as unavailable, uncharged.
- Let an operator delete an account (`awwo-control delete-account`, `backend/internal/operator/deletion.go` with its checks in `deletion_plan.go` and its writes in `deletion_apply.go`; runbook in `backend/README.md`, "Deleting an account"). A deletion request could be marked handled only once the account was gone (migration 038), but a plain `DELETE FROM users` was refused by seven foreign keys: memberships, audit actors, invitations sent and accepted, run actors and the two graph tables from migration 007. The command runs in one transaction and is a read-only preview without `--apply` (which needs OS root); a retry of the same operation returns the first receipt. Each workspace the person alone owns needs a choice: handed over to one of its members (whose membership is then dated at the handover, so it pushes none of their own plan workspaces out of their plan), or deleted with everything in it. The workspace the account was created with (named after the person at a first ClawHunt sign-in, or by them at sign-up; found by its creation date, the account's own) is handed over only with a name given (`--rename-workspaces`, plain text that starts with something to see; its own name again keeps it, unless it ends in " · AwwO" as a first ClawHunt sign-in's does), since no route renames a workspace. Without `--request-id` (a request sent by email) the command refuses while the account has a pending request in the app (to be named, so that it is marked handled) or when its latest one was withdrawn or declined, unless `--supersede-request` names that latest one as superseded, which the record keeps. As the owner chose (2026-10-19), the person's work in the workspaces that stay is kept without their name: runs keep their outputs and messages with no actor, and the graph rows whose actor is required become the workspace owner's; the person's invitations are deleted; audit rows stay with no actor, so the request's record survives. The command refuses while ClawHunt's subscription is live in `user_plans` (it must be cancelled at ClawHunt first), for a day after a checkout or billing portal opened from AwwO, while the person or a workspace to hand over or delete has anything running (a web import, managed dispatch or TypeSafe evaluation that was never settled counts only as long as the API itself treats it as running), and for a platform administrator. It takes its locks in the API's own order (the workspaces it hands over or deletes, the account's deletion requests, the account, its plan mirror and plan watch, each new owner's membership), so a withdrawal, a plan sync, a checkout's plan watch or a member's removal that got there first is waited for and then seen, and one that comes later waits for the command and then runs on what it left (a withdrawal, a plan sync or a checkout's plan watch finds the account gone); a checkout opened while the command runs still gets its ClawHunt page (the API asks for it before it records the watch), so the runbook has the operator look at ClawHunt again a day later. A deleted workspace's knowledge goes last: migration 021's trigger on knowledge origins is switched off for one statement and back to its state before the commit. A later ClawHunt sign-in creates a new account: the identity link goes with the old one. Tests: `internal/operator/deletion_test.go` covers every refusal (each leaves the database as it was), the kept work, replays, the knowledge-origin trigger (back to its state afterwards), two handovers to one member, renames, and the locks (an admission, a withdrawal, a plan sync, a checkout or a member's removal committed while the deletion waits is seen and refused; a membership gained then is deleted with the account); it also pins every reference, trigger, workspace table and column named like a user id that the tool depends on. 96 mutants of the tool were each killed by the tests. `internal/app/account_deletion_test.go` builds an account through the API, deletes it (its first workspace handed over under a new name) and marks the request handled through the 038 handler, then signs a ClawHunt account in again after the plan wait. The API, website and workers are unchanged: only `cmd/control` uses the package.
- Pro and Max are shown as credit vouchers on the plans page (owner 2026-10-19: 「用户在这里的对于购买套餐的欲望太低。要做出来 coupon 这种质感的东西，兑换券的感觉，要吸引他们购买」). `apps/web/src/saas/PlanVoucher.tsx` + `plan-voucher.css`: each plan's monthly credits as the face value (面值), what it gives, a decorative serial, and a tear-off stub with the price and the way to buy (「立即开通 Pro」 / "Get Pro", with 「按月订阅 · 可随时取消 · 由 Stripe 安全支付」 under it) or to switch, along a perforation with two notches; Pro in the theme's live teal, Max in its gold and lilac; the plan the account holds stamped 「使用中」 / "Active"; a sheen on hover (none with reduced motion); in a narrow column the stub goes under the text; forced colours keep the face value readable; only the design system's tokens, so every appearance style colours it. Every figure is the server's catalog (GET /billing), Max's "5× the credits of Pro" included, and nothing claims a discount: a subscriber's bigger plan says that a mid-period upgrade charges only the prorated difference and adds its credits, a free account reads that the credits arrive once the payment goes through. Where a run is refused for want of a plan, `PlanUpsell` is a small voucher too, its stub capped so its text never narrows to a sliver.
- Link the license texts of the code the hosted app ships (third-party notices follow-up 2026-10-18). Since the 2026-10-17 web release the site serves them at `/third-party-licenses.txt` (the file `apps/web/scripts/bundle-licences.mjs` writes to the root of the site), but no page linked it, so a visitor could reach it only by knowing the address. The sign-in page now ends with 「开源许可」 / "Open-source licenses", after the cases (also while the sign-in methods cannot be read), and the workspace's 更多选项 / More options menu has the same item; both open the file in a tab of their own, as the PDF preview and the skill library open theirs, and their tooltip says so. The dev server (`npm run dev:saas`) answers that path with the committed `apps/web/src/saas/bundleLicences.txt`, which only the build writes out, so the links open it there too instead of the page Vite falls back to. `apps/web/tests/saas-licences-link.test.tsx` checks both links in both languages, the footer's place, and the dev server's answer.
- Make a video from reference pictures (M-1a, 2026-10-17): a new video model, 「视频 · 多图参考」 / "Video · From references" (`rh.seedance-2-multimodal`, RunningHub's multimodal route of the Seedance 2.0 family), starts from up to 9 pictures, so the characters, ships and places of a film keep their look from shot to shot. The pictures a video node's message attaches, or its reference input brings, are frozen at admission as for the other providers (PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 10 MB each) and, before the task is submitted, each is uploaded to RunningHub (`runningHub.uploadReference`, `POST /openapi/v2/media/upload/binary`, free and creating no task); the answer is read strictly (code 0, an https `download_url` without credentials, at most 2048 bytes) and every failure is a closed code, the transient ones tried again. The URLs go in the request's `imageUrls` in order (`runningHubReferenceField`, written with the fixed fields; every other RunningHub model's body is unchanged), and the catalog check allows pictures on a RunningHub model only where such a field is named, and no parameter or fixed field on it. The model offers resolution (480p, 720p; 1080p not until it has been measured), duration (4–15 s), ratio (default adaptive), sound and seed; reference video and audio, real-person conversion and the last frame are neither offered nor sent. One real generation with the operator's key on 2026-10-17 (two reference pictures, 720p, 5 s: 261 s, $1.00, billed by the second; the same knight as the pictures, in the scene the words asked for) set its price at three times that, 300 credits per five seconds, and its `verified` date. The catalogue marks it `referenceMode: "subjects"`, so the composer and the reference port's guide say every picture, a single one too, is a subject reference that words can call @Image 1, @Image 2 (never a first frame). Tests: `runninghub_refs_test.go` (new: the entry, the request with and without pictures, the catalog refusals, the upload against the fake RunningHub's new upload route, a Postgres run uploading two pictures before its submission and one failing at its upload unsent), and the web's composer and wiring-guide tests. Verified by that generation.
- Run a canvas node again by itself when its run failed for a transient reason (Canvas RSI loop 1, R-1 of the 2026-10-17 design): a worker or provider that was unavailable, busy or rate limited, a refused admission, a dropped stream, a lost workspace, and the media provider's unavailable, busy and missing-result codes (`media_failed` only when the provider charged nothing). The node goes back to waiting, says 「自动重试中（第 n 次，共 m 次）」 / "Retrying automatically (n of m)", and is admitted again after 15 s, then 30 s, 60 s and at most 120 s, through the same admission as any node, so every attempt is a run of its own, counted and billed as one; its downstream nodes wait for it as for a node still running. Limits, refusals, refused content, cancelled and interrupted runs, admission refusals and (since 2026-10-18) a run timeout are never retried. `AWWO_GRAPH_NODE_RETRIES` (0 to 5, unset 2) bounds it per node and 0 turns it off; anything else is refused at startup. Migration 036 adds each graph node's `attempts`, `retry_at` and `attempt_log` and two workspace-scoped tables, `canvas_experiences` (one row per retry, settled to succeeded or failed with the node) and `canvas_lessons` (for the later loops). Graph runs report each node's `attempts` and `attemptLog` and the graph's `nodeRetries`; a run's archive names its node's attempts, and the graph evidence export collects the earlier attempts' runs.
- Add two built-in video skills, written from what 703 prompts for videos made as code have in common (owner request 2026-10-16: add the awesome-opus5-5-videos collection to AwwO's capabilities; ideas only, since each prompt is its creator's own post): `code-video-brief` has a node write a one-page brief before any code (format and the render size and length to pick, the facts it may show and a "Do not claim" line, the look and a banned-effects list, motion, a beat-by-beat timeline with every word on screen, a sound cue sheet for the editor since AwwO renders picture only, the frames to check), picks among motion graphics, explainers, 3D scenes and builds shown as video (a build's state is rebuilt for every t from a fixed script; a canvas video is seeked inside `renderAt`), and gives on-screen words three roles (poster words, captions, labels) with reading holds; `vertical-reel` tells the member to render at 1080 x 1920, gives approximate safe areas around a feed's buttons and caption and 9:16 text sizes that replace promo-film's landscape ones (keeping its 96 px side margins), the first seconds, sound-off reading, landscape footage as cards rather than crops, rhythm by length, how to cut a reel longer than AwwO's 20-second render into parts that join cleanly in an editor, and the ending. Both are in AwwO's own words (no shared five-word run with the collection) and credited as ideas only in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. A reel's node can attach all four video skills (with code-motion and promo-film) within one node's 20 KiB skill budget, and `TestBuiltinSkillsVideoSetFitsOneNode` keeps it that way. The built-in library now has 28 skills.
- Read a web page from simple mode (owner request 2026-10-16: 「普通模式也加上从网址读取」). The web reader was reachable only from developer mode's knowledge map. A simple-mode canvas now shows 「从网址读取」 in its canvas bar when the server reads the web (`apps/web/src/saas/CanvasWebReader.tsx`): one public address read by the same server reader, with its allowance (the count is always the server's, read again on opening and every minute while the day's reads are used up) and its refusals in words. The page is saved to the workspace's knowledge, and 「加入任务」 adds it to what the canvas's next tasks cite and drafts the assistant's request. The server first checks the whole selection as a plan or a run would (`GET /knowledge/context?revisionIds=`: at most eight, 64 KiB in all; `knowledge_context_limit` is now said in words), so a page too large to carry is refused in the dialog, not when the task starts. Both the knowledge map and simple mode show the one selection the bridge holds (`useCanvasKnowledgeCount`), so references set in one mode stay visible, and clearable, after switching to the other.
- Build a page from its modules without a model: the `assemble` node kind (owner request 2026-10-16 for flagship cases, which need pages of 150 KB and more while every case page was capped near 42 KB because its last node re-typed all modules in one 32,000-token call). Each `{{in:<input id>}}` slot of its template takes that input's exact text; a value that is one code fence goes in without its fence lines, and inside `<script>`/`<style>` closing tags and `<!--` are escaped (the same 18 vectors pin the Go and TypeScript code, `backend/internal/app/testdata/assemble_vectors.json`). No model, run or quota; it settles in the same graph pass as its inputs. It can also deliver the page as a file, stored as the canvas's artifact, for a sandbox node downstream.
- Let a node run code and its tests: the `sandbox` runtime, chosen node by node in the node's settings (never AwwO's automatic choice). Served by an OpenAI Agents worker in project-execution mode (`AWWO_SANDBOX_AGENTS_URL`, `AWWO_SANDBOX_AGENTS_TOKEN`, which need `AWWO_WORKSPACE_CALLBACK_URL`), the node reads its inputs as files, writes code, runs commands in a Docker sandbox and delivers real files, every model call admitted and settled like project execution's. Migration 034 widens the runtime checks.
- Make the sandbox workspaces able to read and build with real tools (owner request 2026-10-16: REA in AwwO). A 直接执行 task now gets the uploaded files its message names in a read-only `/inputs`; `AWWO_OPENMAUS_WORKSPACE_TOOLS` / `AWWO_OPENAI_AGENTS_WORKSPACE_TOOLS` (`rea`, `check-page`) tell the agent about programs the image has; and `backend/cmd/egress-proxy` gives workspaces a controlled way to the web: the container stays `--network=none`, a read-only socket mount and a per-run proxy password reach public addresses on ports 80 and 443 only, within a per-run traffic allowance (`AWWO_WORKSPACE_EGRESS_DIR`, `AWWO_WORKSPACE_EGRESS_SECRET`; `docs/awwo-workspace-web.md`). All off until configured.
- Add four built-in skills for building large products in a clean room: `clean-room-spec` (a behaviour spec with every statement observed, inferred or unknown, the only thing that passes the wall), `build-from-spec` (one module to its contract, registering commands, tests and planted failures), `self-test-oracle` (`window.awwoSelfTest` with planted failures the checks must catch; run with `awwo-check-page` in the sandbox) and `rea-app-reading` (REA's static analysis of a JavaScript or Electron app, in the sandbox or 直接执行).
- Give canvas nodes skills: method guidance a node carries into every run (open-source intake 2026-10-15). A library of 26 built-in skills ships in the API binary (`backend/internal/app/skills/`): 12 written for AwwO (motion drawn in code with a `window.renderAt(t)` render contract, shot directing, promo films, video breakdowns, a neon pixel scene, web research, trend digests, criticism, product specs, data analysis, copy editing, hand-off summaries; five of them adapt MIT or Apache-2.0 material, credited on each and in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`) and 14 adapted from wshobson/agents (MIT, credited on each). A workspace can write its own or import a SKILL.md file (`/skills`, versioned, archived rather than deleted). A node lists up to four in Configure (`document.nodes[].skills`, at most 20 KiB together); admission freezes each skill's exact text, version and hash into the run's snapshot and adds it to the system prompt behind a guard, with `</skill` escaped. A node without skills sends byte-identical requests. Developer mode's Skills tool reads each skill in full and writes, imports and archives the workspace's own; beside an adapted built-in skill's source it links the license texts of its sources (`apps/web/src/saas/skillLicences.txt`, generated by `scripts/build-skill-licences.mjs`, checked by `npm run check:skill-licences`).
- Keep workspace memory: short notes (preference, fact, decision, lesson, style) for one canvas or the whole workspace (`/memory`, compare-and-set edits, at most 200 per scope). When a node or a canvas run is admitted, its pinned notes and the ones that best match its task (at most 12 notes, 4 KiB) are frozen into the snapshot and quoted at user-message priority as background data, never as instructions; a note that disagrees with the task loses. Notes are written or confirmed by people (a proposed note waits); nothing is captured silently. A workspace without notes sends byte-identical requests. Developer mode's Memory tool lists, confirms, pins, edits, archives and deletes them.
- Import a knowledge source from a web address (`POST /knowledge/sources/web`, `backend/internal/webread`), off unless `AWWO_WEB_READER=on`. The server reads one public page as `AwwO-Reader`: http(s) on the standard ports to a registered host name, every resolved address checked when it is dialled (no loopback, private, link-local, reserved or mapped addresses), each redirect validated again and robots.txt honoured (RFC 9309), one 20 s deadline and 5 MiB, a site's challenge page refused rather than worked around. The readable text (or a feed's entries) becomes an immutable source whose provenance records the fetch (addresses, redirects, time, status, raw-byte digest, robots verdict). Each read is recorded before anything is fetched and counts against 30 a workspace and 2,000 a site per day (under a site-wide lock), failed ones included; a second request for an operation still reading is refused, one finished meanwhile answers from the stored result, at most four pages are read at once, and a read a crash left open is settled at the next start.
- Render a delivered page as a video (`apps/render-worker`, `/canvases/{id}/renders`), off unless `AWWO_RENDER_URL`, `AWWO_RENDER_TOKEN` and `AWWO_MEDIA_DIR` are set. The worker opens the page the deliverables studio built in Chromium, freezes it at every frame (exactly with `window.renderAt(t)`, on a virtual clock otherwise), encodes an MP4 with ffmpeg and optionally a GIF and a contact sheet; the API checks each file's digest and type and keeps it as the canvas's media. One render at a time per workspace and at the worker (the others wait queued, and a worker still freeing itself is asked again), 20 a workspace and 300 a site per day under a site-wide lock, 0.5–20 s and 1,800 frames; renders the worker never took (busy, down, the API restarting, stopped while queued) are not counted. The outputs are checked before anything is stored and kept with the completed job in one transaction; the render rows outlive their canvas as the allowance's ledger, and a canvas cannot be deleted while it renders; a restart or shutdown marks unfinished renders interrupted instead of rendering twice. The studio offers it as 渲染为视频 on a page to members of an active workspace.
- Add 39 wshobson/agents roles (MIT) to the team market's role picker, exported from a vendored, provenance-pinned snapshot (`third_party/wshobson-agents`, `npm run check:market:wshobson`).
- Add engineering guard rails: the AwwO laws (`docs/laws/awwo-laws.md`), a review brief template, `npm run check:hygiene` (CR, control and invisible Unicode in source, with a reasoned allowlist), `npm run doctor:saas` (read-only toolchain and environment checks) and their tests (`npm run test:saas:engineering`), plus `npm run test:saas:render`. `GET /capabilities` tells the web app which of the new abilities a server offers and how much of today's allowance is left.
- Make the page a hosted canvas's assistant adds deliver itself (found by running the real planner prompt on a local Qwen 3.5 27B, the class of the production default planner, 2026-10-15: asked for 「网页版贪吃蛇」 it added a frontend node with the template's three outputs, delivery notes, a preview link and checks, and kept them even when its server instructions spelled out the remove_field and add_field steps; every case tutorial had set that node's output by hand in developer mode). On a hosted canvas a frontend node a plan adds is now the page itself: one html output (`page`, 网页) and, unless the plan writes one, a page's brief (one complete HTML file that works when opened, the code wired into it pasted unchanged, no notes, code locations, preview links, servers or accounts). The planner is shown the frontend template that way, and its server instructions say to deliver a page, game or tool with one frontend node and add no fields to it. A frontend node already on a canvas, one added by hand, and a canvas outside the hosted app keep the template. The same run showed the reply to a plan that only set a node's acceptance criteria also saying its constraints had changed (a node without task requirements compared unlike an empty frame); it no longer does. Verified: `saas-plan-orchestration` (a hosted and a local frontend node, the planner's view of each), `saas-assistant-orchestration` (change lines), and the local planner rerun, which then made a one-page html node.
- Let the canvas assistant set what developer mode was opened for (owner request 2026-10-15, after every case tutorial opened developer mode midway to pin down each node by hand: its task, its acceptance criteria, its runtime and model; a beginner only talks to the assistant). A plan can now set a node's task requirements (`set_task`: its constraints and its acceptance criteria, each list replaced as given, within the task frame's own limits) and its model (`set_model`: a model the workspace offers, by id or name, or "default", with an effort level the model advertises; the runtime is AwwO's), and a new node takes acceptance criteria in `add_node`. The planner now sees each node's constraints and acceptance criteria (a request copied to several nodes once, named @R1 …, and kept by that name), its model, whether it delivered and how its last run ended, and the models nodes can run; the hosted planner's server instructions tell it to write each persona as a self-contained brief, give every new node checkable acceptance criteria, size every node for one model call (a page node with exactly one html output fed compact code parts, split past about 16,000 characters) and fix a failed node by splitting or narrowing it, or by the default model when a premium one was refused. The reply lists what the canvas now holds under the model's summary (nodes added, removed and renamed, tasks, criteria, constraints, inputs, prompts, models, wires). The 接下来 card offers 「让助手调整画布」 for a failed node and 「让助手帮我填写」 for the inputs a run still needs, each sent as a message the reader sees; its 「去补全」 now opens the node on its input drawer (the Configure panel it opened has no input fields); and a message that only asks to run the canvas (「运行」「跑一下」「run it」, or 「继续运行」 for what is left) runs it as the run button would, instead of reaching a planner that cannot run anything: 「继续运行」 runs the nodes that have not run, or after a failure the failed ones and what they feed, and with every node done runs nothing and says how to run it all again; a message with a number in it (「run 2」) is left to the assistant, never read as the whole canvas. The plan gate (`planning.go`) admits the new operations within the same limits and progress names them; the task frame's 12,000-character total is left to the canvas, which leaves an oversized step out with a note instead of the gate refusing the whole plan, and a model name is counted in characters on both sides. A new node the plan puts on the workspace default (`set_model` "default") keeps it, where the canvas assistant's own model used to replace it. Found by an adversarial review (Codex, two Claude reviewers, then a second round on the fixes) before release. Verified: `saas-plan-orchestration` and `saas-assistant-orchestration` (new), `planning_orchestration_test.go` (new) and the gate's operation pin; the planner context stays within its 16,000-byte budget, and the recovery journal's budget was re-set to 6,400 characters for the larger protocol.
- Give running pages brand fonts, put the canvas's 3D models into the r186 cases, and publish case media as static files (R1b of `docs/commercial-cases-audit-20261014.md`, §7; owner request 2026-10-15: 接着做 R1b：字体、媒体、GLB 模型). Fonts: AwwO now supplies 17 OFL-1.1 families to every running preview (the strict preview, the live page, the case dialog and a canvas's Results): Inter, Space Grotesk, Manrope, Outfit, Montserrat, Unbounded, Orbitron, Exo 2, Oxanium, Rajdhani, Bebas Neue, Playfair Display, Instrument Serif, Cinzel, JetBrains Mono, Press Start 2P and Pixelify Sans, the Latin subsets of the Fontsource 5.3.0 packages (26 files, 747 KB, vendored byte for byte with each family's license in `apps/web/src/canvas/fonts/`, size and sha256 pinned in `previewFontList.ts`). A page that names one in a font-family, a style (its quotes written as entities too), a canvas font string, a font shorthand (sized by a length, `var()`, `calc()` or `clamp()`) or an SVG attribute gets it as an @font-face with a data: source ahead of its own styles (`previewFonts.ts`, through `loadPreviewLibraries` under `PREVIEW_FONTS_KEY`, which waits at most 20 s for them before running the page in its fallback fonts); no request is made, so the type is the same in mainland China, where a page's Google Fonts link never loads, and a page that names none gets nothing. A case canvas opts into naming them in its page rule (`OfficialWorkflow.fonts`). Media: a media case's files are now static files beside the case footage, named by their content (`showcase/media/<case>/<sha256-16>.<ext>`, listed in `production-runs/<case>.media.json`), fetched when its dialog opens (`loadProductionMedia`), instead of base64 data: URLs inside JavaScript (`*.media.ts`, about 4.7 MB over three cases); the files and the manifest listing them load all or none within two minutes, and a dialog whose files could not all be loaded shows no page, with Try again, rather than a page with missing pictures; `publish-run.mjs` re-encodes pictures as JPEG up to 2048 px (was 1600) and clips as H.264 up to 1280 px at CRF 23 (was 960 px at CRF 30), and publishes 3D model nodes (the GLB's geometry and textures byte for byte, the generating service's marks taken out of its JSON chunk: `asset.generator` becomes AwwO and its materials, meshes and nodes are renamed by kind and index, and a mark it cannot take out stops the publish; its preview as WebP). Aurora GT, Neon City and Tales of Mountains and Seas were republished from their runs with byte-identical records. 3D models: the r186 page rule says what AwwO's 3D model nodes hand over (one PBR mesh facing +X with +Y up, centred, its longest side 1 unit); the EV plant twin's cars are now its 3D model node's saloon and Neon Circuit's six cars its 3D model node's racing car, painted per car, with both cases' interfaces set in the brand fonts, republished from production runs of 2026-10-15 (the EV plant's third run of its text; Neon Circuit's fourth text after ten runs of three earlier ones, which found the defects D16-D19 in the audit). A copy of such a case leaves the module that loads the model and the page that pastes it to its first run, as it already did for a page fed pictures directly: their recorded code names the case run's own files (`productionCopy.ts`), and the copy dialog says that a media case's media nodes, and the steps that use their files, make theirs again on the first run. The case dialog's media line says "1 media node". All 17 homepage covers are now 1280×720 (were 960×540): the 15 others re-recorded from their published pages, 12 with the scripted input their covers were made with and Crystal Keep, the Mars mission and Beat Studio with new input scripts. Verified: `tests/canvas-preview-fonts.test.ts` (pins, licenses, detection, both preview builders), the media checks in `tests/saas-production-runs.test.ts` (every published file on disk by size and sha256; a missing, short or stalled file, or a stalled manifest, failing the whole load), the two 3D cases' dialogs in `tests/saas-production-media.test.tsx` (the GLB in place of its path, the brand fonts supplied), and in real Chrome both rebuilt cases as the dialog and as a canvas's Results view run them (the GLB loaded by its canvas path, the fonts applied, no script errors), and the built site's dialogs of all five media cases fetching their files from `/showcase/media/`.
- Offer RunningHub's 18 image and video models again (owner request 2026-10-15: 把rh的key再放回去重启; RunningHub has been off since 2026-10-10, when its key left `media.env`), under generic names like every other media model (owner decisions 2026-10-11, 「模型名也全部改成通用名」): each is named for what it is good for by its own settings, never its maker, family or version (`runningHubLabels` in `runninghub.go`, for example 「图片 · 艺术风格」, 「视频 · 动漫风格」, 「视频 · 超清带声」), under the generic vendor, and the API refuses to start on a RunningHub model without one. X-tasy's models still come first, so a new image or video node still starts on Image · HD and Video · All-round. A RunningHub refusal of a submission for the operator's reason (its key or its balance) now gives a free generation's attempt back as other providers' do: RunningHub answers such a refusal with 200 and an error code, so only its flat answer that names no task (an explicitly empty `taskId` and `status`, an error code, no wrapped data, no results, each key once and in plain ASCII, read the same way by the task parser) counts as one (`rhAnswerNamesNoTask`); an answer that carries or may carry a task (a status such as QUEUED or RUNNING, a repeated or case-variant key), a wrapped one, a refusal of the request itself and any answer to a poll keep counting. Checked against RunningHub on 2026-10-15 with the new key: all 18 endpoints answer an empty request with `1007` and create no task (a made-up endpoint answers `1001`, a made-up key `806`), and one real Seedream generation at 1K finished in 50 s with one picture.
- Open up the free plan for two weeks and add a daily check-in (owner request 2026-10-15: 全面放开…每个给个相对来说比较合适的量给他们，然后鼓励签到，每天签到就加送额度，维持2周; the owner chose 100 calls and 5 image / video / 3D generations a day, 50 calls and 3 generations more for a check-in, until 2026-10-29 00:00 UTC). `AWWO_PROMO_UNTIL` with `AWWO_PROMO_DAILY`, `AWWO_PROMO_ROUTE_LIMITS`, `AWWO_PROMO_ROUTE_TOTAL_PER_DAY`, `AWWO_PROMO_MEDIA_TOTAL_RUNS_PER_DAY`, `AWWO_PROMO_TRIPO_FREE_TOTAL_PER_DAY` and `AWWO_CHECKIN_BONUS` (`promo.go`) raise, until that time, every free workspace's daily total and route allowances to floors and the deployment-wide ceilings to higher values, read wherever admission and the meter read a workspace's limits (`todayAllowance`); nothing is written to a workspace, so everything reads its stored value again when the time passes, with no restart. A page that loads three.js 0.186.1 through an import map naming `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.186.1/…` (or unpkg, or the same files as `.min.js`) and imports from `'three'` and `'three/addons/…'` now gets AwwO's pinned copy of every file it imports, and of every file those import, as data: URLs in its import map (`apps/web/src/canvas/previewModules.ts`): the core, controls, GLTFLoader, post-processing (EffectComposer, RenderPass, UnrealBloomPass, OutputPass, SMAA, GTAO, SSAO and the rest), RoomEnvironment, Sky, Water, fat lines and the CSS renderers, 89 files of the npm release in all, each pinned by size and sha256 (`previewModules.generated.ts`, written by `scripts/preview-modules.mjs`; `--check` says whether it is current). A copy is the npm file byte for byte except that its relative imports name the canonical URL of the file they mean, which the import map supplies too, since a data: module cannot resolve a relative path; the page's own import-map entries, scopes and scripts are kept, and a module script whose src is a pinned file imports it instead. The interactive preview's policy now allows data: scripts, which are those modules; a page that can already run inline script gains nothing from them and they make no request. Pages on r128 run as before. Verified: 10 new tests (`tests/canvas-preview-modules.test.ts`: sizes, hashes and imports against `node_modules/three`, specifier resolution, the import map in both previews), the existing preview, studio and live-page suites, and in real Chromium under the production sandbox and policy, a page with RoomEnvironment, EffectComposer, UnrealBloomPass and OutputPass rendered through the interactive preview and the live page (`THREE.REVISION` 186, the bloom drawn).

- Choose any model for the canvas assistant, Claude Opus 5.5 included, and the canvas it builds runs on it (owner request 2026-10-12: 画布助手之类我无法选择opus5.5模型，把这东西给我开了，要能用这个跑). The picker under the assistant's composer is now the assistant's model (画布助手的模型): a model the reader picks there is kept for the account in that workspace (`awwo.assistant.model.v1`, every canvas, across reloads, while the service still offers it), the Agent components a plan adds start on it (`withAssistantModel`, `assistantModel.ts`: only nodes the plan created and left unset; media nodes, team nodes, bound nodes and Jev's choices keep theirs; the workspace entry on the same runtime first, otherwise another runtime that offers the model), and direct tasks run on it as before. Until the reader picks one, nothing changes: the service's first model is shown and new components keep the workspace default. Direct tasks can now use Bedrock models: the Pi worker serves a managed-execution call on one through its Converse bridge, sending it as one streaming request and gathering the stream (text, tool calls joined by index, finish reason, usage) into the one completion the call waits for (`bedrockComputerRequest`, `gatherChatStream`); an error frame, a stream without a finish reason or a `length` stop fails the call rather than returning part of an answer. The worker claims it on /health (`computerBedrock: true`) and the API offers a worker's Bedrock models for direct tasks, and admits a task on one, only where it is claimed (`computerModelChoices`, `createRun`); the openai-agents workers make no claim and refuse as before. Which Bedrock models a direct task can use is the Pi worker's catalog: the release adds `bedrock.claude-opus-5-5` to it (host drop-in `98-assistant-opus.conf`). Planning the canvas itself stays on the platform's free planner model. Verified: 3 new worker tests through the real bridge over a fake Converse SDK (a tool call split across chunks, its result replayed as a Converse tool result, reasoning never returned; truncated, throttled and `max_tokens` streams fail), the Go choice test and a Postgres test that a claimed Bedrock model is offered and its direct task admitted, and 5 vitest cases (`tests/saas-assistant-model.test.tsx`).
