The first production figure, once its error was repaired, opened without an error and stood still: its loop never called `draw()`, and `draw()` wrote `setAttribute("innerHTML", …)`. AwwO's in-page reporter now watches a figure the kit has mounted while it is on screen (`pageErrors.ts`): if nothing in its drawing changes by itself for 4 seconds, it hovers at two points and presses → ← Space Enter End Home, half a second each, and any change ends the watch for good. A figure that never changed is reported with what AwwO saw (an attribute named like a property; whether its animation loop ran, from a count of `requestAnimationFrame` calls), and its node gets one repair request saying so (`pageRepair.ts`, header `· still`), shown in its chat as 「原理图解不会动，AwwO 自动修复一次：…」. That once is its own, beside the once of a page that fails, so a figure whose error was repaired and that still does not move is asked once more, and never again for the same delivery. Not judged: a figure that is hidden or off screen (the kit pauses it), one drawn on a canvas, any page that is not a kit figure. The figure guide's checklist now names both mistakes. Verified in real Chrome through AwwO's preview: that production page and the round-1 LRU and bloom pages are reported; every round-2 and round-3 page that runs, the three model repairs and the guide's example are not, with reduced motion too; nothing is reported while the frame is off screen.

Every example's canvas ran end to end on Claude Opus 5.5 with AwwO's own image, video and 3D generation, and the homepage now shows the page its last page node delivered, byte for byte (`examples/generated/official/<id>.ts`, its SHA-256 in `generatedRecords.ts`), with the pictures, clip and 3D render it names put in place as data: URLs (`<id>.media.ts`, `showcaseDocument.ts`). Each example loads lazily, in an opaque sandbox under the canvas preview policy, plus `media-src data:` for the clip, `allow-forms` for a page's own submit handlers (`form-action 'none'` still stops any submission) and `clipboard-write`. Written by `.local/official-cases/publish.ts` and `records.ts`; checked in headless Edge at the homepage frame size by `qa.py`: no script errors on load or after pressing each page's first buttons, every generated picture shows, FRAME's clip plays.
- Generate a video from reference pictures (owner request 2026-10-12: 视频节点也加参考图). The three video models take the first picture a video node's message names (an upload of this canvas, or the picture wired into the video node's new reference input) as the video's first frame, and a second one as its last frame: X-tasy mode `interpolation` with roles `first_frame` and `last_frame` at the `adaptive` ratio, which the 2.5 model requires with frames, as X-tasy's `GET /openapi/v1/models` lists them for every one of these models (read 2026-10-12). A third picture and other files are left out; without pictures a video is generated from words as before, and AwwO charges the same credits either way. The composer says what the pictures are used for (`attach.mediaRefVideo`).
- Run a message whose pictures its model cannot see on a model that can (owner request 2026-10-12: 附图时自动换成能看图的模型). When a node's message, a canvas run's node or the canvas assistant's request carries a picture a worker could show and the chosen model does not take images, that one run moves to a seeing model of the same worker that the workspace may use: a free model first, then the planner's model, then catalog order, passing over (on a free workspace) a model whose paid route has no call left today or is closed to it, so the switch never turns the message into a `premium_quota_exceeded` refusal. Only the run moves: the node keeps its model, a message without pictures stays where it was, an effort the new model does not offer is dropped, and the run's snapshot records the model it left (`visionFrom`). With no such model the pictures are described in words, as before. The route-allowance check gained a lock-free read for this (`routeLimit`, `freeModelCeiling`); reservations keep their locks.
- Count presses of 「看下一步」, 「查看验收报告」 and the questions the canvas assistant answers on the page (owner request 2026-10-12: 给看下一步和验收报告按钮加点击统计). The hosted canvas posts the button's name alone to `POST /tenants/{id}/canvases/{canvasId}/ui-events` (`saas/uiEvents.ts`, best effort, never waited on), and the API (`ui_events.go`) writes one audit event per press, `ui.review.next_steps`, `ui.review.open_report` or `ui.assistant.local_answer`, on the canvas with no metadata: only those names, only a member's press on that workspace's canvas, membership checked again as the row is written, and a repeat by the same person on the same canvas within two seconds counted once. Platform admins see them in the audit list; no migration. Before this, the server saw only the rework itself, from the runs that carried a review's findings.
- Show a reworked Agent the review findings it was given, in both modes (owner request 2026-10-12: 普通用户模式也显示写进节点的验收意见). 「按验收意见返工」 writes the findings into the Agent's task requirements, which only the developer-mode settings showed; the Agent's own chat now opens on a one-line note, 「带着「交付验收」的验收意见」, that unfolds to the instruction and the findings exactly as each run of the Agent gets them (`ReworkFindingsNote`, read from either language's marker by `reworkFindings`), and says where to change them (in 普通用户模式: switch to developer mode). Read-only; nothing about the rework or the document changes.
- Generate images and videos on the operator's Jimeng member account (owner request 2026-10-12: 把即梦 CLI 整理结合到 AwwO 里面). Jimeng's official canvas CLI, `dreamina-canvas`, signed in once on the host by device authorization, is driven as a provider the way the JimengCli_api project turns the older Jimeng CLI into an API, but with an argument vector instead of a shell string (that project interpolates the prompt into `exec`), an environment of its own (the API's secrets never reach the CLI), bounded output, timeouts and at most four calls at once. One generation is one node on a Jimeng canvas per UTC day, saved and run in one call under its node, update and submit ids derived from the AwwO run, so a resend after a lost or busy answer is the same operation and is never paid twice (verified live 2026-10-12: the repeated call made no second resource); it is followed with `operation status` and its PNG or MP4 fetched with `resource download` into a private scratch file. Four models, shown by generic names only: 图片 · 电影质感 and 图片 · 极速 (both edit one reference picture), 视频 · 电影级 (up to 1080p) and 视频 · 极速, at most 15 seconds. `AWWO_JIMENG_CREDIT_CEILING` (default 700 Jimeng credits) is passed as the CLI's own `--credit-ceiling`, so a quote above it stops before anything is generated (`media_credit_ceiling`, nothing charged). The models are offered only by an explicit grant (`AWWO_JIMENG_WORKSPACES`, `AWWO_JIMENG_ALL_WORKSPACES` with the owned-workspace cap, or an allowlist naming them), never to an unrestricted workspace alone, because they spend a personal member account; where granted they lead the catalogue, so new and planned media nodes start on them. A paid plan pays three AwwO credits per Jimeng credit quoted on 2026-10-12. Every failure is a closed code read from the CLI's structured error; its message (which can echo the prompt) is never stored. JimengCli_api itself is not deployed.
- Canvas runs hand their pictures and clips to the page that uses them. An image, video or 3D node's `result` may now be wired into a text input (a page node's `context`, or a text/markdown/html field of a contract node), in the canvas editor and in a run's graph alike (`edgeTypesFit`, `canFeed`); until now only another image node's reference input could take it, so a generated asset could not reach the node that builds the page. The input reads the stored files as `<node id>/<file name>` paths (the API's `mediaDeliveryText`, mirrored in the web for a node's own Send and the client graph runner), the HTML output policy tells a page it may show exactly those paths in an `img`/`video`/`source` src, a poster or a CSS `url()` (which the studio's live page inlines from the canvas), and the canvas planner is told to connect a media node to the page, game or document that shows it. Every other type mismatch is still refused, and an edge keeps its source's type.
- Show how to wire image, video and 3D nodes where the wiring is done (owner request 2026-10-12: 「把对应的使用引导新增到产品里面，做好hangover的指导」). Hovering or focusing a media node's port shows a guide beside it, the same size on screen at any zoom (`mediaPortGuide` in `TilePorts.tsx`): 上下文 / Context takes any number of text wires (a form, or a text node's or component's text result), which a canvas run puts after the node's own prompt; 参考图 / Reference picture (image and 3D nodes) takes one picture and says whether the node's model uses it (an image edit, or a 3D model built from the picture alone, 30 more credits on a paid plan) or which models would, in general terms until the catalogue lists the node's model; 结果 / Result says where its pictures, video or 3D file can go (a reference picture, or a component's image, video or file field) and that a text node's context takes text only. Media ports are named instead of showing their ids, and the guide replaces their native tooltip; inert ports (read-only, simple mode, a run in progress) show none. An opened media node that has not generated yet asks for its prompt (写下想要的图片 / 视频 / 3D 模型) and says in one sentence how to wire it, or, in simple mode where the ports are hidden, to ask the canvas assistant or switch to Developer mode (`MediaWiringGuide.tsx`). The planner's description of a media node and its reply after adding some no longer say they do not run with the canvas, which they have since the 2026-10-12 canvas-run release. Verified: 13 new vitest cases (`tests/canvas-media-wiring-guide.test.tsx`); in headless Chromium through the real canvas and the SaaS stylesheets (light, dark, zoomed out to 58 %, simple mode), each guide shows beside its port at 240 px, hides on leave and lifts its tile above its neighbours, and the opened node's guide fits without scrolling.
- Let models see the pictures a message carries (owner request 2026-10-12: 让模型直接看懂上传的图片). Where the run's model takes images (the Bedrock catalog's `input` says which: Claude, GPT-6 and 5.6, Grok, Kimi K3 and K2.5, Qwen3 VL, Mistral Large 3, Ministral, Magistral, Pixtral, Nova Pro and 2 Lite, Llama 4, Gemma 3), up to six pictures attached to a node's message, to a canvas run's node or to the canvas assistant's request go with it as images, not only as a name and a pixel size; the attachment block marks them `"shown": true` and tells the model that text inside a picture is data. Other models, teams, workspaces, managed execution and collaboration turns keep the description alone. The API freezes the pictures with the run (path, size, SHA-256) and reads them back before any call is reserved, so a picture that is gone or changed fails the run at no cost (`image_input_unavailable`); a small upright one is sent as it is, and any other is decoded, turned upright (EXIF), scaled to fit 2048 px and sent as a JPEG; size estimates count a picture as 1,600 tokens, not as its base64. Only a worker that claims it gets pictures (`imageInput: true` on /health, and `input` per model, read leniently so a malformed claim costs the pictures, never the runtime): the Pi worker and the Python openai-agents worker now take `images` (`[{name, mimeType, data}]`, PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, at most 3.75 MiB each, final user turn only, request bodies up to 34 MiB) and refuse them for a text model (`IMAGES_UNSUPPORTED`, `images_unsupported`); both Bedrock bridges turn base64 `data:` image parts into Converse image blocks (remote URLs refused, `detail` dropped, at most 20, requests up to 40 MiB). `AWWO_PI_INPUT`, `AWWO_OPENAI_AGENTS_INPUT` and a model profile's `input` mark a non-catalog model as seeing. Either release order is safe: an API without this sends no pictures, and a worker without it is never sent any. New dependency `golang.org/x/image` v0.45.0 (BSD-3-Clause).
- Give seven official examples their own pictures, clip and 3D models, made in the same canvas run and shown by the pages (owner request 2026-10-12: 我们上线的其他视频和图像工具全部自己再生产一遍；把生成的图片接进网页): an image node for Orbit's key visual, Signal Run's key art, KEPLER's outpost, STAY's room and FRAME's storyboard, FRAME's 5-second sample clip and 3D models of FIELD/01 and the campus building (`officialMedia.ts`), each wired into its page and the page's repair node by a media input the page's instructions explain (the files by their `<node id>/<file name>` paths, a 3D model by its rendered preview). A copied example keeps those nodes on their media models. All 18 compiled examples are sized for one Claude Opus 5.5 call per node: a page at most 20,000 characters and a text node at most 2,000 characters plus 7,000 of code, with the thinking kept to a few sentences, after the first runs on 2026-10-12 had three heavy nodes cut off at the 32,000-token output limit; FOUNDRY's page, cut off again at 20,000, is held to 13,000 characters, and so is KEPLER's playable page, cut off at 20,000 with its concept art wired in, and HABITAT's twin console, cut off at 20,000 with its building's 3D preview wired in.
- Generate media from a reference picture (owner request 2026-10-12: 做媒体组件的参考图生成). The first picture attached to an image or 3D node's message, or wired into its new `reference` input from an upstream image node in a canvas run, is the generation's reference where the node's model takes one (`references` in the media catalogue): 3D nodes build the model from the picture alone through Tripo's image-to-model (POST /v3/files, then /v3/generation/image-to-model; words are not needed and not sent; 30 more credits on a paid plan, Tripo's +10 times three), and the image models 图片 · 高清, 图片 · 标准多张 and 图片 · 标准多张 Pro edit it through X-tasy's img2img (POST /openapi/v1/files, prepared, then `references: [{role: reference_image, file_id}]`). The picture is chosen and frozen with the run (path, size, SHA-256), checked again before it is uploaded, and only this canvas's uploads and generated pictures can be one; a failed upload ends the run before any task exists, so nothing is billed (`media_reference_unavailable`). The stored prompt keeps the reference's line, so the transcript shows the picture used. The composer says which picture a model uses or which models take one; video models and the other image models stay words-only until verified. The canvas assistant is told that image and 3D nodes take a reference, so it can chain a character or product image into a 3D node.
- Quote PDF text to the model (owner request 2026-10-12: 加上 PDF 正文提取). A PDF attached to a message is read page by page within the message's text budget, like an Office document: each font's ToUnicode map is decoded first (PDFs printed by Chrome carry Chinese only there), CJK radical look-alikes are folded to the ordinary characters, and the work is bounded (64 MB, 120 pages, 8 s, two at a time, every page recovered). A scanned or image-only PDF, a password-protected or damaged one, is said to have no readable text. New dependency `github.com/ledongthuc/pdf` (BSD-3-Clause), pinned.
- Send a delivered page that fails when it runs back to its component once, with the error (owner decision 2026-10-12: 「加上页面出错时自动修一次」). Every running preview (cards on the board, the deliverable drawer, the studio, the 成果 view) runs AwwO's error reporter ahead of the page (`PAGE_ERROR_SCRIPT`, in `PREVIEW_HOST_SCRIPT` with the viewport fix), which hands the first uncaught error or unhandled rejection to the host; a cross-origin "Script error.", the ResizeObserver notice, a request the preview blocks and a missing WebGL context do not count. The canvas finds the node that published that page in an HTML field of its current, complete run result and sends it one message through the component's own chat: the browser's message, the page's lines where it happened, the page as delivered, and a request for the whole fixed page alone, which goes back into its field with the delivery's other fields kept (`pageRepairDelivery`); the chat shows one line, 「页面运行出错，AwwO 自动修复一次：…」. Once per delivery: the request is recorded in the canvas's browser storage before it starts, so other views, tabs and reloads leave it alone, and a delivery from a run started within 30 minutes of the request is that repair's result and is not repaired again; while a run is active the request waits and starts once the canvas is idle. It is one model call on the node's own model, as a chat message is. Case recordings, hand-published values, failed runs, read-only canvases and pages over 200,000 characters are never repaired. Verified: 17 new vitest cases; in Chrome through the real preview, the two round-2 figure pages that never ran reported `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ')'` and `Identifier 'tokens' has already been declared` with their lines, and pages that run reported nothing; given AwwO's request once, Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 4.5 each returned a page that runs (Haiku changed the one bracket, Sonnet renamed the clashing function).
- Run image, video and 3D nodes as part of a canvas or component run (owner decision 2026-10-12: 「让画布运行也能跑图片和3D节点」). A media node is admitted with its graph, its model and settings frozen then; when its turn comes it generates from its own prompt (its draft, or else its latest Send) followed by the text wired into its context input, cut to its model's length, on the same allowances, locks and billing as its own Send (`admitMediaGeneration`, now shared with `createMediaRun`), and its stored files become its delivery. A downstream prompt names those files as `<node id>/<file name>`, which the results studio's previews resolve to that node's file. A reference image wired into an image node orders the run but is not sent (no provider here takes one yet), and a collaboration still leaves media nodes out (`media_collaboration_unsupported`). The canvas assistant is told that canvas runs generate them.
- Make the canvas assistant's message box and every component's inputs composite boxes that take files of any type (owner decision 2026-10-11: 「画布助手和组件 输入都得是复合工作框，要能够上传所有的媒体文件类型」). A "+" button, a drop or a paste attaches images, video, audio, 3D models, documents, code and archives (64 MB each, ten to a message) to the assistant, to a component's message box and to its text, Markdown and file inputs (the file input no longer says "the file is not uploaded"). Each file shows as a chip, a thumbnail for pictures, and travels as a `[附件] name · awwo-file:<id>` line at the end of the text, so drafts, recovered requests, plans and inputs keep it without a second channel. `POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/canvases/{id}/uploads` streams the bytes into `AWWO_MEDIA_DIR/<tenant>/uploads/<sha256>.bin` (identical files share one, swept with the media files) and records an `upload` artifact of the canvas; the type is sniffed from the bytes, only sniffed images, video and audio are served inline, and everything else downloads as an attachment. `DELETE …/uploads/{uploadId}` takes back a file never sent. Bounds: `AWWO_UPLOAD_MAX_MB` (64, below Cloudflare's 100 MB body limit), `AWWO_UPLOADS_PER_DAY` (200 a workspace) and `AWWO_UPLOAD_WORKSPACE_MB` (2048); the route is exempt from the 30 s request deadline and the server's 30 s read timeout and bounds itself at 20 minutes, and production nginx keeps its 2 MB body limit everywhere else while one location for exactly this route takes 70 MB, buffered, with the `/api` location's headers and flood limits (docs/awwo-saas-deploy.md; the compose `deploy/saas/nginx.conf` matches). Admission resolves the references that belong to the run's own canvas (component conversations, plans, graph runs and managed tasks alike) and appends one quoted untrusted-data block after the user's words: the text of text and code files and of Word, PowerPoint, Excel and ODT documents (24 KB a file, 48 KB a message, a partial copy marked), name, type, size and picture size for everything else, and the files themselves for workspace runtimes. The block is kept in the conversation, so a follow-up still has the text; transcripts show the files as chips and never the quoted data. The planner is told to hand a file to the component that needs it by writing its line into one of that component's inputs. Media components still generate from words only, and say so when files are attached; uploads stay out of the deliverables listing. Verified: Go build, vet and unit tests; a PostgreSQL integration test (upload, sniffing, inline and attachment serving, canvas scope, daily and size bounds, delete, the worker prompt and its replay); the request-characterization goldens; both web typechecks; eleven new vitest cases and the affected canvas suites.
- Add 原理图解 / Explainer figure (owner request 2026-10-11 for wheresryan22/anatomy: 「把这个研究明白，本地测试好，装到awwo里去」), a component that explains an idea, mechanism or algorithm by drawing a real, well-made machine whose motion is the idea: one interactive isometric page that runs as soon as it is shown, with hover and arrow-key control, an idle tour and a live readout from one model. Its single model call follows a compact guide (`apps/web/src/canvas/figureKit/figure-guide.md`) and draws with AwwO's figure kit, Anatomy's MIT drawing modules (`third_party/anatomy`, dbf697a) bundled into one classic script (`window.Anatomy`) whose output is byte-identical to the upstream kit. A page names the kit by one versioned URL (`https://awwo.clawhunt.store/kits/anatomy/1/anatomy.js`): AwwO's running previews inline the pinned file (size and SHA-256 checked) for that tag, the way they supply three.js r128, and the hosted site serves the same bytes there (a missing file is a 404, never the app) so a downloaded page still draws. The canvas assistant plans a figure node for an explainer-figure request (the router sends such requests to planning and the API's plan gate accepts `figure`); the Jev planner does not offer it, and the HTML output policy also allows a script whose exact URL the node instructions say AwwO supplies. Three one-shot rounds with Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5.6 Luna and DeepSeek 3.2 were rendered in the real preview sanitizer; the guide was revised after the first two (state-dependent parts in their own groups, nothing floats, every change is motion, one declaration per name), and the third ran 4 of 4 with no console error.

- Let the canvas assistant add media nodes (owner decision 2026-10-11: 「让画布助手按需加图片视频和3D节点」; a read-only report that day found that since the media release nobody had added one, and the planner could not: its seven templates were all text or code Agents). Where the workspace can generate them, the planning protocol offers `add_node` with `templateId` `image`, `video` or `model3d` (only the kinds the workspace's media catalogue has; none on a local canvas), and the planner is told to add one per asset the request needs, its prompt in `inputValues.prompt`, instead of having a text Agent describe the asset. A new media node starts on the kind's first offered model, as the add menu does, with the prompt in its composer (cut to what the model takes, e.g. 1,024 characters for 3D, and said); a `set_input` with `fieldId: "prompt"` rewrites an existing media node's prompt; any other input, a persona or a field edit on a media node is left out and said, and a kind the workspace cannot generate is not added, with the steps that name it, instead of failing the plan. Existing media nodes reach the planner by kind and prompt, never by model. Nothing is generated by planning: the reply says how many media nodes were added and that each generates when sent. The API's plan gate and planning progress accept the three media templates (progress reads `model3d`, a template id with a digit).
- Run canvas components side by side. A node's chat or 运行节点 now starts in its own run lane (up to four on a page, each with its own journal, ownership lock and stop), so one running component never holds the rest of the canvas: other nodes stay editable and runnable, layout (move, resize, enlarge) stays free, and only the running nodes' configuration, wires and existence are held. A whole-canvas run, a review loop or a collaboration still runs alone. A running card carries its own stop (「停下这个组件」) and the run chip says how many components run side by side; two nodes bound to one agent still take turns across lanes. The API admits a graph run unless its scope overlaps an active graph on the canvas (409 `graph_busy`; a collaboration still runs alone) and refuses a node whose session already has a run (409 `resource_in_use`); scoped node preparation waits only for work on its own nodes. Migration 028 replaces the one-active-graph-per-canvas unique index with a plain index; it is backward-compatible with the previous API. Reopening a canvas recovers every active graph into its own lane. The workspace's concurrent-run cap still applies: a graph beyond it waits for a slot.
- Resize every component card freely, including while it runs or as a reader: a corner grip, a double-click and an enlarge button draw the card larger, and from 340×230 it shows its deliverable live (pages run, documents, pictures, video, 3D and the text a running node is streaming). Card sizes are a per-browser view preference beside the canvas cache (`awwo.canvas.card-frames.v1`), never part of the document, so they need no edit permission and add no undo step.
- Add the results studio (成果工作台), an IDE-like deliverable window: a file tree grouped by node (the canvas's result first, archives expanding in place), search over file names and contents, viewers for pages (desktop, tablet and phone widths), Markdown, highlighted code, tables, images (zoom and pan), video, audio, 3D, PDF and archives, plus copy, download, download-all as a ZIP, maximize and open-in-new-tab. A delivered page runs as written in a sandboxed opaque origin (no `allow-same-origin`, no popups or top navigation) under an injected Content-Security-Policy (inline code and well-known public CDNs only, no form submission or `<base>`), its links handed to the host and a page that sends its own frame elsewhere put back (stopped after three tries within 15 seconds); its relative assets are inlined from the archive or the canvas's other files, and a library AwwO supplies (three.js r128, with the CapsuleGeometry that release lacks) runs from AwwO's pinned copy, so a delivered game needs no network. ZIPs are inflated in the browser with limits on members, per-file and total size and unsafe paths. It opens from a card's menu, an opened node and its delivery drawer, and the 成果 view embeds it.
- Add 普通用户模式 and 开发者模式. Simple mode (the default for a person who never chose) is chat-first: the canvas assistant, each node's own chat with an inline model picker (chat models from the palette, media models by kind), and what the canvas made; the model rail, Bot roster, command search, minimap, selection review, view styles, wiring and ports, the inspector, add-node gestures, run records, JSON export and the knowledge map stay out of sight. Developer mode shows every control as before. The choice is a presentation preference (`awwo.ui-mode.v1`, synced across tabs, switched from the canvas header or the More menu); it never changes a document, a run or what the server accepts.
- Smooth page switches: the HTML shell paints the themed AwwO boot surface at once (a canvas-shaped variant for canvas pages) and opts into cross-document view transitions; an in-app navigation answers immediately with a progress line; loading screens keep that same surface with the real header and back link until the page has its content.

- Run image and video nodes on X-tasy's open API (`service.xtasyart.com/openapi/v1`), the operator's own platform: 7 text-to-image models (Seedream 5.0 Pro, Nano Banana 2, GPT Image 2.5, GPT Image 2, Xtasy 3.0, Xtasy 3.0 Pro, 全能图片 5.0 Pro) and 3 text-to-video models (Xtasy V3, 全能视频 v2.5, 全能视频), each pinned to its X-tasy model id with its closed choices and listed before RunningHub's, so a new image or video node starts on X-tasy wherever it is configured (`AWWO_XTASY_API_KEY`; `AWWO_XTASY_ALL_WORKSPACES` offers them to every workspace within the media daily limits and needs `AWWO_MAX_OWNED_WORKSPACES`). Every send of a run carries one Idempotency-Key, so an answer that never arrived, a busy answer or a server error is sent again and answered with the same task, never a second charge; outputs are downloaded from the API origin alone, with the key, only from the task's own output addresses and without following redirects; a video's extra last-frame picture is not stored; an automatic duration is not offered, so a run's price is known when it is admitted. Paid plans pay three times X-tasy's charge at each model's defaults as measured on 2026-10-10 (images never below 30 credits), and a task X-tasy fails costs no credits. Every model was generated once with the operator's key (`TestXtasyLiveEveryModel`, opt-in).
- Generate 3D models on Tripo's own API (`openapi.tripo3d.ai/v3`): a 3D model node (「3D 模型生成」 in the add menu, 「3D 模型 Agent」 in node settings) runs one text-to-model task on Tripo v3.1 (high precision) or P1 (game low-poly), with Tripo's closed choices (texture, PBR, texture and geometry quality, face limit, negative prompt, real-world size). The task is submitted once and recorded so an API restart resumes it; Tripo's busy answers, which create no task (a full concurrency pool for the model's series, 429 with code 2000, or its rate limit, 1007), are waited out as its `Retry-After` asks, with the run shown as queued, until the run's deadline. The GLB and Tripo's rendered preview are downloaded at once (Tripo's links expire in five minutes), sniffed (binary glTF 2.0 first, then a picture) and stored in `AWWO_MEDIA_DIR` like other media; a preview that cannot be stored leaves the run with its model. The result shows the preview, turns the model in the WebGL viewer on request and offers the GLB. Off until `AWWO_TRIPO_API_KEY` is set beside `AWWO_MEDIA_DIR`; the key goes only to Tripo's origin and Tripo's messages are never shown (failures map to closed codes, 2010 to "top up the balance", a failed task's own code such as 2008 to its reason). Free generations have their own caps, `AWWO_TRIPO_FREE_RUNS_PER_DAY` per workspace (2) and `AWWO_TRIPO_FREE_TOTAL_PER_DAY` across workspaces (40); paid plans spend credits at three times each model's own Tripo price (v3.1 60 with texture, 30 without; P1 120 and 90; detailed texture and geometry add theirs), and nothing for a task Tripo failed or cancelled, which Tripo does not charge; `AWWO_TRIPO_ALL_WORKSPACES=true` offers the models whatever a workspace's model allowlist names, and like `AWWO_MEDIA_UNRESTRICTED_WORKSPACES` needs `AWWO_MAX_OWNED_WORKSPACES`. RunningHub keeps working alone or beside it.
- Show everything a canvas made in its 成果 view: 「这张画布做出的全部成果」 lists every step's pages, stored files, pictures, videos, 3D models and documents first, each opening in the viewer below, stored files downloadable from the list; a file field that came back as a name only is listed as such.
- Edit a node's inputs and deliverables from its template guide (模板参考): 编辑 on each side opens the input field structure or the deliverable form editor, and the guide says the canvas assistant can change them too.

- Let the workspace home's 「最近的成果 / Recent results」 be cleaned up. Each card's menu takes its result off the list (「从最近的成果中移除」: kept per person and workspace in this browser, the canvas and its deliveries untouched, undoable, and shown again once the canvas delivers something new; 「已移除 N 项 · 全部恢复」 brings them all back) or, for a member of an active workspace, deletes the canvas with its conversations and run history after a confirmation. 「管理」 selects several cards to remove or delete at once; deletions run one by one, and a canvas the server refuses (an active run) stays in the dialog with its reason. A deletion here also reloads 「继续工作」.
- Add three opt-in abuse limits, each off by default (unset, 0 or false keeps today's behaviour). `AWWO_FREE_MODEL_TOTAL_PER_DAY` caps the free default models' calls per UTC day across route-limited workspaces (the empty `{}` excepted), checked like the route ceilings under their advisory lock; past it a run fails with `free_capacity_exceeded`, while paid-plan calls and the operator's planner calls neither count nor are held. `AWWO_NEW_ACCOUNTS_PER_IP_PER_DAY` limits the accounts first ClawHunt sign-ins create per client address per UTC day (the sign-in limiter's address, `AWWO_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`; IPv6 by /64), kept in `signup_ip_days` under a keyed hash of the day and the address, never the address, and pruned after three days (migration 027). `AWWO_REQUIRE_VERIFIED_EMAIL=true` creates no account for an identity ClawHunt reports unverified. A refused first sign-in returns with `reason=signup_limited` or `email_unverified`; existing accounts always sign in. The web explains the new code and both reasons in Chinese and English.
- Add the Pro ($20) and Max ($100) monthly plans, sold and renewed by ClawHunt through Stripe and read over the SSO backchannel (`GET /billing`, `POST /billing/checkout` and `/billing/portal`, and a background re-read around renewals, hourly and for a day after a checkout). A plan's credits are what was paid for its period (1 credit = 1 cent: 2,000 or 10,000 a month); Claude, GPT, Bedrock, images and video spend their official price × 1.5 from `AWWO_MODEL_PRICING_JSON`, while the default model stays free within 300 or 1,000 calls a day. A route-limited workspace's plan is its owner's, and its allowances (agents at once, default-model calls and generations a day, owned workspaces) are the account's across the owner's plan workspaces. Every paid call and generation records who pays and for which period, so spend survives canvas deletion; an unreported call is charged an estimate from its size and the time it ran, overspend comes off the next period, and refunds and disputes take credits back. 「套餐与点数 / Plans and credits」 and the usage meter show the plan. Checkout stays closed until `AWWO_BILLING_CHECKOUT_ENABLED=true`. Migration 026.
- Let a one-shot model call through a worker's `/internal/computer-model` turn a chat-template model's hidden thinking off (`thinking: false`, sent on the Chat Completions wire only, never to OpenAI or Google) and lower its output limit (`maxTokens`, never above the profile's). The Pi and JS workers list these `completionOptions`, with their `maxConcurrency`, in `/health`, so the API sends them only where they hold.
- Show what a canvas delivered. A 「编排 | 成果 / Build | Results」 switch in the canvas bar opens the canvas's result in the deliverable viewer, larger and with nothing that edits around it, beside its numbered steps (each step's own delivery opens in place) and a run receipt read from the run records. The result is the furthest page, media or file delivered, otherwise the furthest step; acceptance steps are shown as an agent's check, never as a person's sign-off. Partial results, hand publications and a copied case's recording are labelled as such, a result with later steps still undelivered is called the furthest step so far, and the receipt names only the latest canvas run that completed the step. The board stays as it was underneath, out of reach with its shortcuts paused, and `?view=results` keeps the view across a reload. The workspace home adds 「最近的成果 / Recent results」: the workspace's newest delivering canvases shown by their result (a web page as it renders without scripts, in the same opaque sandbox as every preview), each opening on its results.
- Show a ClawHunt-linked account its own AwwO invite codes: a new "邀请好友 / Invite friends" page (`?account=invites`, linked from the More menu, the account panel and Account security) lists the three codes with their status and copies a share link or the code. The share link is `https://clawhunt.store/awwo#invite=<code>`: the code rides in the fragment, which no server log or analytics records, and opens the main site's invite popup with the code filled in. The API reads the codes from the issuer (`POST /api/v1/auth/clawhunt/invites` → ClawHunt `POST /api/awwo/sso/invites` with the session's grant), accepts only printed codes with a known status, and shows them only when the answer names the session's own subject. Each account reads them at most once at a time and ten times a minute (429), on a bound of its own rather than the sign-in limiter. An unreachable or older issuer, or an API older than the page, reads as "unavailable"; an inactive answer ends the session; an account without a ClawHunt link is told the codes come with one.
- Offer "没有账号？注册 ClawHunt 账号 / New here? Create a ClawHunt account" on the sign-in page. It opens ClawHunt's sign-up view (`start?signup=1` asks the issuer with `prompt=create`; older issuers ignore it), and the page now says the invite code is asked for in a popup right after signing up or in.

- Run image and video nodes on RunningHub's Standard Model API: a curated, strictly parsed catalog of 18 text-to-image and text-to-video models (Seedream, Nano Banana, GPT Image, Qwen-Image, Midjourney, Grok Imagine, Wan, Jimeng, Kling, Seedance, Veo, Sora, Hailuo, Vidu, PixVerse) with each model's closed parameters, chosen in the node inspector and shown with server defaults that are never written into the node. A run is submitted once, its provider task is recorded so an API restart resumes polling instead of paying again, and each result is downloaded through a public-address-only client on allowlisted hosts, sniffed against a closed image/video set, stored under `AWWO_MEDIA_DIR` and shown inline in the transcript (images, and seekable videos via a sandboxed range route). Provider messages are never stored; failures map to closed codes. Media models need an explicit grant (the workspace allowlist names them, or `AWWO_MEDIA_UNRESTRICTED_WORKSPACES=true`); each generation is recorded in a workspace ledger that canvas deletion does not erase, counts toward a per-workspace media limit, a deployment-wide daily ceiling and the workspace's daily run quota, and is refused below a free-disk floor (with space reserved for downloads in progress). Opening media to every unrestricted or new workspace requires `AWWO_MAX_OWNED_WORKSPACES`. Canvas runs and knowledge context do not include media nodes, and only image and video nodes render media records. Off until `AWWO_RUNNINGHUB_API_KEY` (an Enterprise-Shared key) and `AWWO_MEDIA_DIR` are both set. See docs/awwo-runninghub.md.
- Let users choose the look of an opened canvas node from its header: the AwwO default, Codex, WorkBuddy, Claude Code (terminal transcript) or a custom combination of layout, font, size, spacing, corners, reading width, accent and message colour. Styles are CSS skins only (no content is added or hidden), have tuned light and dark palettes that meet WCAG AA, adapt custom colours to each theme, and are saved per signed-in account in the browser with export and strict import.
- Serve about fifty popular models through Amazon Bedrock on all three model workers: a shared Converse bridge presents Bedrock as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Claude has no Chat Completions API there), a curated, strictly validated catalog (`apps/bedrock-models.json`) is enabled with `AWWO_BEDROCK_CATALOG=builtin`, and the model shelf groups models by vendor (DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, GLM, MiniMax, Mistral, Llama, Nova, Gemma, Nemotron besides the existing brands). Workers sign with their AWS credential chain unless a Bedrock API key is set. Under `AWWO_LLMGATE_ONLY` a worker that serves a Bedrock model reports `platformOnly` instead of claiming Gate-only, and the API admits it only when `AWWO_PLATFORM_PROVIDERS` also allows `bedrock`; personal-credential workers refuse Bedrock models and personal connections stay Gate-only. The built-in catalog is verified for us-east-1, and managed execution does not offer Bedrock models (the bridge serves streaming chat only). See docs/awwo-bedrock.md. Off by default; nothing changes until an operator enables it.
- Add a per-model switch that turns a model's hidden thinking off in both openai-agents workers: `AWWO_OPENAI_AGENTS_DISABLE_THINKING=true` for the default model, or `disableThinking: true` on a catalog profile, adds `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false` to that model's Chat Completions requests. It is for Qwen-style models such as qwen3.8-27b-p6, whose hidden reasoning otherwise spends 2,000–8,000 of a node's 4,096 output tokens. Off by default, never inherited, never sent on Responses, and not part of `/health`; it covers the operator model catalog, while personal connections are unchanged.
- Give every homepage production case a real AwwO canvas and its recorded run. A case now opens to “How it was made”: the canvas stage by stage, each agent's task and actual delivery, the delivered result in an opaque sandbox, and a run receipt with model, execution settings, timings and the result's SHA-256. Members can copy a case's canvas as a clean draft. The eight new canvases are sized for the default execution settings (one model call per node, at most 4,096 output tokens) with the model's hidden thinking switched off, and ran that way on a local copy of the production API and worker revisions, with no production writes. Records are generated from raw runs by `scripts/showcase/` and never edited; machine paths and identifiers are redacted, and each note counts every run of its canvas, failed ones included.
- Add a seven-step work-mode tutorial: brief → canvas → agents → handoffs → parallel stages → run states → review and delivery, illustrated with a real case canvas. Accounts registered from 2026-10-03 must complete it during their first 14 days (no close or skip; it returns until finished). Other accounts see it once, skippable. Replay it from More options → How AwwO works.
- Add tenant knowledge sources, immutable revisions, provenance, reviewable proposals and restoration, with selected knowledge revisions frozen into planning and execution context.
- Add a managed OpenMaus execution assistant that reuses AwwO model connections, runs the pinned open-source core in restricted Docker workspaces, and returns approvals, questions, cancellable runs and published artifacts to the canvas. End users do not configure a second OpenMaus account or provider key.
- Add canvas previews for HTML, WebGL 3D, paged PDF and a read-only IDE file tree/source window, with artifact provenance and knowledge archival.
- Add Linux amd64 release packaging for the API, SaaS web, model workers, pinned execution core and immutable workspace image, with checksums, runtime smoke checks and separate CI jobs. Production promotion still requires validated backup/restore evidence, runtime configuration checks and explicit migration authorization; building an artifact does not announce deployment.
- Redraw generated training charts when an embedded result becomes visible or changes width, preserving trained weights and experiment state across canvas/result tab switches.
- Show official workflows and interactive results side by side, with dependency-stage tours, node handoffs, persistent result state, reset/focus controls and embedded-width layouts. Curated model outputs include sanitized run snapshots, explicit incomplete steps, checksum provenance and isolated interactive previews.
- Let users copy an official workflow as an unconfigured draft or apply one available workspace model to all its session nodes, with a fresh availability check before creation. Add a permission-scoped graph evidence download containing run records, summaries and invocation pages with explicit completeness limits. Copying does not start model execution.
- Expand the official collection into twelve industry systems plus six starter studies: connected simulation and operations models for games, buildings, media, hospitality, research, machine learning, education, delivery review, logistics, retail, manufacturing and energy. Add industry/capability discovery and explorable 12–13-node review/repair workflows with clean reusable canvas contracts.
- Refresh a personal model connection using its encrypted saved credential, preserving the connection ID and existing canvas selections; failed discovery leaves the saved catalog intact.
- Six official, interactive examples on the AwwO home and public gallery: a pricing configurator, playable path game, projected 3D product, editable knowledge retrieval, real in-browser logistic-regression training, and budget approvals. Each includes a bilingual dependency canvas, node instructions and acceptance criteria, downloadable canvas JSON, and a permission-aware copy action that creates an unexecuted draft. Curated selections survive unified sign-in without changing OAuth redirect rules.
- Optional API settings for new workspaces: `AWWO_NEW_WORKSPACE_ALLOWED_MODELS` and `AWWO_NEW_WORKSPACE_MAX_RUNS_PER_DAY` set the model list and daily quota of every workspace created afterwards, and `AWWO_MAX_OWNED_WORKSPACES` makes `POST /tenants` answer `403 workspace_limit` to an account that is not a platform admin and already owns at least that many. Unset keeps the previous behaviour; existing workspaces are not changed.
- Optional operator-paid model for canvas plans: with `AWWO_PLANNER_MODEL` (for example `bedrock.claude-haiku-4-5`, served by the Pi worker), a plan the canvas assistant requests runs on that model instead of the planner's default, outside the workspace's model allowlist, route allowances and plan credits; it still counts towards the workspace's daily runs and is counted by no route allowance or ceiling. `AWWO_PLANNER_PER_WORKSPACE_PER_DAY` (30), `AWWO_PLANNER_TOTAL_PER_DAY` (2000) and `AWWO_PLANNER_MAX_INPUT_BYTES` (60000) bound it; past them, or when the worker lacks the model, the plan runs on the default model as before. A run posted to the planner session directly never uses it. The Pi worker can give only the named Claude models extended thinking (`AWWO_PI_BEDROCK_THINKING_BUDGET`, 1024–16000, with `AWWO_PI_BEDROCK_THINKING_MODELS`), applied by the Bedrock bridge to tool-free requests. Unset keeps the previous behaviour.

### Removed

- Leave out of every build the code the three.js it ships took from three Stack Exchange answers (two on Stack Overflow) and from work on OpenProcessing, which are under CC BY-SA (owner 2026-10-19: 「CC BY-SA 那几处代码也直接去掉」): `generateUUID()` and its table of hex digits, `CubicPoly` (the cubic each coordinate of a `CatmullRomCurve3` segment follows) and that curve's knot spacing in `getPoint()`, in `three/build/three.core.js` and in r128's `three.min.js`; r128's `DataUtils.toHalfFloat()`; and `hilbert2D()` and `hilbert3D()` in `three/examples/jsm/utils/GeometryUtils.js`. The Shadertoy cut's plugin, renamed `apps/web/scripts/three-cuts.mjs` (its tests `tests/saas-three-cuts.test.ts` and `tests/native-three-cuts.test.ts`, the image's copy `deploy/saas/workspace/tools/three-cuts.mjs`), makes these cuts the same way: each piece found between markers and known by its sha256, the repository holding no line of it. Each function but the two curves is AwwO's own code that does the same: a random UUID of three.js's form (lower case, upper in r128) from as many calls to `Math.random()` (four, so a page that seeds it draws the same numbers after them), written digit by digit into one flat string (no slower than npm's); the same Catmull-Rom curves (each segment the cubic Hermite curve with the spline's slopes, the knots spaced as before; within 1e-12 of npm's three.js on the tests' curves, exact at a curve's ends and where every control point has the same coordinate, and bit for bit what the cut file gives in both builds' minified output); and the same half for every number in the half's range (for NaN it now gives NaN where r128 gave infinity, and for a number beyond the range infinity where r128 set the float's mantissa bits on infinity's). The table goes, as only `generateUUID()` read it. `hilbert2D()` and `hilbert3D()` throw, saying they are not in AwwO's copy of three.js; `gosper()` and the rest of the file are as they were. Besides the shaders' names, the build now fails on the links and comments three.js gives with that code (which the cuts take out with it); on any file of either three.js package but three's core and module builds, its add-ons but the TSL ones, and r128's `three.min.js` (its sources and other builds repeat what is cut), which takes the place of the block on its WebGPU and TSL code; and on any file of either package the build takes in, as code, as text or as an asset, that credits Stack Exchange or OpenProcessing but for three links read as references only (as `EXRLoader.js`, `MeshSurfaceSampler.js` and `3DMLoader.js` do, which nothing ships today); `scripts/preview-modules.mjs` and the image's `keep-preview-files.mjs` refuse such a file too. Pins: `three.core.js` 1,457,209 bytes and `GeometryUtils.js` 2,345 bytes in `previewModules.generated.ts` and the image's list, r128 604,160 bytes in `previewLibraries.ts`; `third-party-licenses.txt` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` say this code is not shipped. An image built before this keeps the uncut files.
- Leave out of every build the two shaders the three.js it ships took from Shadertoy, where a shader is under CC BY-NC-SA unless its author says otherwise (owner 2026-10-18: 「Shadertoy 那两个着色器直接去掉」): the WebGL renderer's dithering (shadertoy.com/view/MslGR8, in three 0.186.1 and in r128) and N8's bicubic filtering of the transmission buffer (shadertoy.com/view/Dl2SDW, in 0.186.1). `apps/web/scripts/three-shadertoy.mjs`, in both build configs (for the app and for its workers), reads `three/build/three.module.js` and `three-r128/build/three.min.js` with each shader's body cut out and the function kept under its name and signature (the dev server and both test configs cut their `?raw` imports too, so previews there check the same pins; a code import of three goes there uncut, and neither ships): `dithering()` returns the color it gets (a material with dithering on draws as one with it off) and `textureBicubic()` samples the buffer's mip levels with `textureLod`, as three.js did before it took N8's filter (a rough transmissive material looks a little less smooth). It holds no line of either shader's body: it finds each body between markers (the function's own header and three.js's code around it) and knows it by its sha256. The build fails when either file is not the release the cut was written for, when a body is not the expected one, when one of the files would ship by another way than as code or `?raw` text, when the bundle takes in three.js's WebGPU or TSL code (which holds more code from Shadertoy), and when any file the build writes, checked after the other plugins have emitted theirs, still holds either shader, also inside a base64 `data:` URL. The preview's pins follow what ships: `previewModules.generated.ts` (`scripts/preview-modules.mjs` pins three.module.js after the cut: 660,625 bytes) and the r128 library in `previewLibraries.ts` (603,199 bytes). The sandbox's page check, which serves the preview's three.js files from the workspace image, gets the same cut file: `scripts/preview-modules.mjs` writes the image's list (`deploy/saas/workspace/tools/three-preview-files.json`) with the cut file's sha256 and copies the cut beside it (`tools/three-shadertoy.mjs`, under its `--check`), and the image's build step `keep-preview-files.mjs` cuts its copy before it checks the list (an image built before this keeps the uncut file); `third-party-licenses.txt` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` say the shaders are not shipped. `tests/saas-three-shadertoy.test.ts` and `tests/native-three-shadertoy.test.ts` build both configs and run the emitted `?raw` chunks.
- Remove the 18 official examples (「从一个作品开始」 / “Start with something you can try”) from the signed-out homepage and both workspace homes, with their `?examples=1` gallery and `?official=` links (owner request 2026-10-13 17:34: 这个下面这18个案例都太简单了，没有必要留着，删掉吧，专门把上面的一句话需求，交给一支 Agent 团队。板块的案例再多做点，质量再拔高一些). Their canvases, run records, generated pages and media, reference demos, tests and docs are gone, and an old `?examples=1` link opens the homepage. The production cases keep what they shared with them: `createOfficialDocument` and its types, the media node type, the copy dialog (`OfficialCopySetup`, now for cases only) and `showcasePage`. Every case canvas compiles exactly as before (the canonical canvas text of all 12 cases, in both languages, is unchanged), so the published run records still match their canvases.

THE LONG CHORD's Episode I is one canvas of 305 nodes: a generation's pictures can only be its own canvas's, and an edit's files only its own canvas's, so Acts II and III go on Act I's canvas, where they use its reference sheets as they are and one edit joins the three acts. A graph run, an initialize (its document and its scope) and a collaboration now read up to 400 nodes (`maxGraphNodes`); wires stay at most 2000; as before, a canvas saves with any number of nodes and only a run or an initialize refuses one past the bound. A graph run's admission now hands each node's checks that node alone (`savedNodeDocuments`): it read the whole canvas about six times per node under the workspace's row lock, so twice the nodes would have been four times the work. The canvas assistant's Jev planner adds roles up to 400 nodes and names that bound past it (`MAX_CANVAS_NODES`); a graph's evidence download reads a 400-node graph and, as for any graph, at most 200 of its runs, listing the rest as omitted; the Pi planner still sends every node's outline and every wire whole within a hosted canvas's 120 KB view, so it says a canvas is too large to plan well before 900 wires the more nodes it has (the three-act episode is past it). Tests pin 400 in and 401 out: graph_size_bound_test.go (the parser, a collaboration, initialize, and each node's checks answering from its node alone as from the whole canvas), saas-jev-planning.test.ts, saas-graph-evidence-export.test.ts.
- Offer the DeepSeek API's models to every workspace its model allowlist permits, and run them only where someone chose one (owner 2026-10-21: 「先改隐私条款，然后对所有用户开放 DeepSeek」). ClawHunt's Privacy Policy (clause 08, updated the same day) names DeepSeek, which processes requests in China, and promises that a request goes there only when a DeepSeek model is selected for it, by the user or by the canvas assistant at the user's request. Until now they were offered only to the workspaces a platform administrator owns or whose allowlist names them (`5acdbe38`); the catalogue stamping, the per-call gate and graph admission now hold them to the allowlist like any other model (`tenant_models.go`, `teams.go`). AwwO itself never picks one (`userChosenProvider`): an empty selection never resolves to one (`defaultModel`: not a worker default on DeepSeek, not as the substitute, no default at all rather than DeepSeek), a picture never moves a run onto one (`seeingModels`), a DeepSeek `AWWO_PLANNER_MODEL` never plans (`plannerModelSnapshot`, the plan runs on the default model), and the last gate refuses a DeepSeek call admitted as the operator's own (`reserveInvocation`, by the catalogue's judgement, a default it lists without a provider included); an empty model sent as it is (the worker's own default) is refused where that default is a DeepSeek model (`modelLimits`). The listings mark such a model `userChosen` (the runtime and managed-execution catalogues; a worker default only a user may choose that the worker leaves out of its list is listed too, marked), and the page leaves it out of every choice it makes by itself, whatever the request says (`canvas/userChosenModels.ts`): the model a direct task starts on when the reader picked none (`useManagedExecution.ts`; with no other model, none until the reader picks one) and the default a refused task is offered (`AssistantExecution.tsx`), the models Jev assigns to the roles it adds (`jevPlanning.ts`), the models a canvas plan may put a node on, which its `set_model` resolves against (`CanvasSurface.tsx`), and the sandbox model a node moves to (`InspectorPanel.tsx` `withSandbox`). Only the reader's own pick in a model picker selects one. The two listings show such a model only to a client that says it honours the mark (`X-Awwo-Model-Marks: userChosen`, which the page's API requests send, both listings' among them, `saas/api.ts`; `listedFor`), so a page of an earlier release still open in a tab, which would pick one by itself, is never shown one; the API goes live before the page, since an earlier API marks nothing (`docs/awwo-deepseek.md`). A plan asked to put a node on one leaves the node as it was and says the reader picks it in the node's settings (`applyCanvasPlan`, its list from `planModelsOf`), and Jev says so for a goal requiring one where the workspace has other models; the settings' default-model copy says the first model on the list leaves such models out. Tests: `user_chosen_models_test.go` (replacing `explicit_models_test.go`), `planning_context_test.go`, `saas-user-chosen-models.test.ts`, `saas-jev-planning.test.ts`, `saas-assistant-execution.test.tsx`. Production settings with it: `deepseek-flash` on `AWWO_NEW_WORKSPACE_ALLOWED_MODELS` and on the existing allowlists, priced in `AWWO_MODEL_PRICING_JSON` at the official peak price (`docs/awwo-deepseek.md`).
- Give back only the call a platform time limit cut, not every call of its direct task (security review 2026-10-18; owner decision the same day: 「Refund only the cut call」). Under the rule of 2026-10-17, one such cut gave back every call of the task it failed, and a task could run into one on purpose with a call made to run long (at most 32 calls a day). The cuts are a Gate call's 408, an edge's 504 or 524, a stream the edge closed when silent (`stream:closed:idle`), the worker's HTTP header or body limit, a Bedrock call's 408 or 504, and a Bedrock model's own time limit.
  - Such a call now reads `computer_model_timeout`, failure class `timeout` (`computerPlatformTimeout` in `computer_model_proxy.go`). So does a call this API's own HTTP client cut at its time limit (`computerCallBroke`). It read as the worker's transport, which gave back the whole task wherever that limit (`AWWO_RUN_TIMEOUT`) is shorter than the call's own (review 2026-10-19). It is noted in the new table `refunded_calls` as it settles (migration 039), and comes back alone once its task ended for the platform's sake (`refundedCutCall` in `direct_task_refund.go`). Every other platform fault still gives back the task's every call; the cap of 32 a day counts both.
  - The task's detail says which calls came back (`refundScope`: `task`, `cut`, or null when none did); the task's note and the usage panel say when only the cut call did.
- Let the canvas assistant decide how to handle every message, with nothing to pick by hand (owner 2026-10-18, on a live stream: from arranging the canvas to doing the task directly, the user should not have to choose, as with Claude or Codex). The 「改为直接执行 / 改为调整画布」 links under a reply and on an empty canvas are gone. A correction in the conversation (别改画布，直接帮我写; 还是放到画布上吧) now hands the request before it over the other way, with the correction after it: the server's router marks such a message `"redirect": true`, only where the last request went the other way and has its answer, and the canvas hands that request over as the links did (a plan is undone once its task exists, or kept and said so where it can no longer be undone; a running task is stopped first; a task whose start is unconfirmed is never planned over). The turn keeps the whole request, so a second correction hands the original over again. A message too long to plan becomes a task where one can start.
